  - A refusal that is kept for a version of the software the image does not run is a wrong refusal. The two refusals that were written for the CI runner (a crash of 24.2, a libheif 1.17) are typed answers produced by the code that is in the image whatever it runs on, so the image converts and the CI runner refuses, and one test shows both.
  - Choosing a library version by a single failing conformance vector is the wrong trade: FFmpeg 7.1 is the distribution's maintained line with security updates; a separate FFmpeg build would carry every codec library, a patch and CVE watch of its own, and a second build in CI to test it, for one clip of 17.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - xHE-AAC m4a files (the codec of some broadcast and streaming-app recordings) were refused until the image's FFmpeg was 8.0 or newer; the typed answer names the codec and says a newer build is needed. Entry 105 ended this on the image; the answer remains for any other FFmpeg build.
  - The test of the layout crash runs three `soffice` conversions of a 93-page document (17 s on the image) and needs `pdftotext`, as the other real-file Word tests do.
  - The measurements ran on arm64 only; the image builds for both architectures from the same Debian archive versions.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **A pinned FFmpeg 8 build in the image**: needs a `Dockerfile.worker` change that this change does not make; it is the choice to take when xHE-AAC files appear in real traffic (revisit below). QA took it on 2026-10-25 as FFmpeg 9.0.2 (entry 105).
  - **Removing the typed refusal of a document the suite stops on**: the refusal is the answer for every such document, not for this file.
  - **Routing `dps` as a PowerPoint 97 file from the type table alone**: see above.
- **Verified by**: on the throwaway Debian 13 VM, `tests/image-heif-decode.test.ts` (12 passed, 2 skipped by design), `tests/media-undecodable-streams.test.ts -t xHE-AAC` (4 passed, the refusal branch), `tests/office-suite-typed-failures.test.ts` (conversion branch); on the CI runner's distribution, the same layout test (refusal branch).
- **Revisit when**: Debian trixie ships FFmpeg 8 or newer (a point release or backports), xHE-AAC files appear among the rejected jobs of real traffic, the CI runner's LibreOffice moves to 25.x (the refusal branch of the layout test then runs nowhere and the typed answer needs another real file), or a `.dps` file with a licence that allows a fixture is published.

## 98. PDF text: simple fonts whose glyph names are code-page numbers read as Poppler reads them, and a page is released once pdf.js has delivered what its operator list depends on

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783 rows "Found by #880: simple fonts where Poppler gets characters" and "Found by #880: `gd-026598` to md hits the 60 s limit"; epic #760), decided 2026-10-24 (QA request in issue #783: follow Poppler's `Gfx8BitFont` encoding and name-to-Unicode order, and find what the Markdown route spends). It extends entry 49 (what the reader maps), changes how entry 81 waits, and leaves entry 85 as it is.
- **Decision**:
  - **A simple font without a /ToUnicode map whose /Differences names are all numbers reads each name as its number.** This is Poppler's rule (`poppler/GfxFont.cc` 26.09, `Gfx8BitFont::Gfx8BitFont` lines 1228 to 1295, `parseNumericName` lines 865 to 909, `testForNumericNames` lines 913 to 943; GPL, followed for its behaviour only, in `pdf-numeric-glyph-names.ts`): every name is a number after at most two letters (`G69`, `MT83`, `g110`), every run of /Differences starts at code 5 or below, a name the Adobe Glyph List knows keeps its text, and the number is decimal unless an unknown name is two hexadecimal digits with a letter digit last or a letter and two hexadecimal digits with a letter digit among them. The characters reach pdf.js as a /ToUnicode map of one-byte codes in the incremental update the reader already writes for composite fonts (entry 70's mechanism, `pdf-font-tounicode.ts`), so pdf.js lays the text out from real characters.
  - **Three bounds of ours.** Only a number that is a character of a one-byte code page is taken (U+0020 to U+007E, U+00A0 to U+00FF); any other glyph keeps the text pdf.js gives it and is left out as before when that is none. Hexadecimal is decided for the document, not per font. A font whose name contains "dingbats" reads its names through the Zapf Dingbats list first, as the rest of the reader does (`pdf-glyph-recovery.ts`). The fonts read are the ones the page resources name, at most `PDF_CONTENT_MAX_FONTS` (4,096) a document; the codes are 0 to 255.
  - **The text reader cleans a page up, and closes its document, only after pdf.js has delivered every object the page's operator list depends on.** That is what pdf.js's renderer waits for before it draws: each id of a `dependency` operator, in the page's table or, for an id that starts with `g_`, the document's (`src/display/canvas.js` of pdf.js 6.3.289, `executeOperatorList`, lines 708 to 724). It holds for every job that reads the operator list, the text and density jobs included; entry 81 waited only for the pictures of the Markdown, HTML and Word jobs. Each page's operator list is read at most once, by whichever part of the reader asks first.
  - **Simple-font glyphs Poppler prints as control codes, or not at all, stay left out and counted** (entry 49), as for the four files of the row (below).
- **Why**:
  - **What Poppler prints for the glyphs of the row.** Poppler maps the encoding names through its name table first; only when a name is not found does it try ligatures, `uniXXXX`, `uXXXX`, variants and numbers, and a code whose name gives nothing is passed through as its own value; a ToUnicode map is merged over all of it and wins (lines 1297 to 1301); a code mapped to 0 has no text (`CharCodeToUnicode.cc` lines 499 to 519, `TextOutputDev.cc` line 2745).
    - `gd-304347.pdf`: the 32 glyphs are code 31 of non-embedded `TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT` and `TimesNewRomanPSMT` with /WinAnsiEncoding (an arrow Word set in a font that has none). WinAnsi names no glyph at 31 and every other name is known, so Poppler maps it to 0 and prints nothing ("credit file go to Q3" where the arrow is); the reader prints the same words.
    - `gd-149558.pdf` and `gd-685036.pdf`: the Univers glyphs are the folio digits 2 to 9 of `Univers-CondensedBold`, which the file's own ToUnicode map gives U+0018 (`<32> <0018>` to `<39> <0018>`, written by Adobe PDF Library 7.0). Poppler prints U+0018 from that map, and pdf.js gives the same, as its ToUnicode map also wins (`src/core/fonts.js`, `amendFallbackToUnicode`, lines 230 to 246); they sit in the running heads the layout leaves out. The Souvenir and Univers glyphs are composite CFF fonts without a ToUnicode map, which Poppler reads by the identity mapping (`GfxCIDFont::GfxCIDFont`, lines 1752 to 1759), 32 places off (`#ONTOUR INTERVAL` for "Contour interval"), the text pdf.js gives as well.
    - `govdocs1-002384.pdf`: the 25 glyphs are codes of `cmex10`, a composite TrueType font, that its ToUnicode map does not list; Poppler reads a font that has a map through the map alone (`GfxCIDFont::getNextChar`, lines 1939 to 1948) and prints nothing for them (`N n=1` where the product sign is).
  - **Where Poppler does give characters, it is the numeric names.** Every glyph the reader left out of a simple font in the corpora below was logged with its font and glyph name (21,518 glyphs of simple fonts, 84,831 of Type 3 fonts, 60,576 of composite fonts, in 216 files). Of the rules above only the numeric names give such glyphs a character. They are the names a printer driver writes for the glyphs of a TrueType font it converts, the number being the character code in the font's code page: `G80` is "P" in the `Futura.Light.BTb0317.5` title of `govdocs1-002457.pdf`, `MT83` is "S" in the `Gen_Helvetica` map labels of `gd-649126.pdf`. pdf.js has a rule of its own for such names (`src/core/evaluator.js`, `_simpleFontToUnicode`: two hexadecimal digits after `G`, four after `g`, two or three decimal digits after `C`), so it reads `G69` as "i" where Poppler reads "E", and leaves `G101` and `MT83` as the code.
  - **Why the three bounds.** Poppler reads every number, and the symbol fonts that number their glyphs in a catalogue then read as unrelated characters: the `H20849` of the MathematicalPi fonts is U+5171 (共) in `pdftotext`, 2,800 such glyphs in 15 files; no number of a one-byte character is that large. Poppler decides hexadecimal per font, and a small subset may hold no letter digit: in `gd-915462.pdf` a font named `G46 G49 G47 G55 G52 G45` ("FIGURE" in hexadecimal, as pdf.js reads it) sits beside fonts named `G4D` and `G2C`, and read per font it gave `.1/74-`. Poppler reads the Zapf Dingbats names only for a font whose name ends in `ZapfDingbats` (line 1084), so it prints "I" for the `a73` of `ZapfDingbatsITC` where the list gives ■, which the reader printed before.
  - **The 60 s of `gd-026598.pdf` was a wait that never ended, not work.** On a fresh thread the file converts to Markdown in 0.6 to 1.4 s; a CPU profile of one conversion has the text thread busy about 0.9 s (pdf.js decoding its 307 image streams and the PNG encoding of the pictures) and the Markdown layout about 11 ms. Converted after its own text on the same thread, its Markdown and HTML hit the deadline in 5 of 6, 3 of 3 and 6 of 6 runs, and its text after its text in 9 of 15; the corpus met it only now and then because the text job runs first and the Markdown job second on one thread, and the HTML job after a timeout gets a new thread.
  - **The cause is pdf.js's decoder of CCITT and JBIG2 pictures, which every document of a thread shares.** `WasmImage` (`pdf.worker.mjs` of pdfjs-dist 6.3.289, lines 15509 to 15600; `src/core/wasm_image.js`) keeps one module promise per decoder for the thread; a document that ends clears it (`WasmImage.cleanup`, from `clearGlobalCaches`), and the next decode sets the decoder up again through the message handler of the document that last set the options. A picture of the text job that pdf.js was still decoding when the job closed its document (a picture with a CCITT /Mask on the last page of `gd-026598.pdf`) did that through the closed document, whose handler never answers. Traced on the thread: the module promise is made again through `d0_worker` after the cleanup and before the next document `d1` sets its options, and every CCITT picture of `d1`, a stencil mask inside its operator list included, waits on it. pdf.js decodes a picture in a task that outlives the operator list (`buildPaintImageXObject`, `PDFImage.buildImage(...).then(...)`, which nothing awaits), so a reader that closes the document at once leaves the task running.
  - **Waiting as the renderer does leaves nothing running when the document closes.** Every dependency arrives, as data or as null for a picture pdf.js cannot decode, so the wait ends, and a document converts the same way whatever ran on the thread before it.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Where Poppler's numeric reading is wrong for a bullet or symbol, the reader now prints the same wrong character** instead of leaving the glyph out or printing another wrong one: "n" for the 63 bullets of a converted Wingdings font in `govdocs1-003054.pdf`, "r" in `govdocs1-001680.pdf`, "Æ" in `govdocs1-004389.pdf`, "E" for a © in `govdocs1-001299.pdf`, "C" and "&" for WordPerfect math bullets in `govdocs1-001057.pdf` and `govdocs1-000807.pdf` (where pdf.js gave "g" and "8"), and "m" for the µ of "µm" in `govdocs1-004659.pdf` and `govdocs1-003198.pdf`; each is the character `pdftotext` prints (the counts match). No rule tells these fonts from the text fonts that use the same names.
  - **A text job now waits for the pictures pdf.js decodes on its pages.** The work is the same: pdf.js decoded them before too, after the job had ended, on the same thread. On `gd-026598.pdf`, text conversions in sequence on one thread take 220 to 257 ms each (15 runs, after the first of each process); the code before hit the 60 s deadline in 9 of the 15 and took 241 to 524 ms in the others.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Poppler's numeric rule without bounds**: 2,800 glyphs of 15 files become CJK ideographs and other unrelated characters, and the subset font of `gd-915462.pdf` loses its words.
  - **Reading numeric names in the glyph recovery only**: it reaches the glyphs pdf.js leaves as control codes, not those it reads wrongly (`G69` as "i", a code above 31 as itself), so a title read half right.
  - **Giving pdf.js the `wasmUrl` of its decoders**: the CCITT, JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 pictures would then decode (they come out null today: 19,012 image draws in 290 files of the corpora have such a stream or mask), and after the first decode on a thread the program is kept; but the first decode of a thread can still be set up through a closing document, and which pictures the results hold is a separate decision (a new #783 row).
  - **A new thread for every document**: pays the pdf.js start (125 ms a thread) on every job to avoid a wait that costs nothing.
  - **A shorter deadline or a retry on timeout**: the wait never ends, so a retry on the same thread waits again.
  - **Reading the folio digits of `gd-149558.pdf` from the encoding over the file's ToUnicode map, or leaving out the codes a composite font's ToUnicode map does not list where pdf.js prints the code (the `e`, `6` and `p` of `cmex10` and `cmmi10` in `govdocs1-002384.pdf`, which Poppler leaves out)**: the first is no reference's rule; the second is (Poppler's), but the font-program maps of entry 70 rely on pdf.js printing the code for the CIDs they leave out, so it needs its own change (a new #783 row).
- **Measured**: text, Markdown and HTML of the 1,261 real-world PDFs and of every tenth PDF of the regression corpus by id (950), origin/main against the change, 6,633 conversions each, three processes per side: 60 conversions differ, in 22 files.
  - `gd-083894.pdf` and `govdocs1-001947.pdf` to Markdown hit the 60 s deadline on origin/main and convert on the change, byte for byte as origin/main converts them on a fresh thread (both have CCITT masks). `gd-026598.pdf` did not hit it in this run of origin/main.
  - `cc-0000308.pdf` and `cc-0000398.pdf` are scans without fonts whose OCR text differs with the load of the machine; run alone, origin/main and the change give the same bytes (three runs each).
  - 18 files read numeric glyph names. Word recall against `pdftotext` rises in 14 (`govdocs1-002457.pdf` 0.953 to 0.998, `govdocs1-002471.pdf` 0.954 to 0.998, `gd-147866.pdf` 0.980 to 0.997, `gd-649126.pdf` 0.939 to 0.968, `govdocs1-002676.pdf` 0.956 to 0.969, `govdocs1-002678.pdf` 0.954 to 0.971, `govdocs1-003437.pdf` 0.953 to 0.968, `govdocs1-004659.pdf` 0.881 to 0.897, and six by less than 0.01) and stays the same in 4, and the word order is the same or closer to `pdftotext` in all 18. `gd-649126.pdf` gets back the seven map pages it left out (`SCALE IS APPROXIMATE` twice, as `pdftotext` prints it).
  - Glyphs left out, summed from the warnings of the Markdown route: 50,944 to 50,685 on the real-world corpus and 108,082 to 107,336 on the regression sample. Refusals (the two timeouts): 9 to 8 and 6 to 5.
  - The times of the two runs are not compared: each side ran once, at different loads from other work on the machine.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdf-picture-determinism.test.ts` (red on origin/main: a hand-made two-page PDF whose page 1 paints a CCITT stencil and page 2 a picture with a CCITT /Mask, six text-then-Markdown rounds on one thread, five Markdown conversions hit the deadline; `gd-026598.pdf` text, Markdown, text, HTML three times on one thread, all six Markdown and HTML conversions hit it; after the change both give on one thread what each target gives on a fresh one; the control, a page of 5,000 distinct pictures to text and Markdown in sequence, passes before and after within a 10 s deadline), `tests/pdf-text-font-program-tounicode.test.ts` (hand-made fonts: `G69 G110 ...` read "Energy Area" at codes below and above 32, `MT83 ...` "SCALE", a font of decimal-looking names read as hexadecimal beside a `G4D` font; controls that stay as they are: a font with one name that is not a number, a run that starts past code 5, a font with its own ToUnicode map, a `ZapfDingbatsITC` font's `a73`, and `H20849`, which stays left out; hostile: 200,000 /Differences names, one font named by 300 pages, 5,001 fonts on a page; red on origin/main, 6 of its 12 new tests) and `tests/pdf-text-real-samples.test.ts` (`govdocs1-002457.pdf` reads `PRIMARY ENERGY STORY: The Tale of Fern Fossil` as `pdftotext` does, `gd-649126.pdf` the map labels `pdftotext` prints with one glyph left out, both red on origin/main; `govdocs1-000839.pdf` keeps its 928 MathematicalPi glyphs left out where `pdftotext` prints 共).
- **Revisit when**: a source tells the text fonts with numeric glyph names from the symbol fonts that use them; pdf.js stops clearing its decoders' module promise when a document ends, or fetches the decoder programs without the document's handler; or the reader gives pdf.js the `wasmUrl` of its decoders.

## 99. DXF, EMF and WMF pages cut at a convex clip, DXF coordinates in the unit of the page, and three rows left to a decision

- **Status**: Implemented for the clip and the DXF unit (issue #783, follow-ups of #791: the polygon clipper and the unit rows), decided 2026-10-25 (QA request in issue #783). The rows on pictures in DXF, the crop of metafile pages and the CGM labels are not implemented: each needs a decision or an upstream fix, given below. Narrows the clip refusals of [42](#42-visio-coreldraw-and-metafile-sources-through-the-office-suite-dxf-page-clips-and-the-formats-with-no-reader) and [79](#79-pen-attributes-in-dxf-dash-arrays-as-line-types-strokes-under-a-skew-as-centre-lines-opacity-dropped-clips-that-hide-nothing-dropped).
- **Decision**:
  - **A clip of one convex polygon cuts what it hides; any other clip that hides something stays refused.** A non-page clip is measured as entry 79 measures it, for every geometry reader: the DXF writer drops it when nothing it hides is more than one point outside it (as before), and the EMF, WMF and CGM encoders, which paint what they draw, drop it only when nothing is outside it at all (`CLIP_TOLERANCE_PIXELS` in `svg-clip-region.ts`). Past that, a region of one convex polygon (Poppler writes every clip as one) cuts the flattened device-space geometry: the lines of a path keep their pieces inside the region (Cyrus and Beck, "Generalized two- and three-dimensional clipping", Computers & Graphics 3(1), 1978), and a filled area keeps its part inside it (Sutherland and Hodgman, "Reentrant polygon clipping", CACM 17(1), 1974), which keeps the winding count of every point inside the region and so works for both fill rules and for a path that crosses itself. A DXF writes every path as its line, so each path is cut as lines. A metafile paints the fill and the stroke, so the fill is cut as an area and the stroke as lines, two elements where a shape has both, so no stroke runs along the cut. Under nested clips each clip that hides anything cuts, which gives their intersection (an empty one draws nothing). A clip that hides something and is not one convex polygon (a union of shapes, a concave or holed path) is refused with the reason, and so is a curve in a clip, as before; so is the box of a bitmap-font character, which cannot be cut.
  - **Limits.** The existing ones stay: 8 active clips, 1,024 edges in a clip, 10^9 device pixels, the 500,000-vertex budget of a document and the 2^23 edge tests of its clips. A cut is charged to the edge tests as its vertices times the edges of the region, and the vertices it adds to the vertex budget. A line of 150,000 vertices that crosses the edge of a clip at each one is cut in 0.5 s on the macOS host; one of 400,000 passes the vertex budget and is refused; a 1,000-edge clip against a line of 5,000 vertices stops at the edge-test limit (`tests/dxf-clip-region.test.ts`, hostile clips).
  - **A DXF is in the unit of the root's width attribute**, a pixel when it names none. This is the unit Inkscape's DXF export writes (`share/extensions/dxf_outlines.py`, lines 395 to 402 and 430 to 433, GPL, behaviour only: the user units times inkex's `inkscape_scale`, which is the width in its own unit over the viewBox width, `inkex/elements/_svg.py` lines 341 to 368). Poppler 26 sizes the SVG of a PDF page in `pt` and Poppler 24.02 in unitless pixels of one point each, so the DXF of a PDF or PostScript page is in points with either release; before, it was in points with Poppler 24.02 and in 4/3 points with Poppler 26. The dash lengths of the line types and the TEXT of bitmap-font characters follow the same unit. An SVG sized in millimetres converts to a DXF in millimetres.
- **Why**:
  - The reference DXF exporters draw no clip at all: `dxf_outlines.py` reads none (`process_shape`, lines 265 to 301), and pstoedit declares its three DXF drivers without clipping (`src/drvdxf.cpp` lines 1730, 1751 and 1760). Dropping a clip draws what it hides, which entry 42 refuses; refusing a page for it loses the whole page. A cut keeps the drawing and draws what the PDF shows. Inkscape's EMF export writes the clip as a clip path of the metafile (`src/extension/internal/emf-print.cpp`, `do_clip_if_present`, lines 971 to 1058: `EMR_SAVEDC`, the path, `EMR_SELECTCLIPPATH` with `RGN_COPY`, and `EMR_RESTOREDC`, one level only, lines 983 to 987), and its WMF export writes none. One cut in the geometry reader serves the four writers alike, and WMF has no clip path.
  - Convex regions are what the files hold: every clip of the real files is a rectangle (the 607 clips of `govdocs1-006137.ps` and `govdocs1-001048.ps`, entry 79, and the clips of `sine_wave.emf` and of the three CGM files), and Cyrus and Beck and Sutherland and Hodgman are exact against a convex region. A general polygon clipper is not needed for them.
  - No new dependency. The maintained permissive clippers were weighed first: a TypeScript port of Clipper2 (`clipper2-ts`, BSL-1.0, the one that also cuts open paths) is under a licence that `licenses.allow.json` does not list, and `polygon-clipping` (MIT, a sweep line after Martinez and others) cuts no open paths and depends on `robust-predicates` (Unlicense), also not listed; the two textbook algorithms are about 80 lines.
  - The unit: the DXF of the same PDF must not change size with the Poppler release, and the root width is where both releases agree.
- **Results** (macOS host, Poppler 26.09, LibreOffice 26.8, Ghostscript 10.07, ezdxf 1.4.5):
  - `govdocs1-001048.ps` (15 pages) and `govdocs1-006137.ps` (66 pages) convert to DXF, every page, where both were refused (they leave `known-refusals.json`); ezdxf audits every page without errors. The ink of the cut pages, drawn by ezdxf's drawing add-on at 100 dpi, against Ghostscript's render of the PostScript page: 0.917 (page 11 of `001048`) and 0.980 to 0.990 (pages 20, 43, 50 and 60 of `006137`) of the DXF ink lies within 2 pixels of Ghostscript's ink. The parts the cut removes from page 11 lie on the frame of the plot, outside its clip.
  - The pages of the clipped metafile samples, written from the SVG that Poppler draws of the office suite's PDF: `sine_wave.emf`, `binary_corvette.cgm` and `plotutils-bin-cgm-v3.cgm` write DXF, EMF and WMF, and `circles.cgm` writes DXF (its EMF and WMF stay refused for a dash array, entry 79). The office suite draws the EMF and WMF again at an SSIM against the PDF page of 0.79 and 0.79 (`sine_wave`), 0.90 and 0.90 (`plotutils`), and 0.95 and 0.93 (`corvette`, the A4 page it puts the picture on trimmed). The registry still offers DXF, EMF and WMF for Visio sources only; offering them for `emf` and `cgm` is a registry change that this entry does not make.
  - The four writers give byte for byte what the base gives for the two SVG files of the vector corpus (`shapes.svg`, `label.svg`), which have no clip. In the parity run (`ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1 npm run bench:quality -- --parity --family vector`), 270 of the 273 vector rows are at or above the reference; the other three are the `shapes.svg->wmf` SSIM row, whose WMF is the base's byte for byte (entry 79 records it failing), and two speed rows of SVG to PDF, a route this change does not touch. In the cad family 270 rows pass and 143 are not evaluated: the strict run stops for lack of `dwg2dxf` on the host, so it ran without strict mode.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A stroke under a clip in a metafile is cut on its centre line, so its painted width reaches up to half its width past the clip edge, and a round or square cap is drawn at a cut. A native EMF clip path would hold the width; the cut is the same for every writer.
  - A DXF writes the line of a filled shape cut at the clip and no line along the cut, since the cut is no line of the drawing.
  - A clip that is not one convex polygon and hides something still refuses the page.
  - An SVG converted to DXF directly now writes the unit of its width (an SVG sized `100mm` writes millimetres, where it wrote pixels).
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Clipper2 or polygon-clipping**: see Why; either needs a licence entry and neither is needed for convex regions.
  - **A native clip path in EMF and `META_INTERSECTCLIPRECT` in WMF**: exact for the pen, but the elements would have to carry their clip to each encoder, and DXF and CGM would still need the cut.
  - **Inches in the DXF, as pstoedit writes by default** (`src/drvdxf.cpp` lines 694 to 700, a scale of 1/72 and `-mm` for millimetres; its version 9 header carries no unit, lines 773 to 779): it changes every DXF of a PDF by a factor of 72 against what the converter wrote with Poppler 24.02, and Inkscape, the reference for SVG to DXF, writes the unit of the page. Recorded for QA.
- **Rows left to a decision**:
  - **Pictures in DXF.** A DXF R12 has no picture entity. `IMAGE` and its `IMAGEDEF` need DXF 2000 (ezdxf `entities/image.py`, MIT, lines 54 and 587) and name the picture as an external file (group 1 of `IMAGEDEF`, line 558), so carrying a picture means a DXF 2000 writer and a ZIP of the DXF and its picture files instead of one `.dxf`. Both reference writers drop pictures (entry 74). Which output to give was a product decision, made in [129](#129-refusal-tail-of-the-nightly-run-of-2026-10-31-a-phonetic-guide-in-a-word-document-is-read-as-the-text-it-is-set-over-a-picture-on-a-page-written-as-dxf-is-left-out-with-a-warning-and-eleven-refusals-are-listed-as-explained): the references' own, a page written without the picture and a warning. In EMF and WMF a picture is a bitmap record (Inkscape writes `EMR_STRETCHDIBITS`, `emf-print.cpp` `PrintEmf::image`); no registry route that reaches the metafile encoders has a real file with a picture today (the registry offers EMF and WMF from Visio drawings only, and their pages hold none), and it needs an in-process picture decoder with pixel limits, so it is a follow-up row.
  - **The crop of a metafile page.** The reference does not crop to the ink: Inkscape's EMF import sizes the page to the picture frame of the header (`rclFrame`, `src/extension/internal/emf-inout.cpp` lines 1832 to 1878), and the office suite puts the picture centred on an A4 page at its preferred size (`sd/source/filter/grf/sdgrffilter.cxx` lines 190 to 225). Inkscape 1.4.4's pages against the ink of the same drawing: `computer_mail.emf` 68.28 x 71.26 pt against 67.90 x 71.26, `testWMF.wmf` 117.0 x 72.75 against 116.25 x 72.16, but `TestRoundRect.wmf` 90.23 x 66.15 against 76.30 x 52.22 and `visio_import_source.wmf` 255.2 x 106.45 against 236.7 x 85.7, so a crop to the ink drops margins of 7 to 11 pt that the reference keeps; and the office suite draws `visio_import_source.wmf` 2.11 times larger than Inkscape does. A crop to the frame needs the preferred size the office suite used, and the crop step belongs in the office-suite route of the worker, outside this change. QA decides between the frame and the ink.
  - **The CGM labels.** The office suite's CGM import places a text of vertical alignment HALF at its x coordinate in y: `filter/source/graphicfilter/icgm/actimpr.cxx`, `CGMImpressOutAct::DrawText`, `case TAV_HALF: aTextPos.Y = o3tl::saturating_add(aTextPos.X, ...)` (line 757 on master, 758 on the 24.2 branch), a typo for `aTextPos.Y`. `plotutils-bin-cgm-v3.cgm` sets its seven y-axis labels (RESTRICTED TEXT, distinct positions in the file) at HALF, and they share one x, so all seven land at one y; with the alignment set to TOP in a copy of the file they land 59.5 pt apart. Its six x-axis labels (TOP) are not on the page that the suite draws at all. The fault is in the importer, not in this route; the fix is upstream.
- **Verified by**: `tests/dxf-clip-region.test.ts` (the cut of a line, of a closed outline joined through its first point, of a curve, under a transform of the clipped element, the `<clipPath>` and its shape, a rotated and a triangular region, nested clips and an empty intersection, the refusal of a concave and a nested concave clip with the reason, and the hostile cases above), `tests/svg-metafile-geometry.test.ts` (a fill cut to its area in EMF and WMF, a stroke cut, a filled and stroked shape painted as an area without a pen and lines, a shape inside the clip unchanged, one outside dropped, a concave clip refused, and the winding count of a self-intersecting fill), `tests/svg-page-clip.test.ts` and `tests/dxf-pen-attributes.test.ts` (a clip that is not the page is cut or refused, never dropped), red on the base (33 tests). `tests/svg-to-dxf.test.ts` (a page sized in `pt` and the same page without a unit write the same coordinates, millimetres scale, dash lengths in the unit), red on the base. `tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts` (the two PostScript files convert every page and ezdxf audits them; the bitmap-font TEXT is read in points with either Poppler), `tests/vector-sources-real-samples.test.ts` (the DXF extents of the Visio drawings hold the ink in points).
- **Revisit when**: QA decides the crop of metafile pages, the output for a DXF page with a picture, or the inch unit; a real page hides part of its drawing under a clip that is not one convex polygon; a stroke cut at a clip shows its width past the edge in a real file; the office suite fixes `TAV_HALF`; or the registry is to offer DXF, EMF and WMF for EMF and CGM sources.

## 100. EMF and WMF pages: the frame of the header is the page, and the drawing is handed to the office suite on a page of that size

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783 row "Found by #884: metafile pages follow the header frame in the reference engine"; epic #760), decided 2026-10-25 (QA request: give EMF and WMF pages the size the reference import filter gives them). It extends entry 42 (what reads the metafiles) and leaves the targets and refusals of that entry as they are. Entry 99 (#884) is about the metafiles the worker writes; this entry is about the ones it reads. Amended 2026-10-25 (QA request, row "Found by #885" of issue #783): a metafile whose PDF has no ink is refused. Amended again 2026-10-25 (review of #886): a metafile that is a header and its end record is handed on as an empty page.
- **Decision**:
  - **The page of an EMF or WMF file is the frame of its header, in points, and the drawing is drawn at the scale the header gives.** The header is read in process (`src/lib/conversions/office/metafile-page-frame.ts`) by the rules of the reference import filter (Inkscape 1.4, GPL, followed for its behaviour only): for an EMF, `rclFrame` of EMR_HEADER in 0.01 mm with both edges inside the frame, and 25.4 over 30 of it for a file whose description is "Adobe Systems" and whose next record is SETMAPMODE with the anisotropic mode (`emf-inout.cpp` lines 1832 to 1878, `AI_hack` lines 1486 to 1502); for a WMF, the placeable box over its logical units per inch (0 counts as 1440), both edges inside the box, and for a file with no placeable header or an empty box the first SETWINDOWEXT record, or A4 landscape when the records end first (`wmf-inout.cpp` lines 1602 to 1666, `uwmf.c` `wmfheader_get` and `U_WMRRECSAFE_get`).
  - **The office suite is given a drawing of that page that holds the file as it is, in place of the file.** For a request that the office suite writes as PDF (the PDF itself and the page chain behind PNG, JPEG, SVG, EPS and PostScript), the worker writes an OpenDocument Graphics package (`src/lib/conversions/office/metafile-frame-document.ts`): one page of the frame's size with no margins, one frame of the same size at the origin, the metafile as a package part byte for byte. `withMetafileFrame` in `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts` wraps the LibreOffice run and hands over `odg` instead of `emf` or `wmf`. The suite draws the metafile into the frame's rectangle, so the page and the scale are the frame's.
  - **Bounds of ours, where the reference has none.** A header that gives no page leaves the file to the office suite as before, on its own A4 page: a file that is no EMF or WMF, an EMF whose header size is below 88 bytes, not a multiple of 4, past the end of the file, above 64 KiB or without the signature " EMF", a WMF whose standard header is missing, short or of another type than 1 or 2, a record of the WMF that is shorter than 6 bytes or past the end of the first mebibyte of the file, an empty or reversed frame, a page under 3 or over 14,400 points on either side (PDF 32000-1 Annex C, the sizes a PDF reader has to handle), and a page of more than 10.3 million square points.
  - **The area bound is the page the raster chain holds at its default resolution.** `MAX_METAFILE_PAGE_AREA_POINTS` is the page whose raw RGB bitmap at 150 dpi (`resolvePdfRasterDpi`) is `PPM_PAGE_MAX_BYTES` (128 MiB, `src/worker/poppler-ppm.ts`): 3,210 points on a side for a square, and an A0 sheet (2,384 by 3,370 points, 8.0 million) fits. The PNG route falls back to Poppler's own PNG writer above that limit, but JPEG and TIFF pages have no bound on their bitmap, so a header of 14,400 points on both sides (a 30-byte header, a 5 m page, 2.7 GB of bitmap at 150 dpi) is kept off the chain. A test pins the constant to the two values it comes from, so it changes with them.
  - **Only the start of a file is read to find its page.** The EMF reader looks at the first 64 KiB (a real header is 88 bytes and its description a few dozen) and the WMF reader at the first mebibyte, so a file on disk is read whole only once it has a page, and the records of a WMF without a box are searched in at most 1 MiB, never in the 44 million six-byte records that 256 MiB can hold. The reference reads every record; the window extent is the 3rd, 5th and 7th record, within the first 26 KiB, of the three real WMF files in the corpus (`lo-visio_import_source.wmf`, `lo-testroundrect.wmf`, `tika-testwmf.wmf`), and a record that is the first to cross the limit is read as a record that runs past the end of the file. The reader works on that prefix whatever the caller holds, so a file in memory and a file on disk give the same page.
  - **The package is built within the request's signal.** The metafile is stored in the package, not deflated (the suite reads the part as it is, and deflating up to 256 MiB in JavaScript is seconds of CPU outside the stage timeout), and the signal is checked before and after the package is built.
  - **A metafile that draws nothing is refused with a typed error.** When the PDF that the office suite wrote for an EMF or WMF (the PDF itself and the page chain behind PNG, JPEG, SVG and the other targets) has no ink on its page, the conversion fails with a `ConversionFailedError` (HTTP 400) that says the file draws nothing, and the PDF is removed. Ink is decided by drawing the page with Poppler at 72 dpi and looking for a pixel that is not white (`src/worker/pdf-ink.ts`, the raw PPM page of `poppler-ppm.ts`; 16 to 17 ms for a real file, against 0.5 to 2.2 s for the conversion). The renderer allocates the page bitmap before it writes a byte, so it is held to 2048 MiB of address space as the other page renderers are, besides the output limit of 128 MiB. A fixed `-scale-to` size was measured and left out: it keeps a hairline of 0.1 point on a page of 200 x 120 and on one of 3000 x 3000 points visible at 1000 and 2000 pixels, but it draws a large page below the 72 dpi the check is defined at and enlarges every small page. A metafile is one page, so the first page is the whole drawing, and no other document (a PDF source, an office document, a drawing of several pages) is judged by this: a white page of a document with other drawn pages is never refused. `withMetafileInk` in `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts` wraps the office suite run and the frame wrapper, so the file the suite is given as it is (a header with no usable frame) is held to the same rule. A worker without `pdftoppm` answers an unavailable engine (503) for these conversions and does not hand out a PDF it could not look at; the worker image carries Poppler for every page target. **A metafile that is a header and its end record is handed on without a look,** as an empty page of the header's size: the reference opens such a file and writes an empty page, and refuses only a file whose record walk fails (`isEmptyMetafile` in `metafile-page-frame.ts`, which reads the leading bytes the frame reader already reads). An EMF qualifies when its header states two records and the size of the file, EMR_EOF (type 14) follows the header and is the rest of the file; a WMF qualifies when META_EOF (function 0, three words) follows its standard header and it has no placeable header. The rule is not a record walker: a file that has any other record is looked at as before.
  - **Nothing a file holds is written into the XML.** The package text is constants and the page size to three decimals; the metafile is a stored part, read by the suite's own import filter as when it opened the file.
- **Why**:
  - **What the reference engine does.** For `emf` to `pdf` and `wmf` to `png` the reference service runs Inkscape. Its filters make the document the header's frame (width and height in mm from `rclFrame`, or from the placeable box and its unit) and place the upper left corner of the header's bounds at the corner of the page. The page is therefore the size the file says it has, and a picture that is smaller or larger than its frame keeps its place in it.
  - **What the office suite does without this.** It opens a picture on an A4 page, centred at the size the picture prefers, reduced to fit when it is larger (`sd/source/filter/grf/sdgrffilter.cxx`, `SdGRFFilter::InsertSdrGrafObj`, lines 185 to 221 of the `libreoffice-25-2-0` tag). The page is A4 whatever the file is, and a file that prefers more than A4 is drawn smaller than its frame: `visio_import_source.wmf` came out 2.11 times larger than the reference's page, scaled to fit A4's width.
  - **Measured against Inkscape 1.4.4** (the frame and the ink of the first page, in points; the ink is the box of the pixels that are not white at 72 to 600 dpi):
    - `computer_mail.emf`: page 595.28 x 841.89 before, 68.29 x 71.26 after, Inkscape 68.28 x 71.26; the ink 80.5 x 84.5 before, 68.5 x 71.5 after and in Inkscape. The file is an Adobe Illustrator file, so the 25.4 over 30 rule is what makes the page equal.
    - `TestRoundRect.wmf`: page 90.23 x 66.16 after, Inkscape 90.23 x 66.15; ink 76.5 x 52.5 after (7 from each edge), Inkscape 77 x 53 (6.5).
    - `visio_import_source.wmf` (no placeable header, the window extent gives the box): page 255.20 x 106.44 after, Inkscape 255.2 x 106.45; ink 237 x 86 after and in Inkscape, 499.5 x 181 before.
    - `testWMF.wmf`: page 117.01 x 72.74 after, Inkscape 117 x 72.75; ink 82 x 11 after, 81 x 11 in Inkscape.
    - SSIM of the first page against Inkscape's, before and after, at 200 to 600 dpi: 0.64 to 0.84 for `computer_mail.emf` (Inkscape draws the envelope's body dark and every other renderer white), 0.77 to 0.98 for `TestRoundRect.wmf`, 0.78 to 0.99 for `visio_import_source.wmf` and 0.91 to 0.92 for `testWMF.wmf` (letters 11 points high). `sine_wave.emf` and `testEMF.emf` crash Inkscape 1.4.4 on macOS, so their pages (646.72 x 529.03 and 154.91 x 95.98) are the frames worked out from the headers by hand.
  - **The page size is a property of a drawing, not an option of the PDF export.** The filter data of `draw_pdf_Export` that the worker builds (page range, PDF/A, compression) holds no page size, so the page comes from the document: ODF 1.3 part 1 stores it as `fo:page-width` and `fo:page-height` of `style:page-layout-properties`, named by the master page, and the suite reads it as it reads any drawing. The styles part of the package has an `office:styles` element: a flat file without one kept the A4 page in LibreOffice 26.8. The six drawings of the real files give the pages above in LibreOffice 26.8 (the host) and in 24.2.7 (the Lima VM).
  - **Why not crop the A4 PDF afterwards.** The suite's page holds the picture at a size it chose (centred, and reduced to fit when larger), so the page of the frame is not a cropping of it: a file that prefers more than A4 is drawn at a smaller scale, which a crop does not undo.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A frame is not always what is drawn.** The header's frame is the size the producer wrote; a file whose frame is far larger or smaller than its drawing gets a page of that size with the drawing where the header puts it, as in the reference engine. `TestRoundRect.wmf` has 7 points of white on each side for this reason.
  - **A file whose header gives no page keeps the A4 page and the picture at the suite's scale** (the bounds above), so a page of an absurd header does not decide a PDF; the file still converts.
  - **The headers are read twice**, by this reader and by the suite. They are 88 bytes of an EMF and 40 of a WMF. A WMF without a box also reads its records up to the first window extent, within the first mebibyte.
  - **A page over the area bound, or a WMF whose window extent is past the first mebibyte, keeps the A4 page** as every file did before this entry. An A0 plot fits; a poster of 1.5 m by 1.5 m does not.
  - **A header over junk records is refused, as the reference refuses it.** LibreOffice 24.2.7 (the Lima VM) and 26.8 (the host) load an EMF or WMF whose header is valid and whose records are not without a failure and write a PDF with no ink, from the file itself and from the drawing that holds it alike (checked on eight files in 24.2.7: header only, junk after the header, zero and 0xff bytes, 200 KB of junk, a placeable and a standard WMF header with junk or with nothing after it; on two of them in 26.8). Before this amendment the route answered such a file with an empty page of the frame's size and HTTP 200. Inkscape 1.4.4 opens no document for any of them and writes no PDF: it checks the size and type of every record and stops at the first that is not a record (`emf-inout.cpp` `myEnhMetaFileProc` lines 1680 to 1693, `file_status = 0`, and `Emf::open` lines 3588 to 3597, which makes a document only when the walk succeeded; `wmf-inout.cpp` lines 1703 to 1718 and 3167 to 3174), so its command writes no file (exit 0, `ink_file_open ... cannot be opened`, tried on the junk EMF and WMF, the 88-byte EMF header and a header and its end record are the exception below). No retry on the unframed file is added, since it would give the same answer.
  - **A metafile that is a header and its end record is handed on as an empty page, and a well-formed metafile of other records that draw nothing is refused.** Inkscape 1.4.4 opens an EMF of a header and its end record and a WMF with no placeable header of a standard header and META_EOF, and writes a PDF with no ink for each (994 bytes; A4 landscape for the WMF, the frame's size for the EMF), so the route does the same instead of refusing it as junk: the office suite also writes an empty page for them. A placeable WMF header followed by META_EOF is not in that class: the same Inkscape opens no document for it (it also opens none for a placeable WMF whose only record before META_EOF is a window extent, and writes a page once a window origin and extent are both present), so it stays refused with the junk. Only these two shapes are recognised, from the leading bytes the frame reader already reads; a file of other well-formed records that draw nothing (a window origin and extent and nothing drawn, say) is still refused, because telling it from a file of unreadable records means the record walk the reference makes (the alternative below). A real file of that kind has not been seen in the corpus (the six real EMF and WMF files all draw).
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Inkscape in the worker.** Entry 42 rejects it (GPL-3.0, a large GTK and Python distribution for importers the suite already has); the reference's page rule is a few lines and is read here for its behaviour.
  - **A PDF post-process that sets the MediaBox to the picture's rectangle.** The picture's size and place in the suite's PDF are not the frame's (see above), and finding them again from the PDF is a second reader of what the suite drew.
  - **Importing the metafile and saving an ODG first, then editing its page.** Two office suite runs for every metafile, each about the cost of one conversion, to reach the document this change writes directly.
  - **A walk of the records before the suite is run, as the reference does.** It would refuse exactly the files the reference refuses and write the empty page for a file of readable records that draws nothing, but it is a second reader of EMF (the 122 record types and their sizes) and of WMF (the type table, `U_wmr_properties`) that the office suite then reads again, with the EMF+ records that live inside comment records still to decide. The drawn page answers the question the client has (is there a picture) with the engine that draws it.
  - **Reading the PDF's content stream for a paint operator.** The suite's page for a file it could not draw is a white rectangle painted over the page (`1 1 1 rg` ... `f*`), so the stream has operators; telling that from a drawing that paints white needs the drawing.
  - **Raising the failure of a header that gives no page.** The suite converts these files and the PDF is right but for its page; a typed refusal would remove conversions that work.
- **Verified by**: `tests/metafile-page-frame.test.ts` (the frame of an EMF with and without an offset, the Adobe rule and the four ways it does not apply, the placeable box, the unit 0, a box away from the origin, the window extent with and without a placeable header, A4 landscape; hostile: no metafile, the other format's bytes, an EMF with a wrong signature, a header size below 88, past the end of the file or not a multiple of 4, a truncated header, empty, reversed, 2^31 wide and below-minimum frames, WMF boxes that are reversed or of unit 65535 or 1, records past the end, of size 0 or shorter than 6 bytes, a window extent that is zero or negative or too short, 200,000 records that leave the first mebibyte unread in under a second, a window extent whose record ends at the first mebibyte and one that ends 2 bytes later, the page area at the bound and one unit above it, an A0 sheet, an EMF header of 64 KiB and of 64 KiB and 4 bytes, and the page of a file equal to the page of its prefix; red before the reader existed and before each bound), `tests/office-suite-route.test.ts` (`withMetafileFrame`: the staged drawing's page and frame sizes in points, margins 0, the metafile as a package part byte for byte, the stored media type as the first entry of the package, an input held in a file with its output path, the cases that go to the office suite unchanged, the answer or failure passed through, the picture part stored and the XML deflated, a request cancelled before and while the package is built, and a file on disk that is not read whole unless it has a page; red before `withMetafileFrame` existed and before each of the last three) and `tests/vector-sources-real-samples.test.ts` (the six real EMF and WMF files: the page of each as pinned above through the whole conversion, the first page against Inkscape's for the four it reads, and the render checks of every target at a resolution that gives a small page as many pixels as an A4 page, and four files with a valid header over junk records, which the suite alone writes as a PDF with no ink and which the route refuses for the PDF, PNG and SVG with the typed error, an EMF and a standard WMF of a header and an end record that convert to an empty page of the header's size and a placeable one that is refused, and a real file that still converts with ink; red before `withMetafileInk` was wired in), `tests/office-suite-route.test.ts` (`withMetafileInk`: EMF and WMF refused with the PDF removed, an EMF and a WMF of a header and its end record handed on without a look from a buffer, a staged input and a file on disk, the same EMF header with junk after it refused, a PDF with ink handed on as it is, other sources, other targets and a run with no output not looked at, and the failure of the look standing with the PDF removed), `tests/metafile-page-frame.test.ts` (`isEmptyMetafile`: an EMF of two stated records, its size and EMR_EOF at the end, and a standard WMF with META_EOF first; not empty: another record count or size, a record that is not EMR_EOF, an end record of another size or cut short, a record between, a header only, a window extent first, an end record of four words, a placeable header, a header of type 3), `tests/pdf-ink.test.ts` (the renderer is started with the memory cap; a page of nothing and a page painted white have no ink; a filled shape, a hairline of 0.1 point and a rectangle of 98% grey have; a page of 3,000 x 3,000 points, the raster at the area bound, is read; a file that is no PDF is the renderer's failure, not an answer). Inkscape is the oracle of the file tests, run through `INKSCAPE_PATH`; the tests skip without it (it writes no PDF for the four junk files and for a placeable WMF header and its end record, and an empty page for an EMF header and its end record and for a standard WMF header and its end record, which the route hands on as the same empty page).
- **Revisit when**: the reference engine changes how it reads the header; a metafile of the corpus whose frame the producer wrote wrongly gets a page that the reference service does not give it (the bounds above then need the reference's own handling); or the office suite's PDF export takes a page size, which would end the drawing this change writes; a real EMF or WMF is found that holds only well-formed records that draw nothing (the refusal of such a file then reverses to an empty page, which needs the record walk); or a metafile whose ink is fainter than a pixel of the 72 dpi page is refused as empty.

## 101. PDF pictures: pdf.js gets its WebAssembly decoders for CCITT, JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 pictures under a memory maximum and a check of each picture before it is decoded, and a job that writes no pictures decodes none

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783, the alternative that entry 98 left open: "giving pdf.js the `wasmUrl` of its decoders"), decided 2026-10-25 (QA request). It acts on the condition in the last line of entry 98 and changes what the pictures of entry 81 hold. Amended 2026-10-25 (review of #887): the decoders get a memory maximum, and each picture is checked from its headers before pdf.js reads the document.
- **Decision**:
  - **The text reader gives pdf.js the `wasm` folder of its own package (`wasmUrl: pdfjsDataUrl('wasm')`, `pdf-text-geometry.ts`).** pdf.js 6 decodes CCITT fax, JBIG2 and JPEG 2000 pictures with the modules `jbig2.wasm` and `openjpeg.wasm` that it loads from that folder (`WasmImage`, `pdf.worker.mjs` of pdfjs-dist 6.3.289, lines 9666 to 9766; `JBig2CCITTFaxImage` line 9768, `JpxImage` line 10751). Without the folder the decoder is null, the picture arrives as null and the HTML, Markdown and Word results leave it out. pdf.js's own Node tests pass the same option (`test/unit/test_utils.js`, lines 35 to 37 and 67 to 68, v6.3.289).
  - **A job that writes no pictures sets `maxImageSize` to 0 and so decodes none.** `buildPaintImageXObject` skips an image larger than the budget before any decoder runs (`pdf.worker.mjs` lines 34497 to 34503). The text-only target (`txt`) never asks for pictures (`job.images`), so it no longer pays for the decoding it threw away; the other targets keep the 50 million pixels of entry 81.
  - **The limits of entry 81 stay** (256 pictures a page, 32,768 placements and 128 MiB of picture bytes a document, 50 million pixels a picture's dictionary may declare, the 60 s deadline and the 1,024 MB heap of the text thread), and two are added for the decoders, whose memory is outside that heap.
  - **Each decoder module may grow to 256 MiB** (`PDF_WASM_DECODER_MAX_BYTES`), not the 2 GiB it is built with (`-s MAXIMUM_MEMORY=2GB` in `compile.sh` of pdf.js.jbig2 and pdf.js.openjpeg). The reader passes pdf.js a `BinaryDataFactory` (`pdf-wasm-memory.ts`, an option of `getDocument`) that reads files as pdf.js's own Node factory does (`pdf.mjs` lines 15582 to 15603 and 16133 to 16137) and, for `jbig2.wasm` and `openjpeg.wasm`, rewrites the maximum of the module's memory section in the bytes the old maximum took (a padded LEB128 integer, so no section length changes); a module whose memory has no maximum, or none to lower, makes the load fail, and the picture is then null. A decode that would grow past the maximum gets no memory: the module's `emscripten_resize_heap` catches the failed `grow` and malloc returns null (`pdf.worker.mjs` lines 15387 to 15411). OpenJPEG then returns an error, PDFium's JBIG2 code aborts (`FX_OutOfMemoryTerminate`, `core/fxcrt/fx_memory.cpp` line 70), and either way the decode throws and pdf.js gives the picture as null, as for any picture it cannot decode. The 256 MiB is PDFium's own largest JBIG2 bitmap, 2^31 bits (`kMaxImageBytes`, `core/fxcodec/jbig2/jbig2_image.cpp` lines 30 to 31), and three times the most a real picture took (below).
  - **Each JPEG 2000, JBIG2 and CCITT picture is checked from its headers before pdf.js reads the document** (`pdf-picture-guard.ts`, `pdf-picture-headers.ts`), for a job that writes pictures. A picture whose decode would allocate more than 192 MiB (three quarters of the maximum; the rest holds the module's own data and its 5 % growth steps) or walk more than 100 million pixels (twice the 50 million of a dictionary) is left out: the image object is defined again as `null` in an incremental update of the copy pdf.js reads, the same update that adds the ToUnicode maps of entry 70, and pdf.js skips the drawing as it skips any XObject that is not a stream. An image whose /SMask or /Mask is past a limit is left out with it. What a decode allocates follows the sources of the two codecs. For JPEG 2000 it is the codestream OpenJPEG decodes, inside the `jp2c` box or bare (ISO 15444-1 A.5.1, A.6.1, A.6.2), with the reduction pdf.js applies: pdf.js reads its size from the first `FF 51` pair anywhere in the stream (`JpxImage.parseImageProperties`, `pdf.worker.mjs` lines 16648 to 16670), which a box ahead of the codestream can fake, and reduces only when JPXDecode is the first filter (`PDFImage`, lines 39296 to 39314), by `getReducePowerForJPX` (lines 9199 to 9219; in Node, which has no OffscreenCanvas, every side above 2048 is reduced). The estimate is the 32-bit samples at the reduced size, a tile buffer when there are several tiles, a full-size copy when a component is subsampled (`upsample_component`, `decoder.c` of pdf.js.openjpeg lines 92 to 145), the code-block and precinct structures of the largest tile at every resolution with the coding style of the main header (OpenJPEG `tcd.c` lines 1029 to 1199, `tcd.h` lines 120 to 160; a tile-part header that sets smaller code-blocks is left to the memory maximum), the coding parameters of every tile (`j2k.c` lines 2413 and 2475 to 2483) and the coded bytes. For JBIG2 it is the page buffer pdf.js asks for at the dictionary's size (`decoder.cpp` of pdf.js.jbig2 lines 32 to 62), the bitmap of every region of the stream and of its JBIG2Globals (PDFium keeps an intermediate region's bitmap for the segments that refer to it, `jbig2_context.cpp` lines 862, 985, 1089 and 1167, and allocates a region larger than the page all the same), pattern dictionaries, a minimum for every symbol, and the coded bytes. For CCITT it is the pixels walked: pdf.js asks for the dictionary's rows and each is decoded at /Columns (`decoder.cpp` lines 64 to 88), and PDFium refuses a /Columns or a row count past 65,535 (`faxmodule.cpp` lines 43 and 681 to 707). An inline picture cannot be defined again, so one past a limit refuses the job (413). The check reads a picture as pdf.js does: `/F` before `/Filter` and `/DP` before `/DecodeParms` in every stream (`Parser.filter`, `pdf.worker.mjs` lines 17596 to 17598, through `Dict.get`, lines 6542 to 6549), `/H` before `/Height` for the rows of a CCITT picture (`CCITTFaxStream.decodeImage`, line 15698) and `/Width` and `/Height` for a JBIG2 picture (`Jbig2Stream.decodeImage`, line 16026), the abbreviations `JPX` and `CCF` as their codecs (`makeFilter`, lines 17658 and 17667; `JPX` is decoded at full size, since only the spelling `JPXDecode` is reduced), an indirect /Subtype followed (`Dict.get` fetches it), the file header of a JBIG2 stream and of its JBIG2Globals removed before the segments are read (`Jbig2Stream.stripFileHeader`, lines 16009 to 16016), and a stream with a picture codec filter taken for a picture whatever its /Subtype, since pdf.js decodes an /SMask or /Mask stream as an image without looking at it (`PDFImage.buildImage`, lines 39485 to 39498). The reader of the filters (`filterChain` of `pdf-document.ts`) is the same for every stream of the document, so the content streams, the fonts and the pictures see one /F, /Filter, /DP and /DecodeParms. A JPEG 2000 header is held to the limits OpenJPEG holds it to, 16,384 components (`opj_j2k_read_SIZ`, `j2k.c` line 2141 of 8314119b) and 32 resolution levels (`opj_j2k_read_SPCod_SPCoc`, line 10972, with `OPJ_J2K_MAXRLVLS` of 33 in `j2k.h` line 154), and a header past them, or a marker that runs past the data, is one OpenJPEG refuses and is left to it. A header reader that throws a RangeError on a picture's bytes leaves the image object out and an inline picture to the memory maximum; it never refuses the document.
  - **A document whose pages would decode more than 32,768 of these pictures is refused before any is decoded** (413), counted as pdf.js decodes them: once on each page that draws one, its masks and the inline ones included. It is the placement limit of entry 81 counted before decoding, so it refuses no document that limit would let through, except one with pages of more than 256 such pictures, whose pictures past the 256th are decoded and never recorded.
  - **The check's own cost is bounded.** The headers of each image object are read once whatever the number of pages that draw it, a JBIG2Globals stream once whatever the number of pictures that share it (its segments are walked once and each picture starts from that result; a walk reads at most 65,536 segments, a bound of ours, since PDFium and pdf.js set none and the 131 JBIG2 streams of the 1,269 cached real-world PDFs hold at most 12), an inline picture's dictionary over its own `BI` to `ID` text (an array that is never closed ends there), the filters ahead of a codec (Flate or ASCII wrappers) decode within 64 MiB a document with a refusal past it, and a coded stream whose wrapper this reader does not decode (LZW, RunLength) or that is encrypted is left to the memory maximum. The pages of an encrypted document are not read here (the byte budgets of its content streams are skipped too, `PdfDocument.contentStreams`), so its pictures are not counted either. The coded bytes given to the header readers are budgeted at 64 MiB a document, the budget of the filters ahead of the codecs; the most a real document is given is 2.85 MiB (`govdocs1-003685.pdf`, over the 1,268 cached real-world PDFs): the readers are linear in the bytes they are given, but streams whose /Length is an object written after them can each run to the end of one large stream, so that the spans overlap and their sum is not bounded by the file. A picture or a JBIG2Globals stream that does not fit in what is left, and every one after it, is not read and is left to the memory maximum.
  - **The check is advisory.** The 256 MiB maximum and the 60 s deadline of the text thread are the bounds that bind; the check leaves out, before they are reached, the pictures whose headers show that they would reach the maximum. It scans the objects of the file in file order, where pdf.js follows the cross-reference (duplicate object numbers, objects inside object streams, a trailer that names an /Encrypt that the scan does not apply), so a crafted file can show the check an object other than the one pdf.js decodes. That is a row of the #783 checklist and is not closed by this entry; until it is, a picture the check was shown a different object for is decoded under the maximum.
  - **A module that cannot be loaded gives a null picture, not the JavaScript decoder.** When `jbig2.wasm` or `openjpeg.wasm` fails to load (an unreadable file, or a memory maximum that cannot be lowered), pdf.js imports `${wasmUrl}jbig2_nowasm_fallback.js` or `openjpeg_nowasm_fallback.js`, the JavaScript builds whose heap may grow to 2 GiB (`#instantiateWasm` and `#getJsModule`, `pdf.worker.mjs` lines 15545 to 15575); no option turns that off (`useWasm: false` selects the same files). The factory reads the modules from the real folder, and pdf.js is given a `wasmUrl` below it that holds nothing (`cappedDecoderOptions`, `pdf-wasm-memory.ts`), so the import fails and the picture is null. In Node pdf.js reads `wasmUrl` itself for nothing else: its ICC module is off when pdf.js does not fetch in the worker (`QCMS.setOptions`, line 8514; `getDocument`, `pdf.mjs` line 22004). The pinned pdfjs-dist 6.3.289 patches both modules, so the case does not arise with it; the test makes it arise.
- **Why**:
  - **The pictures were missing from the results.** 19,012 image draws in 290 files of the corpora had a CCITT, JBIG2 or JPEG 2000 stream or mask (entry 98). Poppler's `pdfimages` lists and writes all of them; `pdfimages -list` is the oracle below.
  - **Entry 98 rejected the option because of a wait that no longer exists.** The first decode on a thread could be set up through a document that was closing; entry 98 now releases a page only after pdf.js has delivered what its operator list depends on, so a decode is never cut by the end of a document.
  - **Why `maxImageSize` and not a `wasmUrl` per job.** `WasmImage.cleanup()` clears the module promise but each decoder keeps the bytes it fetched (`#buffer`, lines 9672 and 9717 to 9727), so a `wasmUrl` that only picture jobs pass would still be in use for every later job of the thread. The budget is per document and decides what is decoded.
  - **The decoders are the fast path.** The same files with `useWasm: false`, which makes pdf.js load the JavaScript builds of the decoders (`*_nowasm_fallback.js`), give the same picture bytes and take longer: `govdocs1-003440.pdf` (12 JBIG2 pages) 2.7 s with WebAssembly and 7.2 s without, `govdocs1-003685.pdf` (70 pages) 3.7 s and 5.5 s, `govdocs1-002608.pdf` (119 CCITT pictures) 6.7 s and 7.2 s (in-process reader, 3 runs each, alternating, Linux VM, Node.js 24.20).
  - **Why the memory maximum and the check (review of #887).** The thread's `resourceLimits` bound its V8 heap only. Before this entry the decoders were null, so a picture cost nothing; with them, a few hundred bytes of JPEG 2000 whose real size a decoy marker hides, or a JPEG 2000 behind FlateDecode (pdf.js then decodes it at full size), or JBIG2 regions larger than the page, held up to 2 GiB per module and per thread, and with the 4 threads of the pool the 10 GiB container of the default worker would kill the worker and every job in it. PDFium and pdf.js leave out a picture whose decoder fails (`CPDF_DIB::LoadJpxBitmap` returns null, `core/fpdfapi/page/cpdf_dib.cpp` lines 668 to 690), so leaving it out keeps the text and the other pictures of a document whose one picture is past a limit. The maximum is the bound for what the headers do not show (a JBIG2 symbol's bitmap is coded in the arithmetic data, an encrypted or LZW-wrapped stream is not read); the check keeps a picture from growing a decoder to it, which costs the time and the memory first, and leaves a JBIG2 module that aborted with its leaked memory for the rest of the document.
  - **What the decoder spends.** A CPU profile of `govdocs1-003440.pdf` (not a reported run) has 70 % of its time in two functions of one WebAssembly module (the file's pictures are JBIG2), 3 % in the 1-bit unpack of the reader and 3 % in the garbage collector. The 12 pictures cost about 218 ms each in the timings below.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Scanned documents with a text layer take longer to HTML, Markdown and Word**, because their pictures are now decoded, encoded and embedded. On the Linux VM (4 cores; five passes that alternate base and change, each pass a fresh process per side and file that converts once to warm up and then three timed times, so 15 timed conversions per side and file) the Markdown of seven scanned documents costs, per page, 47 ms (`govdocs1-002608.pdf`, 132 pages: 0.38 s to 6.6 s), 48 ms (`govdocs1-003685.pdf`, 70 pages: 0.38 s to 3.8 s), 60 ms (`govdocs1-004513.pdf`, 135 pages: 1.1 s to 9.3 s), 117 ms (`govdocs1-000157.pdf`, 22 pages of fax tiles, 727 pictures: 0.20 s to 2.8 s) and 218 ms (`govdocs1-003440.pdf`, 12 JBIG2 pages: 0.08 s to 2.7 s) more; the two files with few or small pictures cost 25 ms a page (`govdocs1-000142.pdf`) and 18 ms (`govdocs1-003071.pdf`, 1,286 pictures that were already decoded). The results are larger in step: `govdocs1-004513.pdf` goes from 2 MB to 33.6 MB of Markdown.
  - **A scan of several hundred pages can reach a limit it did not reach**: at 47 to 218 ms a page the 60 s deadline of the text thread is about 270 pages of the slowest kind and 1,300 of the fastest, and the 128 MiB of picture bytes is about 800 pages at the 0.16 MiB a page of `govdocs1-003685.pdf` and `govdocs1-004513.pdf`. A document past either is refused with the typed error of entry 81 where before it converted without its pictures. No file of the two corpora moved from a result to an error: the refusals (10 for text, 12 for Markdown and HTML) are the same files before and after.
  - **Text results get faster where the pictures were decoded for nothing**: `govdocs1-002608.pdf` 261 ms to 148 ms and `govdocs1-003071.pdf` 372 ms to 207 ms (medians of 15, same bytes); the other five files are within the run-to-run range.
  - **A decoder's worst case is 256 MiB per module and thread**: two modules in each of the 4 threads of the pool hold at most 2 GiB beside the 4 GiB of thread heaps, inside the 10 GiB of the default worker and the 14 GiB of the memory worker (`docker-compose.yml`). A real picture took at most 43 MiB of the JPEG 2000 module and 16 MiB (its initial size) of the JBIG2 module in the 251 files below, and large pictures made for the test 76 to 87 MiB (a lossy 8000 x 8000 RGB reduced by pdf.js to 2000 x 2000, a lossless 2048 x 2048 RGB, a 2048 x 2048 RGBA).
  - **The estimates are of the large allocations, not of every byte**, and they count a picture the decoder would refuse anyway (a reduction past the codestream's levels, a region PDFium will not allocate) as if it decoded it; such a picture is left out instead of failing, with the same result. A dropped picture leaves no placement (a picture whose decoder fails leaves a placement without data), so on that page the JPEG pictures go the PNG route of entry 81.
  - **After a JBIG2 decode aborts, the module keeps the memory it leaked for the rest of the document** (the C++ stack does not unwind in WebAssembly); later pictures of that document decode in what is left, and the next document gets a new module (`WasmImage.cleanup`). Forty aborts in one document left the pictures after them decoded, at 314 MiB of resident growth.
  - **The check costs little**: over the 251 files with such a picture, the bytes handed to pdf.js take 162 ms longer to prepare in all (1,841 ms to 2,003 ms, best of three per file, in process on the Mac at a load average of 3.4), at most 68 ms for one file (`govdocs1-002489.pdf`); a job that writes no pictures does not run it.
  - **A document with more than 64 MiB of decoded wrapper bytes ahead of its picture codecs is refused** (413), where before it converted; none of the 1,261 real-world PDFs reaches it: each reads within one 64 MiB budget even when the stored bytes of every picture are counted as well.
  - **The licence texts of the decoders have to ship** (`docs/licensing.md`, section on the WebAssembly decoders): `Dockerfile.worker` copies the six `LICENSE_*` files of the `wasm` folder into `/licenses/pdfjs-dist-wasm/`, because `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` embeds only the licence files at the root of a package (section 6.2).
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **`useWasm: false`**: the same pictures, 1.1 to 2.7 times the time (above).
  - **A `wasmUrl` for picture jobs only**: the decoder keeps its bytes for the whole thread (above), so the saving would depend on the order of the jobs.
  - **Decoding the three formats outside pdf.js** (OpenJPEG and a fax decoder from the worker image): a second colour path that differs from pdf.js's for the same picture, and the pictures of a page come from its operator list already.
  - **Leaving the pictures out and recording a warning**: the pictures are the content of the document (entry 81).
  - **Refusing the job (413) for a picture past a limit, as `pdf-jbig2-guard.ts` does for Poppler**: one oversized picture would cost the text and every other picture, where PDFium and pdf.js leave out only that picture. Inline pictures, which cannot be left out, are refused.
  - **Deleting the `*_nowasm_fallback.js` files from the worker image to close the JavaScript fallback**: the tests and a development run read the package's own folder, and a new pdfjs-dist would bring the files back; the `wasmUrl` below the folder depends on neither.
  - **Lowering the maximum in the worker image (`Dockerfile.worker`) with a pinned digest**: the tests and a development run would read the unpatched files, and a new pdfjs-dist would need a new digest; the factory reads the module's sections and fails closed when it cannot lower the maximum.
  - **A count of 256 decoded pictures a page**: pages of real documents decode up to 446 (`govdocs1-003690.pdf`), whose pictures past the 256th are not recorded but would be refused.
  - **A document budget of decode time from pixels**: the decoders' speed depends on the content by three orders of magnitude (a white CCITT row of 65,535 columns decodes at 38,000 pixels a millisecond, the CCITT scans of `govdocs1-002608.pdf` at 186 and a JBIG2 scan at 25 with the rest of the conversion), so a budget either refuses documents that finish or does not bound the slow ones; the 60 s deadline stays the bound on time.
- **Measured**: text, Markdown and HTML of the 1,261 real-world PDFs and of every tenth PDF of the regression corpus by id (950), origin/main (`d6605e4c`) against the change, 6,633 conversions each, three processes per side; Word of the 251 of those files that have such a picture.
  - **Text**: 2,211 conversions, one differs: `cc-2800979.pdf`, a scan without fonts whose OCR text differs with the load of the machine (1,984 and 1,986 bytes in the loaded run; 1,982 bytes in all three runs of each side when run alone, Markdown included).
  - **Markdown and HTML**: 238 files change, and no output changes otherwise (the OCR file above is the 239th). Pictures in the Markdown: 96,639 to 108,509 (11,870 more); the same 12 refusals before and after.
  - **Word**: 250 of 251 documents change, drawings 14,020 to 17,819 and media files 12,554 to 15,963; the 251st (`govdocs1-000282.pdf`) is refused by the 5,000-picture limit of the Word writer before and after.
  - **Oracle** (`pdfimages -list`, 120 files with a CCITT, JBIG2 or JPEG 2000 image row): the Markdown holds those pictures at those sizes in 104. The 16 others: 12 files have no text layer (`pdftotext` finds no character), their Markdown is the same bytes as their text and holds no picture before and after (the pages are recognized, as for the scans of entry 98); `govdocs1-001659.pdf` holds all 19 pictures, but 11 of them are JPEG 2000 pictures under a larger CCITT /Mask and the reader writes them at the size of the mask (`182x78` for the listed `121x52`); `govdocs1-004121.pdf`, `govdocs1-003071.pdf` and `govdocs1-004389.pdf` have pages with 642, 2,505 and 3,150 image rows and stop at the 256 pictures a page.
  - **Times of the corpus runs are not compared**: both sides ran with other work on the machine (load average 7 to 10).
  - **Decoder memory and the check (review of #887)**: the Markdown and Word outputs of the 251 files with such a picture, before the check (`9b0801c9`) and after it, hold the same pictures: 23,688 in the Markdown, every Markdown file the same bytes, 17,819 drawings and 15,963 media files in the Word files, and the same one refusal; the check leaves out no picture of them. Over the 1,261 real-world PDFs the largest estimate is 34.2 MiB (`govdocs1-001307.pdf`, which took 43 MiB of module memory), the longest walk 69 million pixels (`govdocs1-003399.pdf`), the most decoded pictures 496 a document and 446 a page, and no JBIG2 picture has more region pixels than its page. Read in the reader's thread (Mac, Node 24), each hostile picture of the tests is left out with no resident growth to speak of (0 to 1 MiB after a warm-up job), where without the check a 4096 x 4096 RGB JPEG 2000 behind FlateDecode grew the process by 197 MiB and was decoded, and stacked JBIG2 regions grew it by 174 MiB before the abort; a JPEG 2000 of 8000 x 8000 behind LZW, which the check cannot read, ends at the maximum with a null picture and 52 MiB of growth, and without the maximum it was decoded in 1.4 s with 963 MiB of growth. After the fixes of the second review round the 251 files give the same result again: 23,688 pictures in the Markdown, every file the same bytes as before the round (`db2f2a45`), no error, and no document given more than the budget.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdf-picture-decoders.test.ts` (the decoding and the text-job tests were red before the change: a CCITT Group 4, a JBIG2 and a JPEG 2000 picture made by other tools, read as the pixels they code and written into Markdown through the text thread; a text job decodes none of them; hostile pictures, each within 15 s and 512 MiB of resident set: a JBIG2 page declaring 100,000 x 100,000 pixels, a CCITT picture of a billion columns, a JPEG 2000 size marker of 60,000 x 60,000, a 12,000 x 12,000 picture in 1,178 bytes decoded within the pixel limit, 600 distinct JPEG 2000 pictures on one page kept to 256; the 4 pictures of `govdocs1-000142.pdf` and the 70 of `govdocs1-003685.pdf` at the sizes `pdfimages` lists), `tests/third-party-notices.test.ts` (the licence texts are copied into `/licenses`), `tests/pdf-picture-decoders-limits.test.ts` (all in the reader's thread with the resident memory of the process sampled: a module lowered to 256 MiB grows to it and no further, and a module without a memory maximum, or with one that cannot hold the new one, is refused; a 4-component 2048 x 2048 and a 3-component 3584 x 3584 JPEG 2000 behind FlateDecode decoded at full size, an 8000 x 8000 decoded at the 2000 x 2000 pdf.js reduces it to; left out within 96 MiB of growth: a 3-component 4096 x 4096 JPEG 2000 behind FlateDecode, a JP2 whose decoy size marker would have it decoded at 8000 x 8000, a JBIG2 generic region of 65,535 x 65,535 on a 64 x 32 page, eight intermediate JBIG2 regions of 16,384 x 16,384, a CCITT picture of 8 x 65,535 decoded at 65,535 columns; an inline CCITT picture of that size refused and a small one read; 32,769 CCITT pictures on a page refused before decoding; 100 pictures that share a JBIG2Globals stream of 1 MiB converted, which reading it once per picture would refuse; 65 JPEG 2000 streams of 1 MiB stored without a wrapper converted, which charging them to the 64 MiB wrapper budget would refuse; under the maximum, within 416 MiB of growth: an 8000 x 8000 JPEG 2000 behind LZW and three JBIG2 pictures whose regions stack past it give null pictures and the picture after them is decoded, and 4 threads of the pool doing so at once. Each test of the check fails with the check taken out by hand, each test of the maximum with the maximum taken out, the shared-globals test with the globals read again for each picture, and the 65 MiB test with stored bytes charged), `tests/pdf-picture-guard.test.ts` (red before the review fixes except the `CCF` spelling, which was already read: /F, /DP and /H before /Filter, /DecodeParms and /Height, `JPX` decoded at full size where `JPXDecode` is reduced, an indirect /Subtype, an /SMask with a codec filter and no /Subtype, the file header of a JBIG2 stream and of its JBIG2Globals with and without a page count, a content stream whose filter is written /F inflated within the byte budgets, 16,384 against 16,385 components and 32 against 33 levels, a COC marker that runs out of bytes neither throwing nor refusing the document for an object or an inline picture, 200,000 objects named in one update, 1,000 pictures that share 8 MiB of zero bytes as JBIG2Globals, 4,000 inline images with an array that is never closed, and 100 pictures whose /Length runs to the end of a 16 MiB stream, of which the first three are read), `tests/pdf-picture-header-errors.test.ts` (a header reader made to throw a RangeError: the image object is left out, an inline picture is not refused, another error is not hidden), `tests/pdf-wasm-fallback.test.ts` (the pinned pdfjs-dist version, both modules taking the maximum, no fallback file below the `wasmUrl` while the folder has them, and a module that cannot take the maximum giving a null picture where the same folder given to pdf.js as `wasmUrl` decodes it in the JavaScript fallback), the corpus comparisons above, and the Linux VM timings above.
- **Revisit when**: pdf.js stops keeping the fetched decoder bytes, or changes the size limits of its decoders, its reduction of JPEG 2000 pictures or how it reads their size; pdf.js.jbig2 or pdf.js.openjpeg change the codecs they build (the estimates follow PDFium bb1f9f71 and OpenJPEG 8314119b); a real picture needs more than the 192 MiB check or the 256 MiB maximum; a real document reaches the 60 s deadline or the 128 MiB of picture bytes only because of these pictures; pdfjs-dist is upgraded (`tests/pdf-wasm-fallback.test.ts` pins 6.3.289), or pdf.js gives a way to turn the JavaScript fallback off or reads `wasmUrl` for something else in Node; the scan follows the cross-reference as pdf.js does (the #783 row); or the worker image gets a decoder that is faster than the pdf.js modules.

## 102. IGES: the Global and Terminate sections are checked before the kernel reads a file, a mesh is written to IGES by the kernel, and OBJ carries the colours in an MTL file

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783, the four rows "Follow-ups from #792 (STEP and IGES)"; epic #760), decided 2026-10-25 (QA request in issue #783). It changes three statements of entry 43 (the Hollerith follow-up, "OBJ carries no materials" and "no mesh to IGES through the kernel"); entry 43 points here.
- **Decision**:
