It never deletes an upload, a result that a queued or running job reads as its input, an undelivered result younger than ten minutes, or an undelivered result of which some bytes were sent within the undelivered time (its client may resume the download). A pass is judged as a whole, not one deletion at a time: a result can free less than one step of the measurement, and writes that arrive between two measurements hide the drop of any single deletion. It stops when 20 results are gone and the use is still not lower than when the pass began (the disk is then full of something deleting results cannot free: uploads, a spool, files still open), or when three deletions failed in a row (the store is down or refusing). A result whose object is already gone, or that a job claimed in the meantime, is skipped and counts for nothing, and a result whose deletion failed is left alone until its retry time. A pass that deleted nothing (no result may go, or every deletion failed) or that did not lower the use is remembered, and early deletion waits five minutes unless the use moved by a percentage point or more, so a disk that stays full costs at most 20 results per five minutes in a process, and requests do not read every record again and again. Only the disk of the storage directory drives the deletion: the temporary directory of a worker is its own file system, and a large conversion that fills it is not freed by deleting results. Each deleted result answers its owner 410 with `reason: "capacity"` and is logged as a warning. Above `RESULT_DISK_REFUSE_PERCENT` (default 95) a new upload or conversion runs the early deletion first and answers 503 with `Retry-After: 60` only if the disk is still above it, the fuller of the storage directory's file system and the temporary directory's (a file system that holds both is measured once), which is the only place the temporary directory counts; the check comes before authentication, so a refused request uses no quota. Only starting something takes new space, so the parts, the completion and the abort of an upload already running go on (the abort frees space). The answer, with the deletion it may run, is measured at most once every five seconds in a process, and a disk that cannot be measured, or an early deletion that cannot run at all because the records cannot be read, lets the request in. A measured full disk refuses when deleting results did not bring it under the limit, also when every single deletion failed. The three must rise strictly and the highest is at most 99. Object-store drivers (`s3`, `oci`) have no fixed size, so none of this applies to them.
  - **A result chained as a job input is kept for the job.** Submitting a job whose input is an earlier result of the user refuses a result the rule already deleted (404, as for a missing object). Just before the job is queued, the result is held for that job; a result deleted in between is refused the same way, and a job that cannot be queued gives the hold up again. The hold ends when the job completes, fails for the last time or is cancelled (for a graph, when the graph ends), and after a day at the latest when that end is never reported. Up to 32 jobs hold one result at once. While any hold lasts, neither the sweep nor an early deletion removes the result.
  - **Every result is downloaded through the application.** The `downloadUrl` of a job result is always `/api/storage/file/<key>`, also on `s3` and `oci`; a direct link to the bucket is not issued, because the application could not see that it was used. `POST /api/storage/multipart?action=presign` with `type: "download"` refuses a job result and a conversion result that has a record (400), and refuses while the ledger cannot be read. On `s3` and `oci` the body is streamed from the bucket under the 60-second inactivity timeout only; the 15-minute ceiling of a storage request ends when the headers arrive, so a slow client can take a large result.
  - **An anonymous result answers 410 to anyone who holds its link.** A result without an owner is reachable by its key alone, which is a capability URL; after deletion the same holders get 410 for a day instead of 404. Nobody without the link learns anything.
  - **The job record reports it.** `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` has `retention` with `state` (`available` or `deleted`), `deleteAt` (the deletion time of the result itself; a job that still reads it postpones the deletion until it ends), `deliveredAt` and `reason` (`delivered`, `expired` or `capacity`). The account file list leaves out a deleted file and counts an available one down to its deletion time.
  - **A bucket lifecycle rule is only a backstop.** Rules expire whole days at best and run asynchronously, so they cannot enforce minutes; set one at one day on `results/`, `conversions/`, `uploads/` and `intermediate/` and incomplete multipart uploads, so an object the sweep missed is gone within a day.
  - **No retention or storage header on an answer (2026-11-02).** `/api/convert` and `/api/convert/batch` no longer send `X-Zero-Data-Retention: true` or `X-Storage-Footprint: 0-bytes`, and the browser's fallback path no longer sends `X-Zero-Retention: true` with its request, which no route read. The two inline routes return the result in the body of the answer and store nothing, so this rule does not apply to them; the headers were dropped because comparable services send no retention claim with each answer: the reference converter's documentation states how long its exported files stay available, and an object store sends the expiry of a stored object with that object. Retention is stated in the API documentation and in the `expiresAt` of the v1 conversion answers, and in the interface copy as the rule above (entry 139, UI copy). `tests/zero-retention.test.ts` and `tests/api.test.ts` assert that the headers are absent, and `tests/copy-claims.test.ts` fails when a file under `src` names one of the three headers again.
- **Why**:
  - **Comparable conversion services keep a file for a bounded time, and none documents deleting on delivery by itself.** Read on 2026-10-30 from their own documentation, without the names: a PDF tool states that "all files processed within our platform are automatically and permanently deleted within two hours of being processed" and offers deletion from the download screen; a second PDF tool's help center gives about one hour after processing (read through a search summary of the page); a conversion API stores a result for up to 3 hours only when asked to and streams it back otherwise; a second conversion API deletes automatically after 24 hours at the latest and lets the user delete earlier; a document-services API keeps an uploaded asset transiently for 24 hours with an explicit delete call and a one-hour download link; a third conversion API lets the user choose to "delete the file instantly after you downloaded it". The undelivered time of one hour is the shortest of the common windows (one to three hours; the day-long ones are the outer bound), and a delivered result goes much sooner than any of them.
  - **Why a grace period and not deletion at the last byte.** A client may ask again after a complete delivery: a second click, a download manager that checks the size and fetches the tail again, a browser that retries after a failed save. RFC 9110 section 14 lets a client re-request any range, and a response is only known to have been taken when the connection ended well, which the server cannot see from its side of the socket buffer. Ten minutes is long enough for those and short enough that nothing is kept for the user's later convenience; it is a decision, not a figure the services above state, and the policy is one environment variable. The cost of a too-short value is a 410 for a retry; of a too-long one, minutes of storage.
  - **Why the first complete delivery and not the first request.** A request that stops early (a dropped connection, a closed tab) must not take the result away; the user would have to convert again and be charged again. Only the full body, or ranges that add up to it, counts.
  - **Why the application serves every download.** The scale-out drivers could hand out a presigned link, which saves the application the traffic, but then the bucket answers the client and nothing records the delivery; the object would stay until a lifecycle rule removed it, a day at the earliest.
  - **A bucket cannot enforce this alone.** Lifecycle expiration is in whole days and the object is removed asynchronously after it is eligible (S3 "Expiring objects": "There may be a delay between the expiration date and the date at which Amazon S3 removes an object"; OCI Object Lifecycle Management: "You specify the number of days", runs once a day).
  - **The disk thresholds are the ones open-source infrastructure uses for the same job.** The kubelet deletes unused container images when disk use passes `imageGCHighThresholdPercent` (default 85) and stops at `imageGCLowThresholdPercent` (default 80), oldest first (Kubernetes documentation, "Garbage collection of unused containers and images", and the kubelet configuration reference; OKD documents the same pair). Elasticsearch blocks writes to every index on a node past its flood-stage disk watermark, `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.flood_stage`, default 95% ("Disk-based shard allocation settings"). The same two-threshold hysteresis stops the deletion from running on every sweep at the edge, and the refusal is the flood stage.
  - **Why the guards on early deletion.** Ten minutes of age covers the usual path of a client that polls its job and downloads the result within seconds to minutes of its end; a disk that fills faster than that fills from uploads and spools, which deleting fresh results would not free. A pass that deleted twenty results and did not lower the use tells that case apart from a deletion whose effect `statfs` shows a moment later, and judging the pass instead of each deletion keeps tiny results and concurrent writes from stopping a deletion that works. Five seconds between measurements bounds the cost of a burst of refused requests to one `statfs` and one read of the records per process, while a disk that was freed lets requests in again within five seconds.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Traffic.** Results on `s3` and `oci` pass through the web process instead of coming straight from the bucket. A large result occupies a web connection for the length of the download.
  - **A retry after the grace period converts again.** The user pays a second conversion for a file they downloaded twenty minutes ago; the 410 says why.
  - **Records are one small file or one Redis key per result.** The file ledger is read once per sweep (a minute apart), at most 32 files at a time, and the same pass removes temporary files and locks older than an hour that a stopped process left; that is fine for the single host of the launch and is why a larger deployment uses Redis. An early deletion reads every live record, because its order is not the order of either store; it runs only above the high threshold, at most once per sweep and once per five seconds of refused requests.
  - **Early deletion takes results a user may still want.** A delivered result in its grace period goes first because its user already has it; an undelivered one goes only after all of those, so the user must convert again. Refusing new work at 95% keeps the disk from filling while the deletion catches up; the alternative, a write failing half-way, loses the work anyway.
  - **The raw body of a synchronous conversion (`?raw=true`) and its `dataUri` are not deliveries.** The response itself carried the file; the stored copy that `downloadUrl` names still waits for the undelivered time unless it is downloaded.
  - **A result larger than 64 MiB made by a worker of the local driver** keeps its file in that worker's scratch directory; another process's sweep removes the stored record but not that file, which the worker's own time-to-live sweep removes at the undelivered time.
  - **Uploads that no job ever used** keep their own lifetime (up to a day) until a separate change shortens it; this entry deletes an input after the last job that reads it ends. More than 32 jobs holding one upload at once are refused like a missing input (the cap of a chained result), and an upload is kept for the grace period after its last job, not removed at that instant, because a client may ask for one more format right after the last answer.
  - **Intermediate artifacts of a graph** are removed when the graph ends and, if the worker dies first, after a day.
  - **A deleted upload's record is forgotten, not kept for a day.** Nobody asks for an upload after it is gone, so there is no 410 to answer. The cost is a narrow race: a job that is authorized before the sweep deletes the upload and held after it finds no record and no object, is queued, and fails on the missing input like any other missing file; its hold and the record then end by themselves.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Delete at the last byte.** A retry or a resumed download after an unobserved socket failure would find nothing.
  - **Delete after N downloads.** A normal user downloads once, so N adds storage time for nobody; an unfinished download would count as one.
  - **Mark the object itself** (the expiry in the object's own metadata). An object store cannot change metadata in place, so a copy of every result per delivery would be needed, and nothing would sweep the objects.
  - **Presigned download links on the object-store drivers.** They cannot be observed.
  - **A lifecycle rule alone.** Whole days, asynchronous.
- **Verified by**: `tests/result-retention.test.ts` (the policy and its refusal of a malformed value; the merging of sent ranges and its cap; a second click served inside the grace period and 410 after it, also before the sweep ran and when deleting then fails; 410 to the owner and 404 to anyone else after a sweep; a cancelled read, a client gone while the next chunk was pending, and a tail range not counted; a cancelled download plus the resumed rest counted; two ranges counted; `X-Accel-Buffering: no`; a result removed again when its record cannot be written, in the sync route helper and in the worker; downloads, the job record and the account list served while the ledger cannot be read, and uploads never reading it; an undelivered result deleted after an hour; a result due while the server was down cleaned by the next sweep; an upload left alone; the job record and the account list; parallel range records from two processes kept; a failing delete moved behind the others and a record reopened again when the ledger failed during the reopening; a missing object of a delivered result or an upload logged with its key and an expired result's not; the record of a deleted upload forgotten and a deleted result's kept; the deletion time of the result itself reported while a job holds it; a deletion that never finishes given up so that the sweep goes on; the object of a held result, and of an upload read near the end of its day, kept by the storage past its stored lifetime, also in a process that saved it when another process extended it on the shared disk; a slow sweep logged once with no second sweep started beside it; old temporary files removed; a writer whose stale lock was broken leaving the next writer's lock alone; every live record listed; a chained input held by two jobs past the undelivered time until both released it, refused once deleted, and its hold ended after a day without a release; the ledger of a test file put back after a test replaced it; a Redis outage failing 50 parallel calls after one shared wait and the next ones at once, with no listener warning), `tests/result-capacity.test.ts` (the thresholds and their refusal at start-up; the fuller of the storage and temporary directories for admission, measured once when they share a disk; the order of early deletion and its stop at 80%; an upload never deleted for space; a held input untouched, also when the job takes it while the deletion runs; a half-downloaded result kept so its resume answers 206; undelivered results younger than ten minutes kept; the stop after twenty deletions that together did not lower the use and the pause after it, over repeated calls and over ten minutes of requests; a pass judged by the whole drop when each result frees less than a step of the measurement or writes arrive between the measurements; the pause after a pass with nothing to delete and after a pass whose deletions all failed (three attempts, not one per request); a result waiting for its retry left alone; a result whose object is already gone skipped; a measurement that never answers letting new files in; a full temporary directory deleting no result while still refusing new files; 410 with `capacity`; 503 with `Retry-After` at 95% and admission after the deletion freed space; admission when `statfs` fails or the records cannot be read; one measurement and one read of the records per five seconds for a burst of requests; tus parts, completion and abort going on at 97% while a new upload is refused), `tests/s3-object-client.test.ts` (a download body read for longer than the request ceiling, and a stalled body still timed out), `tests/storage-presign-download-access.test.ts` (no signed link for a job result or a tracked conversion result), `tests/result-retention-remote.test.ts` (an object removed from an S3-compatible bucket, against a stub server that verifies signatures), `tests/result-retention-redis.test.ts` (the same through Redis, parallel range records from two connections, a due key without a record dropped, a failing delete moved behind, 32 updates from four connections racing on one record all kept, and an upload held by two jobs and deleted one grace period after the last, a chained result kept past its time while held, and the start-up sweep through the connection the environment selects, part of `npm run test:redis`), `tests/job-input-key-authorization.test.ts` (every `import.upload` node of a graph authorized before any is held, so another user's output is neither held nor converted through a second node; a key that only begins with "inline" authorized like any stored key), `tests/job-input-deletion.test.ts` (an upload converted by three jobs, one after the other and two at the same time, kept until the last ends and deleted after the grace period; an input kept while a retry is pending and deleted after the last attempt, deleted on cancel, kept for a chained output of the user, kept for a graph or a job that never held it or that could not be queued, and deleted when a graph completes, fails or is cancelled; the grace period starting again at each job's end and capped at a day after the first read, and a hold on an upload ending a day after it was first read; a chained result held while its job is queued and released when it is cancelled, the hold given up when the job cannot be queued, and an input deleted before queueing refused), `tests/idempotency-concurrency.test.ts` (ten requests with one key starting together still give exactly one job and nine 409s with the disk measurement stubbed), and a real run of the stack through the HTTP API with the times shortened (upload, convert, download, wait, 410), evidence in the pull request.
- **Revisit when**: the disk of a launch host reaches the high threshold in normal traffic (size the disk, not the thresholds), a deployment uses a bucket for results at scale (move the download to a signed redirect only if the delivery can be reported back, and make a hold raise the expiry of the object in the bucket), the grace period causes support requests, an object store offers lifecycle rules shorter than a day, uploads that no job used are shortened, or the privacy text is reviewed (issue #665).

## 126. A legacy workbook is always handed to the office suite, which decrypts the default password; an encrypted workbook or Word document the suite cannot load is named as encrypted

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783, rows of the real-world run of 2026-10-30: 155 jobs over 65 Office files refused as damaged), decided 2026-10-31 (QA request: convert what the reference converts; an XLS with the default open password converts).
- **Decision**:
  - **An Excel 97-2003 workbook with a FilePass record goes to LibreOffice like any other workbook.** LibreOffice tries the default password `VelvetSweatshop` first and decrypts a workbook that uses it, for the RC4 form (Apache POI's `50833.xls` and a fuzzer file of the corpus) and for the XOR form (`60284.xls`). Before, the worker looked for the record before it started the suite and answered 422 for every workbook that had one, so the three corpus files that Excel itself opens without asking were refused. The check is gone; the worker holds no decryption code of its own.
  - **A text target of such a workbook (CSV, TSV, JSON, HTML, Markdown) is read from the suite's XLSX.** The in-process reader still stops at the FilePass record (it never decrypts); its 422 now sends the file through the suite's XLSX (`retryRefusedLegacyDocument`, the route a malformed legacy file already takes), and the reader of the XLSX writes the target. When the suite cannot load the file, the reader's 422 stands.
  - **A workbook or Word document that the suite could not load is answered 422 when it is encrypted** (`withLegacyOfficeRecovery`, around every LibreOffice run). The suite reports a file that needs another password like a damaged one ("source file could not be loaded"); the worker then looks for the FilePass record of the workbook, or the fEncrypted flag of the file information block of the Word document ([MS-DOC] 2.5.2), and names the file encrypted, as it did for a PowerPoint. The two Word files of the corpus that needed a password (`password_password_cryptoapi.doc`, `password_tika_binaryrc4.doc`) were answered 400 "damaged"; they are 422 now. A real password is still 422 and still not accepted: the API has no password option for Office files.
  - **Files that LibreOffice cannot read stay refused as damaged (400).** The 65 refused files were run through the suite of the worker image (LibreOffice 25.2.3.2, no network, input read-only), `pdf` and the application's own format each: none of the 65 converts. The package repair of LibreOffice (`ZipPackage` `m_bForceRecovery`, set from the `RepairPackage` media property or the `?repairpackage` URL parameter; `SfxMedium::IsRepairPackage` reads `SID_REPAIRPACKAGE`) is switched on by the user's answer in the interactive dialog, which `soffice --headless --convert-to` never gives, so no ZIP is repaired there and the worker does not repair one either.
- **Why**:
  - **References.** LibreOffice 25.2 `sc/source/filter/excel/xlroot.cxx` `XclRoot::RequestEncryptionData` (lines 253 to 257) passes `XclRootData::gaDefPassword` (`sc/source/filter/inc/xlroot.hxx` line 85, `VelvetSweatshop`) as the first default password to `ScfApiHelper::QueryEncryptionDataForMedium`, and `comphelper/source/misc/docpasswordhelper.cxx` `DocPasswordHelper::requestAndVerifyDocPassword` (lines 554 to 575) verifies the defaults before it asks anyone. `sc/source/filter/excel/xicontent.cxx` `XclImpDecryptHelper::ReadFilepass` (line 1249) and `lclReadFilepass5`, `lclReadFilepass8` (lines 1112 to 1245) read the XOR, RC4 and CryptoAPI forms. Apache POI `Biff8EncryptionKey` and `Biff8DecryptingStream` use the same default password (behaviour only, no code copied).
  - **Measured, which of the two ways has the smaller trusted surface.** The worker image's LibreOffice converted `50833.xls` and the fuzzer file `poihssffuzzer-4651309315719168.xls` (RC4 1.1 whose verifier decrypts under `VelvetSweatshop`, checked with a separate script) and `60284.xls` (a BIFF5 XOR FilePass) to PDF and ODS, and refused `password.xls`, `51832.xls` (RC4 with another password), `xor-encryption-abc.xls` (XOR, `abc`) and `35897-type4.xls` (CryptoAPI). Following POI would add RC4, MD5 key derivation, the XOR obfuscation and CryptoAPI to the worker (a verifier of the password, then a decryption of every record of the workbook, then handing the plain workbook to the suite); letting the suite decrypt adds none, and the suite already parses the decrypted bytes. The cost is one suite start for a workbook with a real password before its 422, which the sandbox and the job time limit already bound.
  - **The encrypted answer follows the failure, because the failure alone is ambiguous.** An intact encrypted file and a damaged one give the suite the same message, so the answer asks the file after the suite failed, in the one place that wraps every suite run (the page chain, the interchange routes and the direct write all go through it), as the presentation retry already does for PowerPoint.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A workbook with a real password costs one suite start before the 422.** The earlier check refused it with no process started.
  - **A damaged workbook that has a FilePass record, which the suite cannot load, is named encrypted.** The record is the sign Excel writes only for a protected workbook; the old check made the same call.
  - **A file larger than the in-memory limit is not judged** and keeps the suite's "damaged" answer, as before for the old check.
  - **The suite decrypts a file with the default password and the worker converts it.** Nothing a user protected with a password of their own is opened: the default is the one password everyone knows, which is why the reference opens such a file without asking.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Decrypting in the worker (POI's RC4 and XOR, CryptoAPI).** A second cryptographic implementation in the trusted base for a result the suite already gives.
  - **Verifying the default password in the worker and starting the suite only then.** The same code as decrypting, without the saving that mattered (the suite start).
  - **Repairing broken ZIPs in the worker, or running the suite through its API with `RepairPackage`.** None of the 65 files is read by the suite of the image in its normal mode; a repair mode is a change of the reference behaviour that no corpus file asks for, and the image has no Python UNO binding to call it with.
  - **Passing the files of the fuzzers on.** Those that the suite of the image cannot read are refused by it with the message the user can act on.
- **Verified by**: `tests/legacy-office-encrypted-answer.test.ts` (the FilePass and fEncrypted readers on crafted compound files and bare streams; the wrapper on a stand-in suite: the file passes to the suite, the 422 follows the suite's failure only for an encrypted file, other failures keep their error; the real files `50833.xls`, `60284.xls` and the fuzzer file convert to every route and carry the cell text; `password.xls`, `xor-encryption-abc.xls`, `51832.xls`, and the two Word files are 422; a truncated `.docx` and a compound file of random bytes stay refused as damaged), `tests/xls-biff8-corpus-regressions.test.ts` (the synthetic FilePass bodies still answer 422 for every target), and a run of the 155 refused jobs before and after (table in the pull request).
- **Revisit when**: the worker image moves to a LibreOffice that reads more of the fuzzer files (26.8 on a laptop converts nine of the legacy fuzzer files that 25.2.3.2 refuses; re-run the 65 files), the API gets a password option for Office files (then the suite is given it, as for a PDF), or a corpus file that LibreOffice reads is refused again.

## 128. Rows of the nightly run of 2026-10-31: five media names list the container their real files are, a PDF with no page tree is refused by that name, and five corpus files that hold no content are marked

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783, rows of the real-world run 41163999218 on main 79d2e3b0: 37 jobs that the run of 2026-10-30 did not list), decided 2026-10-31 (QA request: fix the real regressions at their root).
- **Decision**:
  - **Five media names list the container the real files under them are** (`MEDIA_INPUT_DEMUXERS` in `src/lib/conversions/media-process.ts`, entry 119): `.asf` adds `argo_asf`, `.caf` adds `aiff`, `.mpc` adds `ea`, `.divx` and `.xvid` add `lmlm4`, and `.mpg` and `.mpeg` add `mpegts`. Twelve jobs on five files of the FFmpeg test suite and samples were refused ("ffprobe could not inspect the input media"): Argonaut Games ASF (`ASF\0` header), an AIFF file (`FORM` and `AIFF`) named `.caf`, an Electronic Arts file (`MPCh` tag) named `.mpc`, an LMLM4 stream named `.divx` and an MPEG transport stream named `.mpg`. Entry 119 forces the demuxers of the declared format, and FFmpeg checks the whitelist after its probe has chosen (`avformat_open_input`, demux.c line 286: "Format not on whitelist"), so a file of another container than its name has to find that container in its format's list. With the list of a name that also gives the container, FFmpeg's probe picks it as before the change, from the bytes. Each demuxer reads one local file and opens no other (argo_asf.c, aiffdec.c, electronicarts.c, lmlm4.c and mpegts.c of FFmpeg 9.0.2, the release of the worker image); none is a reference format (`REFERENCE_INPUT_FORMATS`), so a concat list, a playlist or a manifest under any of these names is refused as before.
  - **A catalog whose `/Pages` entry is not a page tree is refused by that name** (`readPdfPageFrames`, `src/lib/conversions/pdf-page-geometry.ts`): "Invalid PDF: the /Pages entry of the catalog is not a page tree." The message was the parser's own TypeError, "the page tree could not be read (_this.catalog.Pages(...).traverse is not a function)": pdf-lib gives a page tree only to a dictionary typed `/Type /Pages`, and `pdfjs-issue15590.pdf` has the dictionary of a JavaScript action there. The error class (`PdfPageFrameError`, a typed 400) is the same; the check is made before the tree is walked.
  - **Five corpus files that hold no content carry `emptyInput`** (`bench/realworld/manifest.json`), each with the reason read from the file by a tool other than the converter: `govdocs1-000058.html` (a table around an image reference and an empty paragraph, 734 bytes), `govdocs1-001421.html` (a frameset of three frames, 453 bytes), `govdocs1-001721.html` (scripts, style sheet links and a frameset, 3,658 bytes), `govdocs1-002028.html` (a meta refresh over an empty body, 224 bytes) and `office-spreadsheet-bug64512_embed.xlsx` (an empty `sheetData`, two embedded objects with no text). The e-book of an HTML page keeps its title in the metadata, so the OEB archive of these four has content documents with no text; the output check (`oebArchiveProblem`) read that as a bad output. The gate rule does not change (entry 71): a zero-byte or textless output is accepted only for an input the corpus marks.
  - **Five rows leave `bench/parity-gaps.json`**, the ones the gate named as "now at parity" in nightly run 41163999218: `image/screenshot.png->avif/throughput`, `image/lineart.png->avif/throughput`, `image/wm-deep-dart.png->avif/throughput`, `video/clip.mp4->vp9/throughput` and `ocr/scan.png->pdf/throughput`.
- **Refusals that stand** (each checked with a reader other than the converter, on the same files):
  - **The seven PDF to XLS and XLSX refusals are the refusals of PDF to DOCX**, measured file by file (the table is in the pull request); a sheet needs the same text layer and reads the same pages. `pdfjs-issue15590.pdf` has no page tree (`qpdf --check`: "root of pages tree has no /Kids array", Poppler: "Page count in top-level pages object is wrong type"). `pdf-qpdf-deep-pages.pdf` is a page tree that loops (qpdf: "Loop detected in /Pages structure", Poppler: "Loop in Pages tree"). `qpdf-issue-146.pdf` and `qpdf-issue-99.pdf` are damaged (qpdf: "ignoring excessively deeply nested data structure" and "recovered trailer has no /Root entry"). `pdfjs-empty_protected.pdf` and `qpdf-encrypted-with-images.pdf` open with the empty password (`qpdf --check` prints an empty user password, Poppler lists their pages, and the converter renders them to PNG), `pdf-pdfjs-issue17333.pdf` is not encrypted, and the three hold no text: `pdftotext` prints nothing, and the pages of the second hold two logo pictures with no letters. The sheet and the document writers answer "PDF has no text layer and OCR recognised no text on any page" for them, and the text writer an empty file.
  - **The XLS to ODS and PDF timeouts at 45 s are not ours.** Measured here, `office-spreadsheet-florida_data.ashx.xls` converts in 3.1 s to ODS and 2.7 s to PDF, and `govdocs1-001700.xls` in 2.5 s to ODS (LibreOffice 26.8, the dispatcher of the worker), and the worker image's LibreOffice 25.2.3 converts the same files in 0.8 to 3.1 s (`soffice --convert-to`). The CI runner has LibreOffice 24.2.7 (the Ubuntu 24.04 package) and runs three jobs at once on 4 vCPUs; the same two files took 40.7 s and 39.5 s there on 2026-10-30 and timed out on 2026-10-31, with seven XLS jobs over 40 s on both nights and an unchanged distribution over the 1,226 XLS jobs of each (median 1,363 and 1,340 ms, p90 3,726 and 3,702 ms). The rows stay as measurements of the runner; no conversion code of ours runs for that long.
  - Unchanged: the DjVu "binary null bytes" refusals (no reader yet), the EOT file compressed with MicroType Express, `office-spreadsheet-58896.xlsx` to XLS (257 columns, the format's 256), and the OCR page budget on `govdocs1-002014.pdf` (runner load).
- **Why**:
  - **References.** FFmpeg 9.0.2 `libavformat`: `argo_asf.c` `argo_asf_probe`, `aiffdec.c` `aiff_probe`, `electronicarts.c` `ea_probe`, `lmlm4.c` `lmlm4_probe`, `mpegts.c`, and `allformats.c` for the names (`ffmpeg -demuxers` of the worker image lists `argo_asf`, `aiff`, `ea`, `lmlm4` and `mpegts`); `ffprobe` with no demuxer given names the container of each file (`argo_asf`, `aiff`, `ea`, `lmlm4`, `mpegts`). pdf-lib 1.17.1 `PDFObjectParser.parseDict` for the type that makes a page tree. qpdf 12.2.0 and Poppler for the PDF refusals, and the FFmpeg and Poppler outputs above for each file.
  - **The cause was found by sweeping the corpus, not by the five files.** All 224 media files of the corpus that are not GIF (the corpus holds 374 files of media formats, 150 of them GIF) were opened with the exact options of `mediaInputArgs` on the worker image's `ffprobe` 9.0.2: before the change 7 of the first 197 did not open, and after it 2 of the 224 do not (`tika-testac3.ac3` and `tika-test2.swf`, which FFmpeg's own probe with no demuxer given does not open either, so they are damaged files and not a regression).
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A file of any other container under a name keeps failing to open** (entry 119): an `.mp4` that is an AVI file is read as the signature shows, but a `.wma` that is an Argonaut file is not. The five lists name the containers real files were found to be; a new one is added with the file that shows it.
  - **A catalog whose page tree lacks `/Type /Pages` is refused too**, as pdf-lib sees it, though Poppler and pdf.js infer the type from `/Kids`. The file this refusal was seen on has no `/Kids` at all, and ISO 32000-1 table 29 requires `/Type /Pages` of a page tree node.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Every demuxer in every list**: rejected in entry 119 and still so; the probe would choose among all of them by the bytes.
  - **Probing with FFmpeg and no whitelist when the forced demuxer fails**: it reopens the file with the guess that entry 119 removed, and the guess is what could read a crafted file.
  - **Repairing a page tree without `/Type` before pdf-lib reads it**: the specification requires the type, and the repair would be a parser of ours for a shape it does not allow.
  - **Raising the 45 s limit of the XLS conversions**: the files convert in 1 to 3 s, so the limit is not the cause.
- **Verified by**: `tests/media-container-named-otherwise.test.ts` (the five real files: `ffprobe` names the container, the opened input lists it, the probe finds streams, and the conversion to MP4 or FLAC has an audio stream and a duration; red on origin/main, 10 of 10, with the refusals of the nightly run), `tests/pdf-page-frames-root.test.ts` (a `/Pages` entry that is a plain dictionary and `pdfjs-issue15590.pdf`: red on origin/main, 2 of 3, with the TypeError in the message; the control of a one-page tree), `tests/media-reference-inputs.test.ts` (the playlists and lists stay refused), `tests/realworld-corpus.test.ts` (the 44 marked files, each with a reason), `tests/bench-parity.test.ts` (the gaps that remain), and the four HTML files converted to EPUB, then to OEB with the `ebook-convert` of the worker image, and read by the output check: refused as having no text before the mark, accepted after it.
- **Revisit when**: a real file of another container than its name is found for a format (add the demuxer with the file), the nightly run of the CI image moves to a LibreOffice that converts the two workbooks within the limit (then the 40 s rows are gone), or a PDF with a page tree that lacks `/Type /Pages` has to be converted.

## 127. A 7.1 source is mixed down to 5.1(side) for AC-3, a JPEG that ends inside its scan is decoded as far as it goes, the record formats are offered as sheets inside the grid of the target, and a page counter is dropped from a text sheet only in a form that says so

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #671 rows and the three decisions on #783 of 2026-10-31, with the review changes of the pull request), decided 2026-10-31 (QA request: close the small conversion rows against the reference engines).
- **Decision**:
  - **A source with more channels than AC-3 codes is written as 5.1(side).** The AC-3 target has `downmixLayout: '5.1(side)'`, so a 7.1 file converted with no channel count gets the filter `aresample=ochl=5.1(side)` and the stream is 5.1(side), six channels. Before, it was refused with a client error (400) for a count the caller never set. A caller who names a count keeps it: `audio.channels: 2` writes stereo, and `audio.channels: 8` or `audioChannels: "7.1"` is still refused with the limit named, because the encoder cannot code it. The mix states no normalisation (`normalisedDownmix` is set for WMA only, `media-audio-targets.ts`): the encoder takes floating-point samples, FFmpeg's own format negotiation leaves a mix for those unnormalised, and that is the file `ffmpeg -c:a ac3` writes with no filter. The layout is the one FFmpeg's negotiation picks, 5.1(side). FFmpeg's layout `5.1` is the back layout, which folds a side channel into the back at a different gain: a first version of the filter used it and its side channels came out 3.01 dB away from the reference.
  - **A JPEG that ends inside its scan data is decoded as far as it goes.** The image library opens it with `failOn: 'none'`, so the decoder's "premature end" is a warning and not a failure; the rows the file does not hold are filled by the decoder (mid grey, 128 in every sample, as libjpeg does) and the picture keeps the dimensions of the header. The option is set only for a truncated stream (`truncatedJpegDecodeOptions`, `image-jpeg-stream.ts`), which is a stream whose first scan header is complete and that holds no end-of-image marker (`FF D9`) after the start of that scan. The test is a search for the marker and not the failure of the segment walk: a stray marker in a complete file makes the walk lose its place without the file being cut, and a corrupt file that still ends with its marker keeps the strict default, so it is reported. In entropy-coded data every `FF` is followed by `00` (ITU-T T.81, B.1.1.5), so a marker found there ends the stream. A stream that ends before its first scan has no pixels and is refused with the typed decode error (`Invalid image: the header could not be decoded`), as before.
  - **A truncated scan must hold one bit for each 8x8 block of the declared frame.** The blocks are those of every component of the frame header: `ceil(ceil(width x h / hmax) / 8) x ceil(ceil(height x v / vmax) / 8)` for each component, h and v being its sampling factors (T.81, A.2.2 and B.2.2), and the scan holds at least that many bits (`minimumScanBytes`, bytes from the first scan header to the end of the stream). Below it the stream is refused with the typed decode error, so a few bytes cannot stand for a full-size raster: the first 359 bytes of the 768 x 512 photo of the corpus (every header, no scan byte) and the same bytes with the frame header rewritten to 8000 x 8000 were opened at full size, the second as a 192 MB raster under the 100 megapixel limit. One bit is below the least a block costs in a first scan (its DC difference takes a Huffman code of at least one bit, ITU-T T.81, F.1.2.1), so the floor refuses a stream that is too short to be a picture of that size at all and is not a measure of how much of the picture the stream holds. The bound holds only for a Huffman-coded DCT frame (SOF0, SOF1, SOF2): an arithmetic-coded frame can code a flat block in less than a bit and a lossless frame codes samples, not blocks, so a truncated stream of any other frame keeps the strict decode. The half of the photo and the real file `lo-tdf138950.jpeg` hold far more than the floor and convert. A JPEG to PDF still embeds a complete JPEG as it is; a truncated one is decoded and written as a raster of the source size, where it was refused.
  - **NDJSON, JSON Lines, YAML, YML and XML are offered as `xlsx`, `ods` and `xls`.** The pairs were not in the registry, so the routing the data engine had for them could not be reached. A record is a row and a key is a column, read with the readers of the CSV, JSON and Parquet targets (`STRUCTURED_SHEET_SOURCES`), where the office engine would have read the text as comma-delimited cells. A value with a comma, a quote or a line break stays in its cell.
  - **A table of records is bounded before its matrix is built.** Records times columns is allocated from the union of the keys, so a line with a key of its own adds a column to every row: 16,384 one-key lines are 16,384 columns and 268 million cells. `tabulate` (`data.ts`) now checks the count of columns, rows and cells first. A spreadsheet target (`xlsx`, `ods`, `xls`) is refused with the typed limit error (`SheetLimitError`, 413) past the columns and rows of its grid (16,384 and 1,048,576; 256 and 65,536 for `.xls`, the header row counted) and past 20,000,000 cells (`XLSX_MAX_MATERIALISED_CELLS`). Every other target is bounded by its own writer's limits, checked before the matrix exists rather than after it: ODS by 1,000,000 cells (`ODS_MAX_CELLS`: its `content.xml` is one string, about 80 characters of markup for an empty cell, and 3,000 one-key lines, 9 million cells from 35 KB, ended in an untyped `RangeError` after 870 MB), PDF by the 16,384 columns and 1,000,000 cells its page layout draws (`PDF_TABLE_MAX_COLUMNS`, `PDF_TABLE_MAX_CELLS`), Parquet by its writer's 4,096 columns, 10,000,000 rows and 20,000,000 cells, and CSV and TSV by the Parquet cell bound; each answers the payload limit (`PayloadLimitError`, 413). The ODS writer (`generateOdsFromData`) takes the bounds of an XLSX worksheet and the ODS cell bound for every caller: 16,384 columns and 1,048,576 rows a sheet, 10,000 sheets and 1,000,000 cells a workbook.
  - **A page counter is dropped from a text sheet only in a form that says so.** A running header or footer line that prints only a number is left out of the text sheets of a PDF workbook, and not counted as text left out beside the tables, when every line of its group differs from its page index by the same offset.
    - Offset 0, a counter that starts at page 1, is taken in every form: `3`, `Page 3`, `3 of 9`, `3 / 9`, and the same between a pair of the same mark (`- 3 -`, `— 3 —`, `– 3 –`, `· 3 ·`). A bare number counts only when it recurs on two pages or more, so a lone `1` in the top band of a one-page document is a section number and stays.
    - Another constant offset, a counter that starts after an unnumbered cover, is taken only in a form that says it is a page (`Page 3`, `3 of 9`, `Page 3 of 9`, the paired marks) and over three pages or more. A bare number or a fraction (`3 / 9`) never qualifies at an offset: `1001`, `1002`, `1003` in a header band, `5` and `6` on two pages, and `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3` on pages 2 to 4 are text.
    - A mark on one side only (`- 3`, `3 -`) is not a counter at any offset.
    - A number that is the same on every page, or follows no constant offset, is kept as a row.
  - **The original rows of #671 hold on the current main.** All 18 jobs of the run of 2026-10-09 (empty output, 9; output bytes not of the target, 9) are `ok` in the nightly of 2026-10-30, and the checks below read each output with a reader other than the converter. The final output check (`checkConversionOutput`) is unchanged: container bytes under a text target fail with a typed 500, and a text target with no content is a valid empty file with an `emptyOutput` warning (entry 8).
- **Why**:
  - **References.** FFmpeg n7.1 `libavcodec/ac3enc.c` 156 to 193 (`ff_ac3_ch_layouts`, the layouts the encoder accepts, 5.1 and 5.1(back) the widest) and `libavfilter/avfiltergraph.c` 1000 to 1092 (`swap_channel_layouts_on_filter`, which scores the layouts of the encoder against the input and takes the best, 5.1(side) for 7.1); the same negotiation gave 5.1(side) from `ffmpeg -i seven-one.wav -c:a ac3` on FFmpeg 9.0.2. ImageMagick 7.1.2-0 `coders/jpeg.c` 267 to 283 (`FillInputBuffer` warns `JWRN_JPEG_EOF` and inserts an end-of-image marker, so the decoder goes on) and 384 to 404 (`JPEGWarningHandler` records a warning, up to 1000, and does not fail); with no start-of-scan header the decoder stops with the error `missing SOS marker` and writes nothing, which the same ImageMagick printed for the file cut at its scan header.
  - **The decoder fills the missing rows and the reference does the same.** ImageMagick 7.1.2-29 reads the half-file of the test with the warnings `Premature end of JPEG file` and `Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment`, and its last row equals ours (the test compares them).
  - **The sheet rows are the records the other table targets already write.** The reference service offers none of these five sources as sheets, as it offers none for JSON or CSV to ODS from text of this kind; the pairs follow the registry's existing JSON to XLSX, ODS and XLS rows, and the data engine's reading is the one its CSV target uses.
  - **Page counters.** No reference engine does this: table extractors write the tables and leave the page text out. The rule keeps what a footer prints for the page it is on (offset 0), which a reader of a sheet named `Page 3` finds redundant, and takes an offset only where the text itself says it is a page number and the run is long enough to be a counter and not a coincidence.
  - **The JPEG floor and the segment search are ours.** libjpeg fills whatever the scan lacks, down to no scan byte at all (the 359-byte prefix of the photo opens at full size with `failOn: 'none'`); the floor is a departure from that, made because the input is untrusted and the declared size is the only thing that sets the raster. The search for the end of the entropy-coded data uses `Buffer.prototype.indexOf` for the next `FF` (a native byte search) where a loop over each byte took 50.1 ms for 42 MiB of scan data with no marker, against 0.74 ms (measured on the arm64 host, ten runs of each).
  - **The bounds of a table of records follow the grids and the readers already in the code.** The columns and rows of a worksheet are those of `sheet-bounds.ts` (Excel specifications and limits; ECMA-376 and [MS-XLS]; LibreOffice Calc `MAXCOLCOUNT`, `MAXROWCOUNT`), and the cells are `XLSX_MAX_MATERIALISED_CELLS`, the most the XLSX reader builds for a workbook, which is also `PARQUET_MAX_CELLS`, the rows times columns the Parquet reader and writer hold in memory at once. The table of records is checked against them before its matrix is built, as the Parquet writer checks `numRows * (columns + 1)` before it encodes.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **The AC-3 mix is FFmpeg's own, not normalised.** The front channels and the LFE keep their level and a side channel holds the side channel plus the back channel at 0.7071 (a row sum of 1.707, measured with the same tone in both pairs: 0.125 in, 0.2133 out), so material at full scale in both pairs of a 7.1 track passes full scale in the side channels, as it does in the file `ffmpeg -c:a ac3` writes. The normalised mix of the first version was 4.6 dB quieter in every channel, the front channels included, which only the side pair needed.
  - **Two channels of a 7.1 track are folded into the sides.** A refusal kept no audio at all, and 7.1 to 5.1 has the one standard fold.
  - **A truncated JPEG shows a grey band where the file is missing.** It is the file's own content, not invented data, so it does not meet the rule of #671 against empty or invalid output. Other warnings of a truncated stream (a corrupt Huffman code before the end) are also tolerated for that stream only.
  - **A cut file with too little scan is refused where libjpeg would read it.** The floor counts the blocks of every component, so a progressive file cut inside a first scan that codes one component alone holds fewer bits than the floor and is refused, and so is a file cut a few kilobytes into a very large frame. The answer is the typed decode error, never a partial raster of a size the file does not support.
  - **A stream that holds an end marker after its scan is read strictly whatever else is wrong with it.** A file cut in the middle that happens to hold `FF D9` later in a header of a following scan (a Huffman table that spells the two bytes) is reported as corrupt where the cut would have been read.
  - **Five more source formats advertise three targets each**, and a record of nested values becomes dotted column names and JSON text for lists, as it does for CSV. An XML or YAML document that is no list of records is one row.
  - **The error of the page counter rule runs both ways, and the direction is different from entry 120's.** Entry 120 said a wrong guess "may add a row to a sheet and never loses one". That claim does not hold for offset 0: a line that equals the page index on every page it recurs on is dropped whatever it means, so a header that numbers sections `1`, `2`, `3` on pages 1, 2, 3 loses those lines from the sheet (entry 132 reports the loss as a warning). A bare number on one page only stays. It holds for the rest: a counter that starts after a cover in a form the rule does not take (a bare number, a fraction, fewer than three pages, a counter printed on part of the pages) stays as a row, which is a line a reader would call furniture. The rule leans to keeping text for everything but a number that equals the page, and the data of the tables is untouched.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **`failOn: 'none'` for every JPEG**: it would also hide the corruption of a complete file, which the reference reports. The option is set for a stream with no end marker only.
  - **Retrying a failed decode with the tolerant option**: the failure arrives from the lazy pipeline at the encoder, after the metadata and the thumbnails were read, so each later reader would need the retry. The stream is judged once, up front.
  - **Refusing a 7.1 source for AC-3 and asking for a channel count**: the reference writes 5.1 with no count, and the refusal named a property the caller never set.
  - **Advertising only `xlsx`, or none, for the record formats**: the data engine writes all three from the same table, and the registry already offers JSON as a source for them.
  - **Reading a page counter from the first number of the line**: a footer such as `2024` or `12%` is text; only the forms above count.
  - **Any constant offset in any form, the first version of this entry**: `1001`, `1002`, `1003` in a header band, `5` and `6` on two pages and `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3` were dropped from the sheets of PDFs without tables, which hold the whole page, with no warning.
  - **Deciding a truncated JPEG by the failure of the segment walk**: the walk also fails on a stray marker in a complete file, and in review 53 of the 54 corrupt-but-complete variants of the photo that fail the strict decode were opened leniently.
  - **No bound on a table of records until the writer**: `tabulate` built records times columns first, and 12,000 one-key lines (about 130 KB) to XLSX took 2,484 MB of resident memory and 3.9 s to write a workbook of 12,000 columns (measured on the arm64 host; the same lines are now refused in 14 ms).
- **Verified by**: `tests/media-audio-targets.test.ts` (a generated 7.1 source to AC-3 with no count read back by `ffprobe` as six channels in the layout `5.1(side)`, stereo when two are named, 8 still refused for AC-3 and WMA; a tone in the front left channel and one in the side left channel of a 7.1 file, each channel of the result within 0.5 dB of the same channel of `ffmpeg -c:a ac3` run with no filter, read by a separate ffmpeg decode: with the normalisation back on both tests fail at 4.65 dB, and with the layout `5.1` the side tone fails at 3.01 dB), `tests/image-truncated-jpeg.test.ts` (the photo of the corpus cut at half its bytes to PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF and PDF with 768 x 512 pixels; the top 30% of the rows equal ImageMagick's decode of the complete file; the last row equals ImageMagick's decode of the cut file; a cut inside the headers, before and inside the scan header refused with the typed error; the zero-scan-byte boundary on the 18,432 blocks of the photo (2,304 bytes, one under refused, the floor opened) and on a frame of one 8x8 block; the first 359 bytes with the frame rewritten to 8000 x 8000 refused; a single stray `FF 12` at offset 50000, which the strict decode refuses with the typed error, and 200 seeded mid-scan corruptions that keep their end marker, all left on the strict default; a progressive JPEG cut at 75% converted and one cut under the floor refused; the real file `lo-tdf138950.jpeg` converted to PNG at 720 x 1280), `tests/image-jpeg-pdf-passthrough.test.ts` (a truncated scan written as a raster of 768 x 512), `tests/data-sources-to-sheets.test.ts` (five sources to three targets read back by LibreOffice and Python's csv module, values with commas, quotes and line breaks; the types of a number and a boolean; the mutation that leaves the five sources out of the set fails 16 tests), `tests/data-records-sheet-bounds.test.ts` (16,384 one-key NDJSON lines to XLSX, ODS and the transient workbook of XLS refused with `SheetLimitError` and to CSV, TSV, Parquet and PDF with the payload limit, each with the heap growing by less than 256 MiB; 16,385 columns and 257 columns named in the message; 65,537 rows to XLS; 5,000 by 5,000 cells; the tables that fit written; ODS refused past 16,384 columns, 1,048,576 rows and 10,000 sheets and the widest row written), `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts` (the five new `.xls` pairs routed to the office suite, which now also list them as native-engine pairs), `tests/pdf-tables-to-sheets.test.ts` (ten forms of footer dropped at offset 0, a decorated counter after an unnumbered cover and two ahead over three pages dropped, and kept: bare `1001`, `1002`, `1003` in a header band, bare `5` and `6`, `Page 5` and `Page 6` on two pages, bare numbers two ahead over four pages, `1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3` on pages 2 to 4 (dropped on pages 1 to 3), the one-sided `- 3`, `3 -`, `— 3`, `3 —`, a bare `1` in the top band of a one-page document, three kinds of footer; one-page tables with `Page 1`, `- 1 -`, `— 1 —` and `1 of 1` without a warning, `Page 4` on page 1 warned, and the converted file with no warning; the keep-tests fail on the first version of the rule), the real file `lo-tdf138950.jpeg` of the corpus (60,662 bytes, 720 x 1280, cut inside its scan), which the nightly of 2026-10-30 refused for ICO and PDF and which now converts to ICO, PDF, PNG and WebP with a PNG that ImageMagick's own decode equals at 120 dB PSNR, and the 18 jobs of #671 on the current main (LibreOffice 26.8 reading the two templates and the five macro workbooks, and the sources parsed with Python for the six files the corpus marks without content; the two PDFs checked with `qpdf --check` and `pdfinfo`).
- **Revisit when**: a real file cut inside the first scan of one component is refused by the floor (count only the blocks of the components that scan codes), a caller needs the grey of a truncated JPEG reported as a warning in the result, the reference service offers the record formats as sheets with different cell rules, or a PDF with a counter on a part of its pages only must be dropped on those pages.

## 129. Refusal tail of the nightly run of 2026-10-31: a phonetic guide in a Word document is read as the text it is set over, a picture on a page written as DXF is left out with a warning, and eleven refusals are listed as explained

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #783, the 38 jobs over 19 files of real-world run 41163999218 on main 79d2e3b0 that stayed refused after policy 128), decided 2026-10-31 (QA request: for each refused file, run the reference engine, fix our side where it converts, keep the refusal where it also fails).
- **Decision**:
  - **A Word document's phonetic guide is read as the text it is set over** (`readRun` in `src/lib/conversions/docx-model.ts`, the `ruby` case). `office-document-61470.docx` holds one run, `<w:ruby>` with the guide `とうきょう` in `w:rt` and the word `東京` in `w:rubyBase`; the reader had no case for `ruby`, so the run was empty and the slide writer answered "There is no text to put on slides." The base text is read as the runs around it, in place, and the guide is not repeated. This is what the office suite's plain-text export writes for the file (`東京`), the oracle of `tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts`; its PDF export draws the guide above the base, which the document model has no inline to carry (the Revisit condition). The drawing-aware reader for documents with shapes is not changed.
  - **A picture on a page written as DXF is left out, and the conversion says so** (`parseSvgGeometries` with `pictures = 'leave-out'` in `src/lib/conversions/svg-geometry.ts`, called by `readSvgPage` in `src/lib/conversions/vector-dxf.ts`). The reference for PostScript, EPS and PDF to DXF is pstoedit and for SVG, Visio, metafile and CorelDRAW sources it is the vector editor's DXF export; neither writes a bitmap. pstoedit 4.3: the DXF drivers are registered with `imageformat::noimage` (`src/drvdxf.cpp` lines 1728, 1749 and 1758), so `/pstoedit.withimages` stays false (`src/pstoedit.cpp` lines 1211 to 1213, `src/pstoedit.pro` lines 146 to 148 and the hook at 3077) and the image operators are not hooked; the base `show_image` only prints that the backend does not support images (`src/drvbase.h` line 596). The editor's `dxf_outlines.py` `process_shape` (lines 265 to 267) returns for every node that is not a path, rectangle, line, circle or ellipse. `govdocs1-004087.ps` (pages 1 to 4), `govdocs1-006990.ps` (page 9 of 36) and `govdocs1-000766.ps` (its one page, a map of 1,756 paths and one picture of 1,571 by 1,340 pixels) were refused with "SVG element <image> is not supported"; each now converts every page, with the warning "Left out the pictures of the pages: a DXF holds lines and text and no bitmaps." in `metadata.warnings`, one line however many pictures. A picture with `display:none` is not counted. The EMF and WMF encoders keep refusing pictures (default `pictures = 'refuse'`), and a mask on a rectangle that is not a bitmap glyph is still refused. The Poppler route opens a warning scope (`convertPdfToSvgPageFormat` in `src/worker/engines.ts`), because only the in-process path had one and the lines of a native chain were dropped.
  - **Eleven refusals are listed as explained** in `bench/realworld/known-refusals.json` (issue 783): six PDFs and five Word documents. The row for `govdocs1-004087.ps` is removed, since the file converts.
- **Refusals that stand**, each checked with the reference engine the formats listing names for the pair, or the closest open one in the published worker image:
  - **Six damaged PDFs** (`qpdf-issue-263`, `-101`, `-99`, `-120`, `-141b` and `pdfjs-bug1020226`, 92 to 4,798 bytes). The reference reads PDF with pdfium (PDF to PNG and JPG), MuPDF (SVG), Poppler (TXT, TIFF), qpdf (PDF), calibre (e-books) and other engines for the Office targets. pdfium (pypdfium2 156.0.8076.0) answers "Data format error" for all six. MuPDF (PyMuPDF 1.28.2) repairs three of them to zero pages, one to a single page with no text, and cannot open the other two. Poppler 25.03.0 `pdfinfo` exits 1 or 99. qpdf 12.2.0 stops on every one in its own reconstruction ("unable to find trailer dictionary while recovering damaged file", "unable to find any pages while recovering damaged file", "unable to find page tree"), so there is nothing for a qpdf repair before reading to hand on; the PDF.js we read with also refuses all six (`InvalidPDFException`, "Illegal character"). The refusals keep their messages ("missing %PDF- header", "Invalid PDF structure", "Invalid Root reference", "Unable to determine PDF page count").
  - **Five Word documents with no body text for slides**: `office-document-59378.docx` (all headers, footers and the six paragraphs empty), `office-document-bug62859.docx` (an empty content control and an empty paragraph), `office-document-headerpic.docx` (a picture in the header), `office-document-issue_51265_3.docx` (four pictures) and `office-document-emptydocumentwithheaderfooter.docx` (the header line "blabal" and the footer line "blabla"). The reference lists no engine for Word to PowerPoint; the office suite's plain-text export is the oracle (entry 88), and it writes white space only for all five.
  - **Two PostScript files stop Ghostscript, the engine of the reference for PostScript to PDF** (and of pstoedit and ImageMagick underneath): `govdocs1-002500.ps` (`/invalidaccess in --put--`) and `govdocs1-006458.ps` (`/limitcheck in --setcolorspace--`). Ghostscript 10.05.1 of the worker image prints the same two errors and leaves a partial PDF of 9 and 1 pages. The causes were established earlier and their tests stay (`tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts`).
  - **Two HEIF files are refused on the CI runner only.** ImageMagick 7.1.1-43 with libheif 1.23.6 of the worker image decodes `libheif-lightning_mini.heif` (256 by 256) and `libheif-uncompressed_comp_rgb_tiled_row_tile_align.heif` (30 by 20), and the converter built from this source and run in that image converts both to JPG, PNG, WebP, PDF and AVIF, with a PNG that has zero differing pixels from ImageMagick's. The runner's libheif 1.17 does not read their brands, so the rows stay.
- **Why**:
  - **References.** ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.3.25 (`ruby`) and 17.3.3.27 (`rubyBase`); LibreOffice 25.2.3 in the worker image for the plain-text export; pstoedit 4.3 and the Inkscape extensions `dxf_outlines.py` for the DXF behaviour above (read, not copied); pdfium, MuPDF, Poppler and qpdf for the PDFs.
  - **Leaving a picture out is what both DXF references do, and the one thing that distinguishes this from entries 42, 74 and 99 is the warning.** Entry 42 refused a picture "rather than drop it without a word", and entry 99 kept the refusal until the output for a page with a picture was decided, having found that both reference writers drop pictures (entry 74). The decision, on QA's instruction to follow the reference's DXF for the source, is that the page converts without the picture and says so, in the warnings that every other lossy step of the converter reports (`metadata.warnings`).
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A page of a scan or a photograph is a picture and nothing else.** It still has no geometry and is refused ("The page draws no vector geometry, so there is nothing to write as DXF."), as before; only a page with a picture and lines or text converts.
  - **The guide itself is written by no target of the document model** (text, HTML, Markdown, PDF, EPUB, ODT, slides), as the office suite's plain-text export leaves it out; the model has no inline for it yet.
  - **The DXF of a Visio drawing with a picture converts** by the same rule (the reference for it is the editor, which also leaves pictures out); the registry still withdraws DXF for the metafile and CorelDRAW sources it withdrew it for.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Writing a picture as an IMAGE entity or a rectangle in its place**: neither reference does, and a DXF reader that cannot load the file the entity names shows nothing or a red box.
  - **Repairing the six PDFs with qpdf before reading**: qpdf cannot reconstruct a trailer or a page tree for any of them, so the repair has no output to read.
  - **Repeating the guide in parentheses after its base text**: no reference writes it so, and it would change the words a text target is checked against.
- **Verified by**: `tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts` (the real file against the office suite's text export, red before the change; the five refusals against the same export and their rows), `tests/docx-model-reader.test.ts` (guides among runs, in a hyperlink and a cell, and 60 levels deep), `tests/dxf-pen-attributes.test.ts` (a picture in four forms, a hidden one, a page of only a picture, 20,000 pictures in bounded time; red when the option is `refuse`), `tests/postscript-real-file-refusals.test.ts` (the three real files: every page, the pages Poppler's SVG draws a picture on keep their geometry, the warning, ezdxf audits without errors), `tests/pdf-unrecoverable-real-files.test.ts` (the six PDFs against qpdf and Poppler, and each refusal against its row).
- **Revisit when**: the document model gains an inline for a phonetic guide (then the HTML and PDF writers can draw it), QA wants the pictures carried in a DXF (entry 99 describes the DXF 2000 route and its cost), a reference engine for one of the six PDFs opens it, or the CI runner's libheif reads the two brands.

## 130. aom is built as a Release at -O3 on arm64 too, and the other build-level levers of the libvips stage (-O3 for the remaining libraries, LTO, a higher CPU target) are measured and not taken

- **Status**: Implemented (epic #759 and issue #641, the arm64 half of entry 121), decided 2026-10-31 (QA request: audit the build flags of the libvips stage and keep only measured wins). The speed and the bytes were measured on the arm64 Lima VM; the x64 library does not change.
- **Decision**:
  - **`docker/sharp-libvips/aom-release.patch` (entry 121's `aom-release-x64.patch`, same two lines) is applied on both platforms.** `build.sh` runs `patch -p1 --forward --fuzz=0 < "$here/aom-release.patch"` without the platform test. aom is then configured with `CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -O3"` and `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` on linux-arm64 as it already is on linux-x64; no other option of the aom build moves.
  - **Nothing else in the stage changes.** The audit below found one library that is built for size on the encode path and has a measured gain at -O3. The other candidates did not move a row outside the noise, or are unsafe for the hosts the image must run on, and are recorded under Alternatives rejected.
- **Why**:
  - **Audit of the build, taken from the compile commands and CMake caches of an arm64 build of the pinned release** (`posix.sh` of sharp-libvips v1.3.4 at `ebb95f8`; lines are from that file):

    | Library | Optimisation level now | LTO | CPU target and SIMD | Upstream's own default or advice |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | libvips 8.18.7 | `-O3` (`CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -O3"`, line 392; Meson's `release` puts `-O3` before the `-Os` of `CFLAGS`, so the extra `-O3` is what wins) | none | `-march=armv8-a`; highway compiles NEON_WITHOUT_AES, NEON, NEON_BF16, SVE, SVE2, SVE_256 and SVE2_128 and dispatches at run time; on x64 `-march=nehalem` with the highway targets of `meson.build` lines 476 to 496 (SSSE3, AVX3_ZEN4, AVX3_SPR and AVX10_2 disabled) | `meson.build` lines 476 to 496 |
    | highway 1.4.0 | Release, `-O3` (line 243) | none | dynamic dispatch of every attainable target | `g3doc/faq.md` lines 437 to 447 |
    | libheif 1.23.5 | Release, `-O3` (line 192) | none | baseline flags; the AV1 work is in aom | |
    | aom 3.15.1 | **`MinSizeRel`, `-Os` (line 182)**; Release `-O3` on x64 since entry 121 | none (the CMake files offer LTO only for the sanitizer builds) | `-march=armv8-a`; the NEON dot product, i8mm, SVE and SVE2 files carry their own `-march`; chosen at run time from the kernel's hardware capabilities (`aom_ports/aarch64_cpudetect.c` lines 150 to 167, `CONFIG_RUNTIME_CPU_DETECT` 1 in `cmake/aom_config_defaults.cmake` line 106); x64 has NASM and per-file SSE2 to AVX2 flags | Release is libaom's default build type (`CMakeLists.txt` lines 34 to 39) |
    | libwebp 1.6.0 | `-O3` (entry 84) | none | NEON in the arm64 baseline; on x64 the SSE2, SSE4.1 and AVX2 files carry their own flags and are dispatched at run time | Release, SIMD on (`CMakeLists.txt` lines 29 to 31 and 103 to 104) |
    | mozjpeg 0826579 | Release, `-O3` (entry 84) | none | `WITH_SIMD` on: NEON on arm64, NASM with cpuid dispatch on x64 | `BUILDING.md` builds with `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` |
    | libpng 1.6.58 | `-O3` (entry 84) | none | the NEON filters are compiled in (24 NEON symbols in `libpng16.a`); on x64 the SSE2 filters (`--enable-intel-sse`) | `INSTALL`: hardware optimisations on |
    | zlib-ng 2.3.3 (zlib-compat) | Release, `-O3` (line 132) | none | run-time CPU detection on, native instructions off (`CMakeLists.txt` lines 104 to 106) | its CMake disables LTO unless native instructions are on (lines 293 to 295 and 377 to 382) |
    | lcms2 2.19.1 | `-O3` (line 172) | none | plain C, no SIMD | |
    | cgif, libimagequant, libultrahdr | `-O3` (lines 219, 356 and 367) | none | baseline | |
    | glib 2.90, libxml2, libexif, expat, libffi, libarchive, freetype, harfbuzz, pixman, cairo, pango, fontconfig, fribidi | `-Os`: the compile lines read `-O3 ... -Os` (Meson) or `-Os` (autotools), and the last one wins | none | baseline | |
    | libtiff 4.7.2 | `MinSizeRel`, `-Os` (line 233) | none | baseline | |
    | librsvg 2.63.2 (Rust) | `opt-level=z`, fat LTO, one codegen unit (lines 92 to 98) | yes | Rust toolchain of its own | |

    Every library is built with `-fPIC -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections`, and the final link has `--gc-sections`. The CPU target is `-march=armv8-a` on arm64 and `-march=nehalem` on x64 (`env.sh`). Highway, aom, libwebp, mozjpeg, libpng and zlib-ng all keep run-time dispatch, so the image runs on any x86-64 and arm64 host.
  - **The speed of aom at -O3 on arm64** (Lima VM, 4 cores, `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`, the product's encoder options: quality 70, effort 3, tune ssim, 4:2:0, 8 bits, 4 threads; one process per side and pair, the sides alternating A, B and B, A, 12 pairs of 5 encodes each, median of the 5 per process, then median over the pairs; base time over head time, above 1 is faster): `kodim23.png` 1.19, `photo-a.jpg` 1.18, `photo-b.png` 1.17, `wm-alpha-graph.png` 1.22, `wm-lineart-family-tree.png` 1.22, `wm-screen-history.png` 1.20 for the library that `build.sh` of this entry makes; every one of the 72 pairs is above 1.07. The same comparison for the library built with the same patch through a build hook before `build.sh` took it over gave 1.15 to 1.24 (12 pairs), and with the dispatch limited to NEON and the dot product (`AOM_SIMD_CAPS=0x5`, which a Neoverse N1 has; its CRC32 bit, 0x2, was left out, and that hash path is integer-only; 14 pairs) 1.17 to 1.25. The WebP, JPEG and PNG rows of the same runs are 0.95 to 1.03, which is noise: the median of the nine WebP rows is 0.99 in two runs and 1.01 in a third, and a code layout effect of 1 to 2 % from the larger aom archive cannot be excluded.
  - **The bytes do not change.** 261 outputs of the 9 corpus pictures (WebP at four qualities, effort 4 and 6, with and without sharp YUV and lossless; JPEG at four qualities in three layouts and the mozjpeg preset; AVIF at 8 bits at qualities 30 to 90 and efforts 3 and 5, 4:4:4 at 10 bits, 12 bits for the 16-bit pictures; PNG at levels 0, 1, 6 and 9, palette PNG, GIF, TIFF; a resize, a rotate and sharpen) are identical to the base build's for this library, and for the libraries of the other candidates below. The AVIF cases were also run with the dispatch limited to NEON and the dot product (`AOM_SIMD_CAPS=0x5`) and to NEON alone (`0x1`), for both builds: identical to the base at the default dispatch. The base run twice gives the same list. `-march=armv8-a` has fused multiply-add and libaom sets no `-ffp-contract`, which is why entry 121 kept arm64 back until the bytes were compared; they are.
  - **Why it is not 2 times.** The work is CPU time, and the hot loops of libaom are NEON intrinsics that `-Os` already emits as vector code; `-O3` adds inlining, unrolling and scheduling (an inference from the flags: aom was not profiled by function). On one thread the CPU time of an encode falls from 42.7 to 35.9 ms for `photo-a.jpg` (1.19) and from 588.7 to 476.0 ms for `wm-screen-history.png` (1.24); on 4 threads the wall time falls from 25.7 to 22.1 ms and from 248.0 to 204.8 ms (1.16 and 1.21). The ratio of CPU time to wall time on 4 threads is 1.72 and 2.47 for the base and 1.70 and 2.42 for the head (the first and last stretches of an encode are serial, entry 121), so the serial stretches are the same on both sides and the gain at 4 threads is the gain in CPU time. The speed rows of the image family that use this library are the photograph AVIF rows; graphics and 16-bit pictures go to the command-line encoder, which the libvips build does not contain.
  - **What bounds the other rows.** A profile of the PNG written as the encoder's input for `wm-screen-history.png` (one thread, 17 ms) is a third lcms2 colour conversion of the picture's embedded profile (`MatShaperEval16`, `PrecalculatedXFORM`, `Unroll3Bytes`, `Pack3Bytes` and `pow`: 33 %, plain C at -O3 already), then libpng's NEON Paeth filter that reads the source (10.7 %), `inflate_fast_neon` (7.9 %) and the band copies of libvips (15 %); `perf` sampling of 200 conversions on the unstripped library of this entry. None of them is built for size, so no flag is left for those rows.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Size and time.** The arm64 library is 21,339,400 bytes against 18,848,888 (+2,490,512, +13.2 %), and the aom archive is larger. The stage builds in 4 min 10 s to 4 min 32 s on the 4-core VM against 4 min 43 s for the base, so build time does not grow measurably.
  - **The VM's cores are not the host's.** The VM reports NEON, the dot product, i8mm and BF16 (no SVE); the Ampere A1 host (Neoverse N1) has the dot product only. The comparison with the dispatch limited to that set gives the same gain and the same bytes, but it is not a measurement on the host. A run on the A1 host is still to be read when the image is built there.
  - **A toolchain bump can change the bytes.** The identity above holds for gcc-toolset-15 15.2.1-7.1. A new compiler can contract floating-point operations of the rate decisions differently, so the 261-output comparison is repeated when `GCC_TOOLSET_RELEASE` moves.
  - **One patch less to carry.** The two arch-specific states of aom are gone; the same two lines apply on both platforms, with `--fuzz=0`.
  - **Reapplying after a sharp upgrade.** The hunk sits at `posix.sh` lines 178 to 187 of the pinned release. If a new release moves its context the build fails at the patch (`--fuzz=0`); the change to remake is `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=MinSizeRel` to `Release` and `CFLAGS="${CFLAGS} -O3"` before `AOM_AS_FLAGS`. There is no new download, so `sources.sha256` does not change.
  - **Reproduction.** Rocky Linux 8 at the digest of `Dockerfile.worker`, `docker/sharp-libvips/toolchain.sh`, then `docker/sharp-libvips/build.sh <out>`. The library built with this entry has SHA-256 `393e266af611258fd743910f7466beef570fb753736e6c7d6710ebb8e5411b22`, the same from two builds (one through a hook that applied the patch, one through `build.sh` of this change); the base built the same way has `d9c245141fe0ed34cdb1f4c616b06047acd6bceedd94bfa3ec77537d8089459e`. As the open finding of epic #759 says, an arm64 rebuild is not reproducible across days or toolchain refreshes, so these digests identify the builds compared here.
  - **Vulnerabilities.** The aom source is the same libaom 3.15.1 as before, so the CVE tracking cost is unchanged: a fix reaches the image when sharp-libvips releases it and the pins move.
  - **CI.** `docker/sharp-libvips/` changes, so the cache key of the stage moves and the first run builds it once (about 18 minutes on a 4-core x64 runner). The x64 library is built with the same flags as before, so no x64 speed comparison is needed for this entry.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **`-O3` for the libraries that are still built for size** (glib, libxml2, libexif, expat, libffi, libarchive, freetype, harfbuzz, pixman, cairo, pango, fontconfig, fribidi; `FLAGS` with `-O3` instead of `-Os`, aom and libtiff keep their `MinSizeRel`): 261 identical outputs, and 12 pairs, every row between 0.98 and 1.02 and the AVIF rows 0.99 to 1.01. None of them is on the path of an encode row; the library grows by 2,097,096 bytes.
  - **LTO for libvips, libwebp, mozjpeg and libpng** (`-flto=4 -ffat-lto-objects`, the link with `-flto`; not for aom, zlib-ng or highway, whose files carry flags of their own, which zlib-ng's CMake turns LTO off for): 261 identical outputs, no gain (12 pairs, rows 0.94 to 1.01; the nine WebP rows 0.97 to 1.01, `wm-screen-history.png->webp` 0.97). Applying LTO to the code that has per-file ISA flags would also give a binary that the VM cannot show to be safe on the A1 host.
  - **A higher static CPU target** (`-march=armv8.2-a+dotprod`, built on top of this entry's patch and compared with it, 12 pairs): the same bytes, no row outside 0.96 to 1.04, the AVIF rows 0.98 to 1.02. It would also stop the image on an arm64 host without those instructions, and the libraries that gain from the extensions already select them at run time.
  - **zlib instead of zlib-ng**: the build already links zlib-ng 2.3.3 in zlib-compat mode at -O3 with run-time CPU detection (`posix.sh` lines 129 to 135).
  - **`-O3` for libheif and lcms2**: both already are (lines 192 and 172).
  - **Other highway targets**: every attainable target is compiled and dispatched; the x64 list is the one libvips sets in `meson.build`.
- **Verified by**: `tests/sharp-libvips-build.test.ts` (the aom patch changes the build type and nothing else, `build.sh` applies `aom-release.patch` on both platforms and `Dockerfile.worker` copies it; red with the platform test still in `build.sh`), the builds, the byte comparison and the timings above (Lima VM `default`, Rocky Linux 8 root, the production scripts under `docker/sharp-libvips/` with a comparison harness that is not in the repository). The arm64 image is built on the arm runner of `deploy-oci.yml` and runs on the A1 host; no CI job compares the arm64 library's bytes or quality, and the nightly runs the x64 library, so it shows only that x64 is unchanged.
- **Revisit when**: sharp is upgraded (the pins and the hunk move), `GCC_TOOLSET_RELEASE` moves (repeat the byte comparison), the first deploy of a build with this entry runs on the A1 host (time an AVIF encode there against the previous release, and roll back if it is slower), or a build of the library for x64 can be compared with the LTO and CPU target rows above on the CI runner.

## 131. The Vorbis encoder of the worker image takes frames of any size, so that FFmpeg 9 hands it a whole frame at a time, and the stream it writes stays the same
