Headless Chrome 156 on a production build: in a probe of the placement code, a trigger in a snug `overflow: hidden` box took focus from the search on open with `hide` and kept it with the measure above; in the page at 1440 px, wheel scrolls left the panel 2 px under its trigger with focus inside until its bottom passed under the 64 px header (panel from y -111 to 210), and the next scroll (y -351 to -30) moved focus to the trigger with the picker still open. The overflow-clip case is the only one where the placement differs from `hide`; every other placement is the library's own.
- **Revisit when**: a page needs a surface the tokens do not name (add the token, never a raw class), QA changes the brand mark or a reference page changes a component listed above, or the fonts change licence or size. For the flow and the copy: when the reference pages change their chips or their intros, when a headless menu becomes a dependency (the split button's menu moves to it), when an ad loader with a consent prompt is added (the ad slots come back with it), or when search data shows the intros cut short at a length other than 160.

## 140. A DNG whose decoder prints `data corrupted at` is developed with a warning when it holds every strip of the raw image LibRaw develops, and every other report on the decoder's stderr still refuses a camera file

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #686, the rows `raw/raw-samsung-s23.dng->jpg|png/converts` and `raw/class-phone->jpg|png/converts`), decided 2026-11-01 (QA request: develop the files LibRaw decodes completely while warning). The rule it replaces came with the native decoder (#410): any text on the decoder's stderr refused the file. The first review of the pull request found that a cut copy of the S23 file developed, which narrowed the rule to DNG and added the checks below; the second chose the raw directory by its photometric interpretation and compared its size with the decoded picture; the third chose the directory as LibRaw does, allowed the size changes LibRaw makes after choosing it, and read the decoder's report before its image; the fourth followed tag 0xf000 and refused the entries through which LibRaw reads a directory the check does not follow; the fifth listed every route by which LibRaw fills a directory slot and refused tag 0x7250, a Panasonic flag on its own and the CIFF signature, and narrowed the Nikon route to an EXIF directory that lists a makernote.
- **Decision**:
  - **One line of LibRaw's own wording from a DNG is a warning, anything else is a problem, and the report is read before the image** (`decoderWarningOffset` in `src/worker/raw-decoder-report.ts`, which `convertWithNativeRaw` in `src/worker/engines.ts` calls once the decoder has written an image, before its layout, pixel cap and completeness checks). The stderr of `dcraw_emu`, trimmed, is a warning only when the source is a DNG and the text is exactly `<the path the engine passed>: data corrupted at <offset>` with an offset of 1 to 15 digits. That is the text of `default_data_callback` in LibRaw's `src/utils/utils_libraw.cpp` (lines 23 to 31 in 0.21.4, the release of Debian 13). An empty stderr is no report. For every other camera format the line refuses the file as before, and so do `Unexpected end of file`, a line about another file, an offset that is no number, a second line and any other text, with the message they always had (`Native RAW decoder reported a problem with the .<format> file: ...`, the working directory shown as `<tmp>` and then cut to 300 characters), also when the image the decoder wrote is unreadable.
  - **The DNG must hold every strip or tile of the raw image LibRaw develops, and the decoded picture must be a size LibRaw writes from it** (`dngRawImageData` in `src/worker/raw-dng-image-data.ts`, whose comment gives the file and lines of each rule). The directories are read as LibRaw 0.21.4 reads them (`parse_tiff` and `parse_tiff_ifd`; the blocks named in this entry were compared with 0.21.2 and 0.22.2, and 0.21.2 is the same while 0.22.2 differs only in the width of integer types, a float read of DefaultScale and a Sony-only branch that skips a nested read): the chain from the header, the SubIFDs of each and the directory a tag 0xf000 names, each read where its entry is met among the parent's, at most 10 in all. A directory of more than 512 entries, which is also what LibRaw reads past the end of the file, counts toward the 10 and ends the list it is in; an entry of more than 8 values that would end past twice the file size is skipped; a value is read with LibRaw's size for its type, and bytes past the end of the file read as 0xff. A chain that points back at itself, or a SubIFD that points at its parent, is read again until the 10 are used.
    - **Tag 0xf000 and the size tags 0xf001 and 0xf002.** LibRaw parses one more directory from the offset in the first value of a tag 0xf000 (`tiff.cpp` lines 425 to 428), in any directory, ignores what it returns, and gives it the next slot, so it comes before the directory the chain lists next and before a SubIFD whose entry follows it. Tags 0xf001 and 0xf002 set a directory's width and height as ImageWidth and ImageLength do (lines 432 to 439), the entry read last winning. A copy of the Canon CFA DNG sample with a tag 0xf000 in IFD0 gives the choice LibRaw makes: the directory the tag names is decoded when the next one lists a strip past the end of the file (whole), by its own size when the next one is another width (whole), and the file is refused as truncated when the named directory is the one that lists the strip past the end. `dcraw_emu` 0.22.2 writes the picture of the named directory in all three cases (960 x 540 also when the next directory is 944 wide, so it did not decode that one).
    - **Every route by which LibRaw fills a directory slot is followed or refused at its trigger** (`unmodelled-layout`). Only `parse_tiff_ifd` adds a slot (`tiff_nifds++`); a `grep` of 0.21.4 and 0.22.2 for each call of it, of `parse_tiff`, and of the parsers that reach them (`parse_minolta`, `parse_exif`, `parse_makernote`, `parse_makernote_0xc634`, `parse_jpeg`, `parse_qt`, the CR3 parser) gives the same calls in both releases. The `tiff.cpp` lines are those of 0.21.4. Route, trigger and decision:
      - The chain from the header (`parse_tiff`, lines 1556 to 1574) and tag 0xf000 (lines 425 to 428) are followed.
      - SubIFDs (tag 0x014a, lines 549 to 577) are followed. Their DSLR-A100 branch (lines 550 to 558) is refused at a directory width of 3872 whatever the model, which the check does not follow; their Hasselblad branch (lines 559 to 567) is refused with the tag 0xc51b that sets its flag.
      - Hasselblad tag 0xc51b (lines 902 to 915), which also restores the slot count, is refused whatever the make.
      - The JPEG stream at a strip offset (tags 0x0111, 0x0201 and 0xf007 read while the directory has no BitsPerSample, lines 91 to 133), whose TIFF `parse_tiff` reads, is refused when the stream starts as a JPEG.
      - The Panasonic tags, whose CameraIFD 0x0120 and stream at tag 0x0118 parse a directory (lines 236 to 247 and 379 to 415), replace LibRaw's first switch once a tag 0x0001 of 4 values holds a number (lines 73 to 76). That tag 0x0001 is refused.
      - Tag 0x7250 in any directory calls `parse_minolta` (lines 615 to 618), whose TTW block calls `parse_tiff` (`minolta.cpp` lines 101 to 102). It is refused. A copy of the Canon CFA DNG whose IFD0 holds one, naming a TIFF of one 950 x 530 directory, is decoded at 950 x 530 by `raw-identify`; the round before took the chain's 960 x 540 copy of IFD0 for it.
      - EXIF tag 0x8769 calls `parse_exif` (lines 778 to 781), whose tag 0x927c calls `parse_makernote` (`exif_gps.cpp` lines 219 to 311), which for a make that starts with NIKON parses a Nikon makernote whose tag 0x0011 calls `parse_tiff_ifd` (`makernotes.cpp` lines 334 to 343, `nikon.cpp` lines 318 to 324). The EXIF tag is refused when the make may start with NIKON and the directory it names lists tag 0x927c. The make is the Make read last (lines 475 to 477). LibRaw copies a UniqueCameraModel over it only while no Model has been read (lines 923 to 934); the check does not follow the model, so any UniqueCameraModel of NIKON counts, and no other clears it. At most 65,535 EXIF entries are read in all, one directory of the largest count; LibRaw reads every EXIF directory an entry names with no limit (`exif_gps.cpp` lines 75 to 77), and past that budget the file is refused.
      - DNGPrivateData (tag 0xc634, lines 1352 to 1480) is refused while no DNGVersion has set a number, where it calls `parse_minolta` and `parse_tiff_ifd` (lines 1473 to 1479), and while the make may start with NIKON, where `parse_makernote_0xc634` parses a Nikon makernote (`makernotes.cpp` lines 60 to 69).
      - A Phase One marker (MMMM or IIII) in the first 32 bytes, where `identify` runs `parse_phase_one` first (`identify.cpp` lines 502 to 508), and HEAPCCDR at byte 6, where it parses the file as a CIFF and reads no TIFF directory (lines 511 to 515), are refused.
      - Kodak tags 0x8290 and 0xfe00 (`parse_kodak_ifd`), Leaf tag 0x8606 (`parse_mos`), GPS tag 0x8825, the Sony SR2 block decrypted in memory (lines 1527 to 1535), `parse_exif` itself (it sets only the shutter of the last slot) and the makernotes of other makes fill no slot and are not routes.
      - The JPEG, Fuji RAF, RIFF, QuickTime, MRM and CR3 headers of `identify` (lines 520 to 705) and its `parse_jpeg` of a file with no make (line 798) need another header than a TIFF one and are not reached.
    - **Which directory is the raw image.** The first whose ImageWidth and ImageLength are 1 to 65535, whose NewSubFileType is 0 and whose PhotometricInterpretation is CFA (32803) or Linear Raw (34892), whatever its Compression (`apply_tiff`). The engine runs `dcraw_emu -T -6 -w -o 1 -Z`, with LibRaw's default options (`LIBRAW_RAWOPTIONS_CONVERTFLOAT_TO_INT` only) and no `-s`, so an enhanced image (NewSubFileType 16), a preview or a mask is never a frame, the largest frame is not preferred, and the first frame is the one decoded. A full-resolution YCbCr preview in IFD0 and an enhanced image before the raw one are not taken for it.
    - **Its size.** The ActiveArea when the directory has one (an extent of 0 falls back to ImageWidth or ImageLength, as `identify` does; an extent that is negative or above 65535 refuses the file, where LibRaw keeps it in the 16 bits of `height` and `width` and would wrap it), its ImageWidth and ImageLength otherwise. LibRaw then drops a row or a column so that a Bayer image starts on an even margin, up to 5 so that an X-Trans margin is a multiple of 6, and up to 18 rows or 16 columns for three camera models, so the picture may be up to 23 pixels smaller than that size on each axis, never larger. It stretches non-square pixels by the DefaultScale it reads last (taller when the pixels are narrower, wider when they are wider, not at all within half a percent of square), and turns the picture when the first directory whose Orientation turns or flips it gives 5 to 8: the iPhone 12 Pro sample, 4032 x 3024 with Orientation 6, is written 3024 x 4032, the five others with Orientation 1 are not turned. A picture of half the size, as a preview would be, is refused.
    - **Its data.** Its tiles, or its strips when it lists no tiles, need SHORT or LONG arrays with as many byte counts as offsets, at least one, none empty and each inside the file; these are the rules of another open-source raw decoder, which reads the raw data from nothing else. The arrays are read 16,384 values at a time and the image data never.
    - **Each finding has its own refusal.** A strip or tile past the end of the file is refused as `The .dng file is truncated: its raw image data runs past the end of the file`. A file that is no classic TIFF (BigTIFF included), lists no CFA or Linear Raw image the decoder develops, lists no usable strips or tiles, whose ActiveArea has an extent that is negative or above 65535, which holds one of the entries above, or whose raw image is not a size the decoded picture can have is refused as `Native RAW decoder reported corrupted data in the .dng file, and the file cannot be shown to be whole: <the reason>`. The check runs only when the decoder printed the line.
    - **Where this differs from LibRaw.** This check does not read EXIF or GPS directories, which fill no slot, except to look for tag 0x927c in an EXIF directory while the make may start with NIKON, and it does not skip a makernote entry that LibRaw skips for its size. The make follows the Make tag only: a UniqueCameraModel of NIKON counts after a Model, and the makes Sarnoff, Leaf and Imacon that other tags write do not clear it. The model name is not followed, so a SubIFD tag in a directory 3872 pixels wide is refused whatever the model; a strip offset read before BitsPerSample is refused when its stream starts as a JPEG, though `ljpeg_start` could still fail on a later marker; a directory whose entries run past the end of the file ends its list, where LibRaw stops reading the file; the size is a range, where LibRaw's own trim depends on the CFA pattern and the model; and the tile grid against the image size and the overlap of tiles are not checked.
  - **A warning does not skip a gate, and it adds one** (`assertDecodedRawWhole` in `src/worker/raw-decoded-tiff.ts`, which the engine calls after the image checks). The image the decoder wrote still has to pass `readDecodedTiffLayout`, `assertWithinPixelCap`, `assertCompleteDecodedImage` (the pixel data as long as its header says) and `hasRepeatedTail` (90 % of the bottom 12 % of rows repeating), as an image that printed nothing does. A file that printed the line must also pass the directory check above, and is refused when its last 9 rows each repeat the row two above (`endsInRepeatedRows`, at most 8 such rows).
  - **The end of the stream is not decided by the decoder after the line.** `LibRaw::derror` (the same file, lines 164 to 187) checks for the end of the stream, prints and throws only while no error has been counted (`if (!data_error && input)`); after the first `data corrupted at` it only counts. A DNG cut later in its data therefore exits 0 with a full-size image whose rows past the cut repeat, and only that one line on stderr. The two checks above are what refuse it.
  - **The result says so, and only API callers see it today.** A developed file with a warning carries `metadata.warnings = ["The RAW decoder reported corrupted data at byte <offset> of the file; some samples of the picture may be wrong."]`, reported with `reportConversionWarning` inside a `withConversionWarnings` scope the engine opens (the dispatcher that the queue workers and the API call opens none), the field the API shows as `warnings` and `X-Conversion-Warnings` (entry 9). The web client shows no conversion warning yet, a row on #671. A file that printed nothing has no `metadata`.
- **Why**:
  - **The Samsung Galaxy S23 file is complete.** It is a DNG of 4000 x 2252 pixels, 3 samples of 12 bits, Linear Raw, one lossless JPEG strip of 22,681,296 bytes at offset 2,731,255 (`WhiteLevel` 4095, no linearisation table). 7,489 of its 27,024,000 samples, all of them green, lie between 4096 and 4183 in 633 rows (rows 169 to 1089), at most 88 above the largest value 12 bits can hold. `ljpeg_row_unrolled` (`src/decoders/decoders_dcraw.cpp`, lines 447 to 540 in 0.21.4; `ljpeg_row` at lines 378 to 445 does the same for the `sraw` layout) calls `derror` for a sample with a bit above the frame's precision, so the first of them, in row 169, printed `data corrupted at 4384328`, byte 1,653,073 of the strip. The offset is inside the one strip (the file has no tiles) and is not trailing padding: the 65 bytes after the strip are the end of the file. The warning is a range check, not a failed decode: a widely used JPEG library (3.2.0) decodes the same strip with no message to the same 27,024,000 samples, the 7,489 included (compared sample by sample), and `dcraw_emu` 0.21.2 (Ubuntu 24.04) and 0.22.2 write the same pixels.
  - **The decoders that develop camera files do not refuse it.** `dcraw_emu` of LibRaw 0.22.2 and 0.21.2 prints the line, exits 0 and writes the whole image. A second open-source raw developer (5.10) prints `Corrupt data near 0x42e648` (the same offset in hexadecimal) and writes the whole image: its `derror`, in its own copy of the original decoder, counts and goes on, with the jump out of the decode commented out. A third (4.6.1) decodes it with the raw decoder named under its data above, which stores each lossless JPEG sample with no range check, prints nothing and writes the whole image. On a grid of 64 x 36 cells the brightness of our picture correlates 0.9999 with the second developer's, 0.990 with the third's and 0.994 with the 4000 x 2252 preview the camera itself embedded, and in each of four horizontal bands at 0.992 or more; none of the three has a row of zeros or a row equal to the one before it. Our picture and that of `dcraw_emu` are the same file, byte for byte in their pixels. The reference of the benchmark's `converts` rows is `dcraw_emu` itself, which developed the file while the product refused it.
  - **The old rule judged by a sentence, and the sentence says little.** LibRaw calls `derror` from 50 places in 11 files (0.21.4) for reasons as different as a sample beyond its bit depth and a count that does not fit. The strip of the same file has a restart interval of 16 rows (`DRI`, 141 intervals), and `ljpeg_row_unrolled` looks for the next restart marker when an interval starts (lines 452 to 460), so damage stays in its interval. Of nine damaged copies of the file (one byte flipped, 4096 bytes of zeros, or 4096 random bytes, each at 2.8 MB, 10 MB and 20 MB of the file), `dcraw_emu` printed `data corrupted at` for all nine, exited 0 and wrote an image each time; against the clean decode, the four it was measured on differed in 1, 4, 538 and 2,245 rows. `derror` prints only the first error, so the benign offset 4384328 hides what follows it in seven of the nine. The second developer develops three of them with its warning. The third refuses the same three, as its raw decoder throws on a code that is not in the Huffman table and on a missing restart marker, two checks LibRaw does not make. No line can tell a patch of bright samples from damaged data.
  - **No count is reachable.** LibRaw counts the errors (`LibRaw::error_count()`, `libraw/libraw.h` line 219 in 0.21.4) but `dcraw_emu` and the C API give no way to read it, so the engine cannot tell 7,489 samples from millions without linking LibRaw. The refusal that remains rests on what the file and the image show: every strip the DNG lists is in the file, the pixel data is as long as declared, and the bottom rows do not repeat.
  - **Only a DNG shows a cut in its own directory, and only the directory LibRaw decodes shows it.** A DNG lists the offset and byte count of every strip or tile of its raw image, and the raw decoders read the raw data from nothing else, so a copy cut anywhere in that data lists bytes it does not have. Checking another directory than the one decoded proves nothing about the picture: with NewSubFileType 16 on its only full-resolution directory a DNG is refused by `dcraw_emu` (`Unsupported file format or not RAW file`) while the rule of the second round took that directory, so this round takes the directory LibRaw takes and no other. The S23 strip ends at byte 25,412,551 of 25,412,616. Cut at 5, 12, 20, 23, 24, 25 and 25.4 million bytes and at 25,412,500 and 25,412,550, every copy that decodes is refused by this check, with LibRaw 0.22.2 and 0.21.2 alike; a cut at 3 million bytes stops the decoder (`Unexpected end of file`), and a copy cut at 25,412,551 bytes, which keeps the strip and drops only the 65 bytes after it, is developed. For other camera formats the directory that holds the raw data is chosen per maker, and the ORF and RW2 headers are not classic TIFF, so for them the line stays a refusal.
  - **The size changes are LibRaw's.** A copy of the Canon CFA DNG sample (960 x 540, ActiveArea 0 0 540 960) with its ActiveArea at 1 1, 1 0, 0 1 and 3 3 is written 958 x 538, 960 x 538, 958 x 540 and 956 x 536, one row or column fewer than its area for each odd margin, and with DefaultScale 1:2 it is written 960 x 1080, by `dcraw_emu` 0.22.2 and 0.21.2 alike. The second round's exact comparison refused each of them when the line was printed.
  - **The bottom-run test is the second line.** The decoded images of the 23, 24 and 25 million byte cuts end in 218, 122 and 26 identical rows, which `hasRepeatedTail` passes and `endsInRepeatedRows` refuses; the full file's last row differs from the row two above it. The filler of this Linear Raw file repeats the row before, so it also repeats the row two above, the period `hasRepeatedTail` uses for Bayer data. A cut inside the last rows of the strip (25,400,000 bytes) leaves no repeated row, which the directory check refuses.
  - **The bottom-run test is the only defence against a download that stopped early but kept the file's size.** A copy of the S23 file whose bytes after 20, 23 or 25 million are zeros prints only the line, its directory lists every strip inside the file, and `hasRepeatedTail` passes it; `endsInRepeatedRows` refuses all three, and the test pins the 23 million byte case.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A file damaged in the middle of its data that decodes to a whole image is developed**, with the warning in its result, as `dcraw_emu` and the second developer develop it; before, the first message of the decoder refused it. The damage in the test above is a few wrong rows or a shifted brightness below them, which a reader of the warning can see. Files whose damage the stderr rule caught only by chance (the first overflow came before any other) are no longer caught.
  - **Some DNGs that print the line are refused for their size, where the first round developed them.** The first round compared no size; now a DNG that printed the line is refused as one that cannot be shown to be whole when its picture is larger than its raw directory, more than 23 pixels smaller on an axis, stretched by another DefaultScale than the one read last, or turned against the first Orientation. The known cases are a Fuji SuperCCD layout, which LibRaw turns by 45 degrees into a picture of another size, a model correction larger than the three LibRaw makes today, a file with one of the triggers above (a Nikon DNG whose EXIF directory lists a makernote, or with private data, included), and an ActiveArea that is negative or above 65535.
  - **Known over-refusals of the route list.** A DNG with a SubIFD tag in a directory 3872 pixels wide is refused whatever its model, where LibRaw takes the DSLR-A100 branch only for that model. A UniqueCameraModel of NIKON read after a Model, a Make of NIKON followed by a Sarnoff, Leaf or Imacon tag, and a makernote entry LibRaw skips for its size refuse a file whose make LibRaw does not hold as NIKON. None of the 31 real DNGs measured hits one. A DNG that prints nothing is not affected.
  - **A cut file that prints nothing is decided by the gates that do not read stderr.** Of the twelve cases of the truncation test (eleven formats cut at half, an ARW at nine tenths), the cases LibRaw stops on print `Unexpected end of file`, exit 2 and write no image: ten with LibRaw 0.22.2 and nine with 0.21.2. The others decode to full size with an empty stderr, the ARW cases with both releases and the NEF with 0.21.2, and the image gates refuse them. None of the twelve relied on the stderr rule.
  - **A DNG that printed the line and whose last 9 rows really repeat** (a flat black or clipped bottom edge) is refused, as every file that printed the line was before this entry. The test runs only where the decoder warned, so a silent file keeps the share of `hasRepeatedTail`.
  - **A camera file of another format that prints the line stays refused**, even when it is whole.
  - **The text is LibRaw's**: a release that changes the wording makes a warning a problem again (the file is refused, as before), never the other way.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Any exit 0 with an image is developed**: it would also pass a second report that is not this one (`Cannot do postprocessing ...` is printed and the run goes on), and every cut DNG above.
  - **The same directory check for every TIFF-based camera format**: it would hold where the raw directory lists its strips, but which directory holds the raw data is chosen per maker, the ORF and RW2 headers are not classic TIFF, and the evidence of this entry is one DNG.
  - **The directory rules of another raw decoder (any full-resolution directory in a compression it decodes)**: the second round's choice. It can check a directory LibRaw never decodes, such as an enhanced image, and miss the one it does; the engine runs LibRaw.
  - **The exact size LibRaw writes**: it depends on the CFA pattern, the margins and the camera model, which LibRaw works out from the maker's tags; the range covers what LibRaw does to a DNG today and still refuses a preview.
  - **Only the bottom-run test**: a cut inside the last rows of the strip leaves no repeated row.
  - **The strict bottom run for every file**: a whole camera file with a flat bottom edge that decoded silently would be refused for nothing the decoder said.
  - **A warning only when the offset is small, or when the samples are few**: the offset says where the first error was, not how many there were, and the count cannot be read (above). The offset is no longer compared with the file size: the directory check decides whether the file is whole.
  - **A second decode with a LibRaw build of our own that reads `error_count()`**: a binary to build, ship and patch for one counter; revisit below.
  - **A check of the lossless JPEG stream in the engine (a code in the table, the stream ending at its marker)**: it is what the other raw decoder does and it would catch the damaged strips, but it is a decoder of its own for one container of many; this entry follows the decoders that develop the file.
  - **Refusing, as the old rule did, and calling the file damaged**: the camera's own file is complete, and the reference tool develops it.
- **Verified by**:
  - `tests/raw-native-decoder-warning.test.ts` (32 cases) and `tests/raw-dng-image-data.test.ts` (55 cases) pass on macOS with LibRaw 0.22.2 and on Ubuntu 24.04 with LibRaw 0.21.2. Neither runs 0.21.4, the release the source lines come from.
  - Every `tests/raw-*.test.ts` file with `tests/bench-parity.test.ts` (31 files, 632 cases and 6 that only check for the tools in strict mode) passes on both, with all the RAW samples present.
  - Red before green in each round. First: 7 cases of the warning test (the S23 file to JPEG and PNG and the stand-in line over a whole image, for the wording; the S23 file cut to 23,000,000 bytes, a stand-in DNG whose strip runs past the end, the line from a NEF, and nine repeated bottom rows, all developed). Second: the two skipped IFD0 layouts and the zero-padded S23 case. Third: 19 of 60 cases on head 4c441e3b. Fourth: 21 cases on head a46c6383. Fifth: 6 of 54 cases of the directory test on head 44d73170 (the Canon copy with tag 0x7250, tag 0x7250 in IFD0, a SubIFD and a 0xf000 directory, a Panasonic flag on its own, a NIKON EXIF directory with no tag 0x927c, the Make read last, and the CIFF signature), then the EXIF budget case before its budget.
  - The warning test covers the S23 file to JPEG and PNG with the warning and offset 4384328 and its brightness against the embedded preview; the file cut to 23,000,000 and 25,412,550 bytes refused as truncated and cut to 25,412,551 bytes developed; the zero-padded copy refused for its repeated bottom rows; the Canon CFA DNG with four ActiveAreas and DefaultScale 1:2 developed at the size LibRaw writes; the line refused for a cut strip, a YCbCr IFD0 over a cut SubIFD, a NEF, a preview-sized picture, a BigTIFF and a DNG with no raw image; reports over an unreadable image; the repeated-row rule; five other reports; and no working directory left behind.
  - The directory test covers strips and tiles in both byte orders, the arrays, the size range, Orientation, ActiveArea, DefaultScale, the choice of the raw directory, the loops and limits (10 directories, 512 entries, a million SubIFDs), tag 0xf000 and its Canon copies, tags 0xf001 and 0xf002, and each route of the list above with the case that it is not.
  - 35 changes to the check in the fourth round and 11 in the fifth (the Panasonic count and value, tag 0x7250, the EXIF makernote scan, the Make overwrite, the UniqueCameraModel rule, the EXIF budget bound and its count, the CIFF signature, the makernote tag) each fail at least one case.
  - The reviewer's file of the fifth round (`m7250c.dng`), which the test rebuilds byte for byte, was `whole` on head 44d73170 and is `unmodelled-layout` now.
  - Of 31 real DNGs (29 of the real-world corpus: iPhone, Pixel, Huawei, LG, OnePlus, Xiaomi, DJI, Leica M8, M9 and M240, Pentax, Samsung, Ricoh, Sigma, Blackmagic and Adobe-converted Canon; and the S23 and Canon samples), none returns `unmodelled-layout`.
  - The six iPhone DNGs at hand (6s Plus, 7 Plus, SE, 8, XS and 12 Pro) print nothing, are developed, and are whole at the size `dcraw_emu` writes, the 12 Pro turned to 3024 x 4032.
  - The S23 sweep (cuts at 3, 5, 12, 20, 23, 24, 25 and 25.4 million bytes and at 25,412,500, 25,412,550, 25,412,551 and 25,412,552 bytes, and copies zeroed after 20, 23 and 25 million) gives the same answers through the dispatcher with both releases: the first stopped by the decoder, the next nine refused as truncated, the next two and the whole file developed with the warning, the three padded copies refused for their repeated bottom rows.
  - The S23 file is pinned in `tests/fixtures/raw/cases.json`, which `npm run fixtures:raw` reads with the two other lists at CI setup (with retries, into the cache keyed on the three lists; 25,412,616 bytes more, 342 MB in all), so no test downloads it. A new key restores the newest older `raw-fixtures-` cache; the fetcher checks the size and SHA-256 of every cached file, downloads only what is missing or wrong, and deletes the files no list names and any `.part` file.
  - `ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1 npm run bench:quality -- --parity --family raw --quality-only`, run in an earlier round on the development Mac (LibRaw 0.22.2), passes the four `converts` rows of the S23 file and the phone class (S23 JPEG SSIM 0.95594 against 0.95758, BD-rate of PSNR -4.59 % and of SSIM -8.72 %, PNG SSIM 0.99996). It lists `raw/dng->gif/bytes` as failing and AVIF and GIF rows as worse than the CI baseline, all on samples whose decoder prints nothing and so never reach this rule. The S23 file gets the same answer in this round's sweep. `tests/bench-parity.test.ts` no longer asks the gap file for any number of entries, and its hand-built rows name a synthetic sample.
- **Revisit when**: the nightly real-world gate shows a camera file that is developed with this warning and has visible damage, a whole DNG refused for its size after the line, or a whole camera file of another format refused for the line; LibRaw's command line tools or a packaged helper print `error_count()` (a budget on the count, or on its share of the samples, would then separate a bright patch from damage); the worker image links LibRaw for another reason; or a release of LibRaw changes the wording or the exit status of the report, checks the end of the stream after the first error, or changes how it chooses or sizes the DNG frame.

## 141. The web interface is offered in English and Korean: English at the unprefixed URLs, Korean under /ko, every visible string in a messages file per language

- **Status**: Implemented (QA decision of 2026-11-01: ship the web interface in English and Korean, locale in the path, English at the existing URLs, hreflang alternates, a language selector, and a test that fails on a missing key; more languages later by adding a messages file), decided 2026-11-01. Covers the language rows of #903.
- **Decision**:
  - **Routing.** next-intl (MIT) with `localePrefix: 'as-needed'` (`src/i18n/routing.ts`): English keeps every current URL, Korean lives under `/ko/...`, and `/en/...` redirects to the unprefixed URL. The pages moved under `src/app/[locale]/`; each page is a server wrapper that sets the request locale (static pages stay prerendered, now once per locale) and renders a view from `src/components/pages/`. The locale middleware runs inside `src/middleware.ts` for every page path; API paths (`/api` and `/api/...`, but not `/api-docs`) keep the earlier handling and are never locale routed, and `/<locale>/api/...` answers 404. A path with a dot names a file and never reaches the locale routing (`/wp-login.php`, `/.env`, `/backup.zip`, `/index.html` answer the cheap 404 they did before), with one exception the registry defines: the dot of a dotted format id, which is always `tar.<suffix>` (`/zip-to-tar.gz`, `/tar.gz-to-zip`). The exception reads the id in any case (`/zip-to-TAR.GZ`), as the path did before. The matcher must be a literal, so a test builds it from the registry's suffix list (`DOTTED_FORMAT_SUFFIXES` in `src/lib/slug-parser.ts`) and fails when the two differ. A path under a locale prefix reaches the page without the matcher's file rule, so the page applies the same rule: it takes out the dotted format ids and answers 404 when a dot remains (`/ko/foo-to-bar.php`, `/en/foo-to-bar.php`, `/ko/backup.zip`).
  - **Negotiation on the root only.** The visitor's language (the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, then `Accept-Language`) decides only `/`; any other unprefixed URL is English, so a shared link opens in the language it names. Only the language selector writes the cookie (in the browser, through next-intl's `Link`), so no page answer carries a `Set-Cookie`. The root's answers say `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, and its redirects `Vary: Accept-Language, Cookie`; on the English page the root rewrites to, Next.js replaces `Vary` with its own (its page handler sets the header), and `no-store` keeps that answer out of every cache. The selector keeps the page's query string.
  - **Messages.** `messages/en.json` and `messages/ko.json` hold every visible string of `src/app` and `src/components`: headings, labels, placeholders, `aria-label`s, titles and descriptions, toasts and errors, empty states, the FAQ, the footer, the format descriptions and the slug pages. The registry's English format descriptions and category labels and the unit catalog's English names stay the source of that English copy and are read into the English messages at load time (`src/i18n/messages.ts`); Korean keeps its own translation of all 302 format descriptions, the 12 categories and the 77 units. Slug titles and descriptions are worded from a typed descriptor the slug parser returns.
  - **What each page carries.** A page hands its client components only the namespaces they read (`PAGE_NAMESPACES` in `src/i18n/client-messages.ts`), and a converter page only the descriptions of its two formats.
  - **Server errors.** API answers stay English (they are the API contract), and the interface words them the way RFC 9457 practice does: the problem `type`, or a stable `code` next to the English `error` of a route of the web application, is the key of a sentence in the page's language; the numbers that sentence names travel as typed fields of the answer (the plan, size and limit of a 413, `maxRequestBytes`, the concurrency `limit`, the quota's `dailyLimit`, the upload budget's `refusal` and limit, a lockout's `retryAfterSeconds`) and are formatted for the locale; the server's English `detail` is never part of the sentence, and no sentence names a status code. A message key is the problem name after `https://api.easyconvert.io/problems/` or the code itself, so the interface keeps no table from one to the other: a code counts only when it is in its closed list in `src/lib/refusal-codes.ts`, and a problem name only when it is an own key of the problem sentences (`Object.hasOwn`), so a name such as `constructor` or `__proto__`, or a message key that is no code, reads as its status class; a sentence that names a number has a key of its own, used when the answer carries the number. One module words them (`src/components/i18n/error-wording.ts`), the routes answer through one helper (`codedRefusal` in `src/lib/api/problem-details.ts`), and the code lists live in `src/lib/refusal-codes.ts`. An answer whose type or code the interface does not know reads as one sentence for its status class (refused, or failed on our side). The server's text is for API clients and logs and never reaches the interface: RFC 9457 aims `detail` at the developer of a client, not at the person using the page, so a refused row or alert shows the one sentence of its `type` or `code` and nothing under it, for a refusal (4xx) and a server failure (5xx) alike (an exception's text can name a path or a program's output, RFC 9457 section 5). The dashboard routes (`/api/account/files/**`, `/api/keys/**`, `/api/webhooks/dlq/**`) find their caller through one function (`resolveDashboardCaller` in `src/lib/api/dashboard-refusal.ts`: the owner of the key the request carries in `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key`, else the signed-in person, with the scope a route reads with and the `*` scope a route that changes keys or failed webhooks needs; a key is an explicit credential and decides over a session cookie sent with it, as public APIs that accept both a cookie and a token authenticate by the header when one is present, so a script that sends a narrow key from a signed-in browser gets that key's scope and not the person's full access; the converted-file routes had tried the key first before the resolver, and `tests/dashboard-route-codes.test.ts` sends a cookie with a `convert:write` key to every route and expects the key's answer) and name a refusal with a code of `DASHBOARD_REFUSAL_CODES` only where the status cannot say the cause: a key without the `*` scope (`admin_scope_required`, a 403 the access check also answers for other causes), key settings or a grace period out of range (`invalid_key_settings`, `invalid_grace_period`, a 400 that has several causes), and a key that could not be made (`key_create_failed`, a fixed sentence through `serverFault`, no longer the exception's text); the dashboard words them by code (`useDashboardErrorWording`). The access check (401, 403, 429, 503) and an unknown id (404) answer without a code, and the status map below words them, as it already did for the same statuses from the proxy; a code that only repeated its status (`sign_in_required`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited`, `service_unavailable`, `not_found`) and one no request could reach (`id_required`, since a route's path always holds its id) are gone. An answer without a code or a problem `type` still comes from the proxy in front (`{"success":false,"error":"Too many requests"}` for its burst limit, `deploy/oci/nginx-easyconvert.conf`) or from an older server, so by default it takes the problem that a small explicit map of the client names for its status (`SINGLE_CAUSE_STATUS_PROBLEMS` in `src/components/i18n/error-wording.ts`), and the map holds only the statuses that have one cause: 401 `unauthorized`, 403 `forbidden`, 404 `not-found`, 405 `method-not-allowed`, 413 `payload-too-large`, 415 `unsupported-media-type`, 429 `rate-limited` and 503 `service-unavailable`. A 401 reads "sign in to continue", a 403 "not allowed for your account" and a 503 "unavailable" instead of "try again in a moment", which never helps when the session has ended, and the proxy's burst limit reads as a short wait and not as the daily limit. Every other untyped status stands for several causes: a refusal (400, 409, 422) reads "check what you entered and the settings you chose", since trying again unchanged would fail again, and a failure (500, 502, 504) reads as the sentence of the action that failed. The server's own table of default types (`DEFAULT_PROBLEM_TYPES` in `src/lib/api/problem-details.ts`) is not read by the interface: it maps 429 to the daily quota, which is right for the routes that send a `type` and wrong for a proxy. The sign-in form turns the map off (`useProblemWording({ byStatus: false, untypedRefusal: 'action' })`) and keeps its action sentence, because one status stands for several causes there and its answers are worded by `code`. A read of the dashboard (its files, failed webhooks or keys) and a replay send nothing to check, so an untyped refusal of one reads as its own sentence (`untypedRefusal: 'action'`) and not as "check what you entered". An answer with a `type` or status the interface has no sentence for reads as the sentence of the action that failed or of its status class, and a refusal that needs its own words gets a sentence (a deletion answered 404 drops its row, since the record is gone, for a file, a failed webhook and an API key alike through one helper, `useRecordDelete` in `src/components/dashboard/useRecordDelete.ts`, which also sends one request per record at a time and reads the list again once the record is gone; each list numbers its reads and applies only the answer of the latest (`useReadSequence` in `src/components/dashboard/useReadSequence.ts`), so a read in flight when the record was deleted, or a second delete's read, cannot bring the row back; a file and a failed webhook read "already deleted", and an API key reads "that API key no longer exists", because a revocation answered 404 means the server does not know the id, not that it was revoked; a key's revocation closes only its own confirmation; the button of a file being deleted is off until its request ends; no dashboard delete route answers 409). A failure only the browser sees (a dropped connection, a script that threw: the client edge, the ZIP of the results, the API reference's specification, the dashboard's requests) has no server log, so the page words it without the reason and `warnBrowserFailure` (`src/lib/browser-failure.ts`) writes the English reason to the console with `console.warn`; that is where a browser-side reason lives, and a person who reports the failure can read it there. The API reference's error box has a retry button, since its copy says to try again. An unclassified 500 of five routes answers a fixed English sentence through `serverFault`, and the server logs the error: `/api/convert`, `/api/auth/login`, `/api/auth/register`, `/api/fetch-url` and `/api/queue/jobs` (the enqueue route of every queued conversion). The catch-alls of `/api/v1/uploads`, `/api/v1/archives/inspect` and `/api/v1/storage/credentials` still send the error's text with their 500 and are a row on #671. A client mistake is no 500: a body that is not `multipart/form-data` answers `/api/convert` 415 with `multipart_required`, and a body that is not a JSON object (malformed, empty, `null`, an array) answers `/api/fetch-url` 400 with `invalid_json`, as sign-in and sign-up answer `invalid_json`. `/api/convert` names each refusal: a missing file, an empty file, a missing target, an unknown format, an unsupported pair, unreadable options, a spoofed or unrecognised content, and the causes of a failed conversion by the `refusalCode` the error's class declares or inherits (a `readonly` field, as `status` is, so a subclass answers its parent's cause; a malformed, encrypted, password-protected or unsafe archive, a missing volume or an encrypted archive header (their declared 422, as `/api/v1/archives/inspect` answers them), an encrypted or DRM-protected document, an unsupported input or method, an input over a decode limit, a time limit, a missing engine, an option that does not apply). Every problem type the server sends has its sentence (unprocessable input, missing engine, job timeout, closed connection, PDF post-processing, PDF/A, unsupported option, unknown format, invalid archive, missing volume, encrypted archive header, corrupt job state, upload part in flight, reused or in-flight idempotency key, an invalid customer storage endpoint, a customer storage provider not yet available): a test reads every problem reference in `src`, fails on a type without a sentence, and fails on a reference whose name is not written out. A conversion in the queue fails with a `ConversionFailure` (`src/lib/conversion-failure.ts`): a code for what the client decides, the server's refusing answer, or a queued job that failed on a worker, worded by the `failedRefusalCode` its worker records from the same field (next to `failedCode` and `failedStatus`, on the job hash and the internal job answer) or as a failed job, with no HTTP status. The worker's reason stays in the job record, the live event, the webhook and the log, where support reads it, and a queue row shows only the sentence of its code. The worker masks the error once, where it catches it (`maskFailure` in `src/lib/security/server-paths.ts`, which runs `scrubError` with the path roots): credentials and the paths under the server's own directories leave the message, the causes and the error's own string fields, and credentials leave the stack (its frames name the files of the code, only operators read it, and no API returns a stack or a job's `stacktrace`), so the stored reason, the live `failed` event, the `job.failed` webhook (which sends the stored reason), its dead letter and the log carry the same text, both graph schedulers mask a node's reason again when they store it, and a job's own log rows (`Job.log`, which the owner's job routes return) are masked the same way. The roots are read once when the process starts: the standard top-level directories of the images (`/opt`, `/etc`, `/var`, `/home`, `/srv`, `/root`, `/run`, `/lib`, `/lib64`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/sbin`, `/tmp`, `/proc`, `/app`, `/shared`), the temporary directory, the working directory (left out when it cannot be read), the storage directory, the directories the sandbox runs engines from (`PATH`, else its default) and the configured tool and path variables of the configuration schema, and the install prefix of each `bin` directory. A root starts a path after anything but a letter, digit, `_`, `.`, `~`, `/` or `-` (so `2>/tmp/err.log`, `|/usr/bin/x` and `file:///tmp/a` are masked and `x/tmp`, `./tmp` and `-I/usr` are not) and when it is followed by the end, a slash, a space, a quote or a closing mark (so `</tmp>` stays an end tag). A quoted path ends at its closing quote (a backtick may close with an apostrophe, `` `/tmp/a b' ``) when no letter or digit follows that quote, with any extension or none (`'/tmp/ec-abc/my file'` is masked whole); any other path ends at its first space or at a bracket, comma, semicolon, colon, equals sign or quote, so `spawn *** ENOENT: not found` and `*** version 10.02` keep the words after the path (`redactPaths` in `src/lib/security/redact.ts`, one forward pass). Every other slash stays, because it names what went wrong: a PDF name (`/Pages /Kids`), an end tag, a JSON pointer, `/dev/null`, a MIME type, a ratio, a URL. Reasons stored before this rule was deployed stay as they were until their job records expire. A refusal code survives the CPU pool: a thread's failure carries the `refusalCode` of its error, and a WOFF2 limit keeps its class and its 413. API-visible changes: the 429 of `/api/auth/login` names the shared problem type `https://api.easyconvert.io/problems/rate-limited` instead of `https://easyconvert.app/errors/rate-limited` (no caller in the repository or the SDK read the old URI, and the API is before 1.0), an unclassified 500 of the five routes no longer carries the exception's text, a body that is not multipart answers `/api/convert` 415 and a body that is not a JSON object answers `/api/fetch-url` 400 (both were 500), a missing archive volume and an encrypted archive header answer `/api/convert` 422 (was 500), and every `code`, number field and `failedRefusalCode` is additive. `/api/fetch-url` and the sign-in routes name every refusal with a `code` (sign-in: invalid JSON, missing fields, wrong credentials, a lockout under the shared `rate-limited` problem type, an undeterminable client address, an unconfigured client-IP trust; sign-up: invalid JSON, invalid email, password length, existing account), and the page words them by code, never by status alone. Option, password and key errors are codes the interface words.
  - **Korean copy.** 해요체 throughout (`~해요`, `~해 주세요`, `~할 수 없어요`; no `~합니다` or `~하십시오`), short active sentences that say what happened and what to do next without blame, no protocol or jargon term in a sentence a person reads (no `HTTP`, status code, `RBAC`; the format dossiers and the developer pages may keep `MIME` and the like), durations in the largest sensible unit through `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (`23시간 후 삭제`, `Deleted in 23 hours`, `곧 삭제` under a minute; the unit is chosen from the floored value, so 3,599 s reads 59 minutes, 5,400 s one hour, 86,399 s 23 hours and 604,799 s 6 days, never the next unit up), the name of an account's sign-in method and of a format in the page's language or as the bare format name (`PNG`), one glossary (변환, 업로드, 다운로드, 파일 형식, 대기열, API 키, 동영상, 압축 파일), no particle attached to a value whose last sound decides it (`{src} 파일을 {tgt} 형식으로`), numbers, sizes and dates through `Intl` for the locale. A conversion from one format to another reads with an arrow in titles, headings and links (`PNG → JPG 변환기`), since two names side by side do not say the direction. An archive is a 압축 파일; 아카이브 stays only inside the name of a format that says archive (tar 아카이브, Java 아카이브(JAR), 웹 애플리케이션 아카이브(WAR), 엔터프라이즈 아카이브(EAR)). A sentence that sends a person to a control names it by its label: a failed row's reason ends "변환을 눌러 다시 시도해 주세요." and "Select Convert to try again.", since the row has no retry of its own and the bar's Convert runs it again. A format button of the picker is named in the page's language by the format name the file row uses ("ULTRAHDR 이미지", "ULTRAHDR Image"), not by the registry's English name.
  - **Time zone.** Dates formatted in the browser read in the viewer's zone (`src/i18n/ViewerTimeZone.tsx`): the server render and the first client render keep the server's zone, so hydration matches, and the browser's zone follows. The switch renews the wording functions, so the dashboard's reads run when the dashboard is enabled and not again with the new functions. The quota reset stays in UTC, where it happens.
  - **Type.** One sans family draws Latin and Hangul, a subset of Pretendard Variable (OFL, weight 400 to 700) generated from the two messages files by `scripts/subset-web-font.py` into a Latin file (preloaded) and a Hangul file (fetched only by a page that draws a syllable); entry 139 has the source, the sizes, the hashes, the licence handling and the size budgets. Korean text breaks between words, not between syllables (`word-break: keep-all` with `overflow-wrap: break-word` on the Korean page), headings included. The subset's middle dot advances 0.25 em, so an unspaced 가운뎃점 between two syllables is drawn.
  - **SEO.** Every page's metadata names its canonical URL in its locale and its alternates in every locale with English as `x-default`, as absolute URLs on the public origin, and that is the only source: next-intl's `Link` header is off (`alternateLinks: false`), because it builds the alternates from the request's host and the raw slug. The web image is built with `APP_ORIGIN`, a constant of the deploy workflow that a test ties to the host of the nginx site file (the push build cannot read the environment secret that holds `APP_URL`, and the origin is no secret); the build stops at once when it is empty (`test -n "$APP_ORIGIN"` before `next build`), `scripts/check-built-alternates.mjs` fails the image build when a prerendered page names a root-relative link, another origin or no `x-default`, and `deploy/oci/deploy.sh` refuses a new release whose home page names another canonical host than the origin Compose resolves for the web (`${APP_ORIGIN:-${APP_URL}}`, read with `docker compose config`, so the quotes of the env file read as Compose reads them; only the `APP_ORIGIN` key is taken from its output, and the deploy stops with Compose's error before the release starts when Compose cannot resolve the web service); it asks for the page as often as the health check, saves it to a file so a cancelled job stops the request, and logs the two hosts only. The language selector links English at its unprefixed URL, so no link of the selector answers with a redirect, and writes the locale cookie when followed. A converter page names its lowercased slug as canonical, and a slug page of formats the registry does not have (or a slug that names nothing) is `noindex`. The API keys page names its own canonical URL.
- **Why**:
  - **Reach.** Korean is the second language QA chose for the interface; without it a Korean reader depends on a browser translation layer, which also translates format names, option values and code samples.
  - **Search.** A locale in the path gives each language its own indexable URL with hreflang pairs, which a query parameter or a client-side switch cannot.
  - **Every current link keeps working**: English at the unprefixed URLs changes no URL that is already shared or indexed.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Bundle.** First load JS grows by 6 to 17 KB per route (home 458 to 471 KB, converter page 483 to 489 KB, auth 122 to 137 KB, account redirect 103 to 120 KB) for the next-intl client runtime, and the middleware from 39.8 to 52.4 KB. The prerendered HTML carries the page's messages: gzipped, home 20.0 to 26.5 KB in English and 27.8 KB in Korean, auth 10.6 to 12.6 KB, API reference 11.9 to 18.2 KB (before the per-page split the full set added 18 KB to every page).
  - **Dependency.** next-intl brings `@swc/core` and `@parcel/watcher` for its message extractor; with its other dependencies about 15 MB unpacked in production `node_modules` (the Linux swc binary is 10.7 MB). The build applies its plugin, and since #949 the server does not: `next.config.mjs` returns the plain config in the server phase (`PHASE_PRODUCTION_SERVER`) and imports the plugin only in the other phases, so `next start` loads neither `@swc/core` nor any native addon (`tests/next-config-runtime-phase.test.ts` records every module a fresh Node process resolves and every addon it opens). **next-intl stays a production dependency.** The web image runs on the worker image's production `node_modules`, and the built pages and middleware bundle the next-intl runtime, so a web image without next-intl starts: the #949 web image with the 52 packages that would leave production removed (19 MB of 597 MB of `node_modules`) booted under the production flags and answered the same status, page language and size on twelve paths, and the same locale redirect of `/` for a Korean browser. It stays because `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists the production packages of the lockfile, and next-intl, use-intl, intl-messageformat and the `@formatjs` parsers ship inside the pages served to every browser, so a development dependency would drop the notices of code the service distributes.
  - **Translation upkeep.** Every new string needs a Korean translation before the tests pass, and every new Hangul syllable a rerun of the font subset.
  - **A 404 under `/ko` for a path with two or more segments shows the global English not-found page**: the single-segment converter route answers every other path.
  - **A path outside the server's directories stays in a reason, and so may part of a spaced one.** A path under no root (a top-level directory the images do not use, or one the configuration does not name) is not masked; masking every slash rewrote PDF names, end tags and JSON pointers in the stored reason for good, and PDF errors are among the most common refusals. A directory the servers start to use belongs in the configuration schema, which adds it to the roots. A path with a space that is not quoted keeps what follows its first space (`/tmp/my dir` reads `*** dir`, `/tmp/a/report 1.pdf: error` reads `*** 1.pdf: error`). This is the accepted limit: a program's arguments, its version and a user's name for a file cannot be told apart by their shape, and every rule that guessed (a file extension before a colon, a later word with a slash) swallowed `version 10.02`, `7.1.1` or `see docs/ref.md` in one case and left a tail in another. Quoting is the signal the programs give, so a quoted name is masked whole. The stack keeps its paths for the same reason as above.
  - **Support reads the reason from the record, not from the page.** A person who reports a failed conversion can no longer copy the server's sentence from the row; the reason is in the job record, the `failed` event, the `job.failed` webhook and the log, and an API client still receives `detail` and `error`.
  - **A test DOM.** The test that the signed-in dashboard reads each resource once renders its hooks to markup and hydrates them with React's own renderer in jsdom (MIT, a development dependency), under the page's providers and ViewerTimeZone; a static render runs no effect, and the loop it guards against only shows when effects run. jsdom is held at 29.1.1, whose engines (`^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24.0.0`) contain the `>=24.0.0` of `package.json`; jsdom 30 asks for `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26`, which leaves out Node 24.0 to 24.14 and 25, and narrowing the engines of the service for a test tool would be the wrong way round. The test runs without StrictMode, as a production build does; a development server, where StrictMode mounts each effect twice on purpose, reads each resource twice.
  - **The image origin is a workflow constant.** One environment exists today, so a constant tied to the nginx host by a test is enough; a second environment needs a repository variable passed as the build argument, a one-line change. The deploy check catches a constant and an `APP_URL` that drift apart, after the build and before the release goes live.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Subdomains per language** (`ko.`): a second host to certify, cookie and proxy configuration per host, and no gain over a path for one product.
  - **A query parameter** (`?lang=ko`): search engines treat it as the same URL, and every internal link would have to carry it.
  - **Client-only translation** (one HTML, strings swapped after load): crawlers and the first paint see English, and `lang` cannot be right in the HTML.
  - **Negotiating on every unprefixed path** (next-intl's default with `as-needed`): a Korean browser opening a shared English link would be redirected away from the page it was sent.
  - **The full KS X 1001 Hangul set** (2,350 syllables): about four times the bytes of the subset the copy needs (entry 139 has the sizes), with a test guarding the subset's coverage.
  - **A "technical details" disclosure under the sentence** (the rule of rounds one to seven): it showed raw English (`File spoofing rejected ... Operation failed closed.`) to a Korean reader who cannot act on it, and a disclosure that opens on every error is noise for the person it was meant for.
  - **The server's English detail after the translated sentence**: it put English in a Korean sentence, and a fact the sentence needs is better sent as a number the locale formats.
  - **Wording sign-in errors by HTTP status**: one status stands for several causes (a 400 for invalid JSON, missing fields or an undeterminable address), so the sentence was wrong for some of them.
  - **A repository variable for the image origin now**: it suits more than one environment, which does not exist yet; the constant and its test say the same with less configuration.
  - **An executable tmpfs for the native compiler** (#949, the failed v0.7.0 deploy): v0.7.0 loaded the plugin in `next.config.mjs` at start, its compiler (`@swc/core`) could not load its native binding in the production container (read-only root, `noexec` tmpfs), and the web server exited before it answered; the deploy rolled back. Mounting `/tmp` or the home directory with exec rights would let the server start, but every upload and conversion scratch sits on those paths, and `noexec` is what keeps a planted binary from running there (entry 122).
  - **A writable cache path for the native addon**, outside the read-only root: it needs a mount that is both writable and executable, the same exposure as above, to hold a compiler the server never uses.
  - **Moving next-intl to the development dependencies**: the image would start (measured above), but the notices of the bundled runtime would leave `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
  - **A smoke test that starts the image without the production flags**: the v0.7.0 image started and answered 200 under a plain `docker run`; it failed only read-only with `noexec` scratch. `scripts/boot-web-image.sh` starts the built web image with the flags of the web service in `docker-compose.prod.yml` (read-only root, no capabilities, uid 10001, no new privileges, the seccomp profile, `noexec` tmpfs on `/tmp`, the home directory and the build cache) and requires the home page to answer 200, on a loopback port Docker picks, so it never collides with another server on the runner; the build job of the deploy workflow loads the image, runs it, and pushes its tags, and moves the worker image's `main` tag, only after it passed, so a deployable tag always names an image that started. It fails on the v0.7.0 web image and passes on the #949 one; the AppArmor profile is left out, as only the production host loads it. A test holds the script's flags to the compose file's, and another runs it against stand-ins for `docker` and `curl`: it passes only on 200, fails on 500, a redirect, an exited container and a failed start, removes the container every time, and refuses an attempt count that is not a whole number of at least 1 before it starts anything.
