  - **The locale middleware keeps a path with whitespace as it came, under a language prefix as well, and lets malformed percent escapes answer 400.** next-intl rewrites to the decoded path read back as a URL, and URL parsing drops a tab or a line break anywhere and a space or control character at the end, so `/pdf-to-jpg%20` reached the slug page as `/pdf-to-jpg` and answered 200. next-intl also redirects a path with a superfluous or capitalised prefix (`/en/x`, `/KO/x`) to the decoded path, so `/en/pdf-to-jpg%20` and `/KO/pdf-to-jpg%20` redirected to a real page. `pageLocaleAnswer` in `src/middleware.ts` checks `hasDroppedUrlChar`, which guards `decodeURI` so a malformed percent escape (`/%E0%A4%A`, `/ko/%E0%A4%A`, `/en/%E0%A4%A`, `/pdf-to-jpg%E0%A4%A`, `/%c0%ae%c0%ae/etc`, `/ko/%c0%ae`) falls through to `handlePageLocale` and Next.js answers 400 Bad Request with zero stderr instead of an uncaught `URIError` (500). When the decoded path holds a dropped character, `pageLocaleAnswer` rewrites directly to `/${locale}${path}` with `X-NEXT-INTL-LOCALE` set to `locale`, ahead of any redirect, so the slug page reads the whole slug and answers 404 in the language of the prefix.
  - **The 404 page** (`src/app/[locale]/not-found.tsx`, `NotFoundPageView`) is, as the reference's is, a thin header holding the brand logo linked to the home page (no navigation, no buttons, no footer, no other link), then centred a small code, one heading that names the route and one sentence, in the language of the path (`/x` and `/ko/x`). The route is the path without its language prefix and leading slash (`foo/bar`), read in the browser. English reads `404`, "The route foo/bar could not be found." and "Sorry, the page you are looking for could not be found."; Korean reads "페이지 없음", "foo/bar 경로를 찾을 수 없어요." and "주소를 다시 확인해 주세요." with no status code, as entry 141 requires. The page names itself in the tab and to a screen reader (`generateMetadata` of `not-found.tsx`: "Page not found | EasyConvert", "페이지를 찾을 수 없어요 | EasyConvert", and its sentence as the description), not as the home page of the layout above it. The framework's error shell renders the document, so the theme script of the layout has not run; the page applies the stored theme (`useThemeToggle` via `themeFor` in `src/hooks/useThemeToggle.ts`), and a visitor with none gets the theme of the system (`prefers-color-scheme`), as every other page does through the script of the layout. The route is shown decoded (`한글`, not `%ED%95%9C%EA%B8%80`, `displayRoute` in `src/lib/display-route.ts`) and cut to 100 characters with an ellipsis; a path that does not decode, or whose decoded form holds a control character or a character that changes the direction of the text (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+2028, U+2029, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), is shown as it came, percent-encoded. Next.js answers the status 404 and adds `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` to the page.
  - **Every non-asset dotted path and bare `/api` goes through the locale middleware and answers 404 with zero stderr.** `config.matcher` in `src/middleware.ts` skips only framework internals (`/_next/`, `/_vercel/`) and static assets (`/fonts/`, `/screenshots/`, `/favicon.ico`, `/icon.svg`, `/apple-icon.png`, `/sample.pdf`), and `isApiPath` matches `/api/...` (while `isLocalePrefixedApiPath` answers 404 on `/<locale>/api` and `/<locale>/api/...`). Every non-asset dotted path (`/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/foo.html`, `/.env`, `/.git/config`, `/wp-login.php`) and bare `/api` goes through `pageLocaleAnswer`, is rewritten under the locale, and is answered 404 by `src/app/[locale]/[slug]/page.tsx` or `src/app/[locale]/[...rest]/page.tsx` with `noindex`, the localized 404 page title, and zero `Error: Internal: NoFallbackError` stack lines on stderr (`export const dynamicParams = false` in `src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx` locks the static pages under `[locale]` to the supported locales).
  - **A path of two or more segments retitles nothing after load.** `src/app/[locale]/[...rest]/page.tsx` exports `generateMetadata`, which calls `notFound()` as the page does. Without it the layout's metadata (the home page's title) travelled in the flight payload the browser hydrates from, and the tab read "EasyConvert | Online File Converter" once the page had loaded, though the server's head held the 404 title.
  - **The body of the 404 page is rendered in the browser under this framework version (Next.js 15.5.28).** The HTML of a 404 holds the status, the title and the robots tag, and the page body comes in the flight payload: the framework's top-level catch takes the document's body for a not-found raised below the layout, and a plain `<h1>` as the not-found page and an empty metadata gave the same result when tried. It is the framework's behaviour, not this change's, and nothing is planned for it.
- **Why**:
  - **The reference answers it so.** Measured with `curl -A "Mozilla/5.0"` on 2026-11-03. 404: `/nonexistent-page-xyz`, `/foo-converter`, `/foo-to-bar`, `/pdf-to-foo`, `/pdf-to-any`, `/video-to-mp4`, `/image-to-pdf`, `/word-to-pdf`, `/mp3-to-pdf`, `/docx-to-mp3`, `/jpg-to-jpeg`, `/docx-to-docx`, `/txt-to-txt`, `/htm-to-html`, `/ocr`, `/ocr-pdf`, `/dpa`, `/acceptable-use`, `/merge-jpg`, `/merge-docx`, `/compress-gif`, `/word-converter`, `/excel-converter`, `/powerpoint-converter`, `/photo-converter`, `/picture-converter`, `/music-converter`, `/PDF-to-JPG` and `/ko/jpg-to-pdf`. 200: `/jpeg-to-jpg`, `/jfif-to-jpg`, `/tif-to-tiff`, `/aif-to-aiff`, `/mp4-to-mp4`, `/pdf-to-pdf`, `/png-to-png`, `/jpg-to-jpg`, `/tgz-to-tar.gz`, `/jpg-to-pdf`, the converter pages of 11 categories, `/pdf-ocr`, `/compress-pdf`, `/compress-png`, `/compress-jpg`, `/merge-pdf`, `/website-png-screenshot`, `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/security`. The pair rule is the registry's own list: the reference serves `/jfif-to-jpg` and not `/jpg-to-jfif`, `/tif-to-tiff` and not `/tiff-to-tif`, `/jpg-to-jpg` and not `/docx-to-docx`, which is what "the registry lists the conversion" gives. Its 404 page is a thin header with the logo, a small red `404`, a heading that names the route and one sentence, with no navigation and no footer; its `/data-converter` is 404 because it has no data formats, which the registry here has, so the page stays. Its URLs are case-sensitive and ours are lowercased (entry 139), which this entry leaves as it is.
  - **A soft 404 costs crawl budget and ranking.** Until now any slug (`/dpa`, `/foo-converter`, `/pdf-to-any`) rendered a converter page with status 200 and a `noindex` tag; a search engine fetched each, and a link from anywhere made it a page. A 404 is the answer a crawler and a visitor both read at once, and it is what a removed page returns.
  - **A converter page that converts nothing is a broken promise.** `/mp3-to-pdf` and `/video-to-mp4` showed an upload card for a conversion the registry does not offer, so a visitor uploaded a file and met a refusal. The page now exists only where the registry lists the conversion.
  - **One rule in one place.** Before, the same decision was spread over the parser (`generic`), an indexability predicate, a file-slug predicate, the OCR aliases and the view's fallbacks; each time a new class of path appeared, one of them lagged.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Pages leave the index.** Every converter page of a name the registry does not know, every `<format>-to-any` page (one indexable self-canonical copy for each registered format), the many-to-one category pairs (`/video-to-mp4`), the OCR aliases and the unlisted conversions now answer 404, and an inbound link to one is a dead link. The pairs were pages of conversions the registry does not offer, or copies of another page; the pages that people converted with are unchanged. Search impressions on the converter pages are watched after launch, and a removed pair that people search for is answered by adding its conversion to the registry, not by a page of its own.
  - **A typo in the address is a 404 page, not a converter page.** The 404 page has the logo linked to the home page, so a visitor reaches the home page from it; it has no navigation, search box or footer, as the reference's has none.
  - **`/word-to-pdf`, `/image-to-pdf` and the like no longer work**, though people may type them; `/docx-to-pdf` and `/jpg-to-pdf` do. The home page's source chips and format catalog lead people to the registered names.
  - **The middleware matcher lists the static asset prefixes and root files of `public/` and `src/app/`** (`/fonts/`, `/screenshots/`, `/favicon.ico`, `/icon.svg`, `/apple-icon.png`, `/sample.pdf`), held in sync with `public/` by `tests/i18n-routing.test.ts`, so any other dotted path goes through the locale middleware and answers 404 from the slug or catch-all page without triggering `NoFallbackError` on `src/app/[locale]/page.tsx`.
  - **The utility formats are a short list, each read from the operation behind it** (`merge` takes `MERGE_FORMATS` that the registry converts to themselves, so only `pdf`; `compress` takes `OPTIMIZABLE_FORMATS`, so only `pdf`). The reference also serves `/compress-png`, `/compress-jpg` and `/compress-jpeg`, and they are 404 here: the job graph has an optimiser for PDF alone, and a page "Make PNG files smaller online" would claim a utility the service does not run. A format gets its compress page when its optimiser is added to `OPTIMIZABLE_FORMATS`, with no change to the parser.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **A soft 404 with noindex** (the status quo): it answers 200 to a crawler, keeps every path a live page and lets a link make one; the reference does not do it.
  - **A redirect of an unknown path to the home page**: it hides the mistake, and a crawler reads a redirect of every junk URL as a soft 404 as well; a visitor who typed `/pdf-to-wrod` would land on the home page with no sign why.
  - **A 404 decided in the middleware**: it would repeat the parser's rule ahead of the page and need the registry in the edge runtime; the page already knows the answer from the one parser.
  - **Skipping all non-`tar.<suffix>` dotted paths in the middleware matcher**: single-segment dotted paths (`/robots.txt`, `/foo.html`, `/wp-login.php`, `/.env`) bypassed the locale rewrite, hit `src/app/[locale]/page.tsx` with `locale` set to the filename, and logged a 3-line `Error: Internal: NoFallbackError` stack on stderr for every request.
  - **Keeping `/video-to-mp4` and the other many-to-one category pairs** (entry 139): the reference answers them 404, and a pair page of a word that is not a format could not name its formats without a second rule for the word.
  - **Keeping the six synonym words** (`word-converter`, `photo-converter` and the rest): the registry has no such category, the reference answers each 404, and no link led to them.
- **Verified by**: `tests/unknown-path-404.test.ts` (the slug page and its metadata answer 404 in English and under `/ko` for each class of path above, a name every object has, a path with a dot and a path with whitespace around it included, and 200 for each page that exists; the catch-all page and its metadata answer 404; `LocaleLayout` exports `dynamicParams = false` and answers 404 for unknown locales; a name that Unicode lowercases to a page name (the Kelvin sign in `lbs-to-Kg`) is 404; the merge and compress pages exist exactly for the formats of their job graph operation that satisfy `isSelfConvertible`; the route of the 404 page is shown decoded, raw for a path that does not decode or holds a control or direction character, and cut at 100 characters; the parser, swept over the registry's own `targetFormats` and `isSameFormat`, finds a page for every conversion the registry lists between two format names, exactly that many, reads each conversion between two names of one format as the page of its source (`tar.bz-to-tar.bz2`, `tbz-to-tar.bz2` included), and names a registered source for every page that is not an information page, which is why `ConverterPageView` keeps no fallback for an unregistered source; the 404 page reads its code, heading naming the route and sentence in both languages under a thin header that holds the logo link alone, with no footer; its metadata titles it as not found), `tests/not-found-theme.test.ts` (`themeFor` and the mounted 404 page are dark for a stored dark theme and for none with a dark system, and light for a stored light theme whatever the document started as and for none with a light system), `tests/built-statuses.test.ts` and `scripts/check-built-statuses.mjs` (the check of a running `next start` server across 37 paths: 404 with noindex and the localized 404 title read from `messages/*.json` for a junk slug, a multi-segment path, a whitespace-padded path with and without a language prefix, `/robots.txt`, `/foo.html`, `/wp-login.php`, `/.env`, `/.git/config`, `/api` and `/ko/robots.txt`; 400 Bad Request for malformed percent escapes `/%E0%A4%A`, `/ko/%E0%A4%A`, `/en/%E0%A4%A`, `/pdf-to-jpg%E0%A4%A`, `/%c0%ae%c0%ae/etc` and `/ko/%c0%ae`; no 404 document names the title of the layout anywhere, the flight payload included; 200 for `/pdf-to-jpg`, `/ko/pdf-to-jpg` and the routes of the app (`/dashboard/api-keys`, `/api-docs`, `/status`, `/unit-converter`, `/auth`), 307 for `/account`, and 404 for each of those routes with `/x` after it, with 0 `NoFallbackError` or `URIError` lines written to stderr on `next start`; run by `scripts/boot-web-image.sh` on the web image before any tag is pushed), `tests/i18n-routing.test.ts` (the rewrite keeps a path with whitespace as it came and sets `X-NEXT-INTL-LOCALE`, under a prefix in any case as well; malformed percent escapes pass through without throwing; non-asset dotted paths and `/api` are rewritten under the locale while every file in `public/` and the root metadata icons are skipped by `config.matcher`; the canonical and alternates of each page, the copies of a format page), `tests/internal-links.test.ts` (every link of the header, the footer, the home page, the converter page of each registered format and category, the pair and utility pages, and the tables behind the home page's chips, popular conversions and directory leads to a route of the app or to a slug the parser reads as a page; red with the footer link `/video-to-gif` and with the related list of a page offering `presentation-to-pdf`), `tests/slug-copy.test.ts` and `tests/redesign-verification.test.ts` (the intros and pages of the pairs and categories that remain), `tests/i18n-client-messages.test.ts` (the 404 page carries only the header's messages).
- **Revisit when**: the registry gains a conversion people search for under a removed name, search impressions of the removed pages show a loss the reference does not have, the reference opens a page this entry answers 404 (it is measured again before a page is added), a utility gains another format, or the 404 page needs more than the logo link.

## 146. The terms, the privacy policy, the data processing terms and the acceptable use policy are written from law and reference research, not reviewed by counsel, and sign-up and API key creation record the accepted terms version

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #901), decided 2026-11-03 (QA decision of 2026-10-30: the legal review is done by research in the issue, not handed to QA).
- **Decision**:
  - **Four pages, each with its own route.** `/terms`, `/privacy`, `/dpa` and `/acceptable-use`, in English and Korean, each with its version date above the title and a table of contents beside the sections. The texts are the Markdown files of `docs/legal/`, which the build imports as text (`src/lib/legal/texts.ts`); `docs/legal/SOURCES.md` cites the source of every clause. The terms and the privacy policy were info pages of the converter slug route; they are removed from that table.
  - **The texts come from research, not from counsel.** They follow the Personal Information Protection Act and its decree as in force on 2026-11-03, the regulator's drafting guideline for privacy policies (2026-04 revision), GDPR articles 13, 14 and 28, the Information and Communications Network Act, the Act on the Regulation of Terms and Conditions and the Copyright Act, checked against the published pages of a comparable conversion service.
  - **Acceptance is recorded with the version, not a flag, and only when the request carries it.** Sign-up and API key creation require `acceptedTermsVersion` equal to the current version (`TERMS_VERSION`, the date the four pages share) and store it on the account or the key. An earlier version, which a page loaded before the terms changed sends, is refused with 400 `terms_outdated`, which the interface words as "reload the page"; anything else with 400 `terms_not_accepted`. The sign-up form and the dashboard's key form each have a required "I accept the terms of service" box. A sign-in with Google keeps the version in its state only when it is the one in force, refuses an earlier one at its start with `terms_outdated`, and creates an account only with the version in force; otherwise it returns to sign-up with `terms_required` (or `terms_outdated` when the terms changed during the sign-in). Both stores keep JSON records, so no migration is needed.
  - **Accounts and keys made before the terms are given notice, not asked to accept.** Their records carry no version, and nothing blocks them; the terms are published on the site and changes are announced there (terms section 9).
  - **The processors are named.** The privacy policy and the data processing terms name the hosting provider, the CDN and the sign-in provider, because the law requires the recipients of a processing to be named. The rule that keeps service names out of repository text does not apply to these legally required lists.
  - **Requests and reports go to `support@aquilaxk.site`.** The contact page and the texts show it. Cloudflare Email Routing forwards it to the operator's own mailbox and keeps no copy, so the privacy policy and the processing terms name that route as a processing by Cloudflare. The four pages share one version constant, since they cite each other's sections.
- **Why**:
  - **Routes and not sections.** The comparable service carries its acceptable use rules inside its terms and offers a processing agreement on request from its security page; it has no `/dpa` or `/acceptable-use`. Issue #901 asks for the four routes, the acceptable use policy has to state the measures against infringing content in advance (Network Act 44-2(5)) and the processing terms have to carry the clauses of GDPR 28(3) in writing (28(9)), so each is a page of its own that the terms include. The layout of each page (date above the title, introduction, contents beside the sections) follows the comparable service.
  - **A version instead of a checkbox flag.** A stored version proves which text was accepted when the terms change, which a boolean cannot.
  - **One source of the text.** The page renders the file that `SOURCES.md` cites, so the published text and the cited text cannot drift.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Not reviewed by counsel.** A clause can be wrong in a way research does not show. This is a known risk, accepted for the free launch.
  - **The operator is named, with an e-mail address and no telephone number.** The privacy officer and controller is named with `support@aquilaxk.site`, which replaces an address on a domain with no mail exchanger (QA decision 2026-11-03).
  - **The operator's mailbox provider is not named.** If the mailbox is a hosted service, it receives the messages as a processor; QA decides whether to name it. Contact messages have no deletion period yet.
  - **No EU representative.** GDPR 27(2)(a) exempts occasional processing without special categories that is unlikely to result in a risk; the service is free and not directed at the EU market. To be revisited with counsel.
  - **A user on a page loaded before a terms change must reload to sign up or to create a key.** The old version is refused with its own code.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Acceptable use and processing terms as sections of the terms page.** Follows the comparable service's placement but not issue #901, and makes the processing terms hard to hand to a business customer.
  - **Texts in the messages files.** Two copies (the docs and the messages) would drift.
  - **Recording acceptance without a request field.** The server would record a version the user may never have seen; the first version of this change did so for API keys.
  - **Asking accounts made before the terms to accept them at their next sign-in.** No account depends on the service yet, and a forced prompt blocks API clients that cannot answer it.
- **Verified by**: `tests/legal-pages.test.ts` (each page in each language shows its version date and title, its contents links land on its sections, its links reach existing pages, its route names its path as canonical, the texts are the files of `docs/legal/`, the web image copies them before the build, and the footer links every page with the privacy policy in bold), `tests/legal-acceptance.test.ts` (sign-up and sign-in with Google store the version, a sign-up without the current version is refused and creates nothing, and a new key stores the version; a key without a version or with an earlier one is refused and none is made; a Google start with an earlier version answers `terms_outdated`), `tests/legal-acceptance-ui.test.ts` (the sign-up form, the sign-up with Google and the dashboard key form send the version only once the box is ticked), `tests/legal-values.test.ts` (every number the texts state is the value of the code, and the two languages have the same sections, list items and table rows), and the four pages answering 200 in English and Korean on a production build.
- **Revisit when**: paid plans are prepared (#902: the business identity of the e-commerce act, payment and refund terms, the payment processor), a regulator or a user asks, a processor is added or replaced (update the lists 30 days before), QA names the mailbox provider or a deletion period for contact messages, or counsel reviews the texts.

## 147. An ended conversion job drops its inline input and webhook secret at once, and is removed with its dead letter 25 hours after it ended; a failed webhook delivery is kept 30 days with its secret encrypted; an account is erased on request by one command

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #901 and #665), decided 2026-11-04.
- **Decision**:
  - **An ended job keeps only what its answers need.** A conversion job is queued with `removeDataOnFinish: ['inputBufferBase64', 'webhookSecret']`; when it completes, fails, is cancelled or is failed by the stalled sweep, the stored job and its dead letter drop those keys. The attempt and the listeners of its end keep them in memory, so the completed or failed webhook is still signed. The stored data is read again for this, not taken from the attempt, whose copy the processor may have changed.
  - **An ended job is removed 25 hours after it ended.** The jobs are queued with `removeOnComplete` and `removeOnFail` set to `{ age }`, BullMQ's KeepJobs: when a job ends, the jobs of its end state that ended more than `age` seconds ago are removed, with their entry in the index of their user, and for failed jobs the dead letters recorded before that time. The age is `RESULT_UNDELIVERED_TTL_SECONDS` plus a day (`GONE_RECORD_MS`): while the result can be downloaded, and then while a download of the deleted result answers 410, both of which need the job to tell who owns the result. A sweep every 5 minutes (`sweepEndedRecords`, BullMQ's `Queue.clean` with the same grace) covers a queue that goes quiet, cancelled jobs and jobs queued before the option existed. A job of several steps drops its webhook secret and sets its keys to expire after the same time when it ends.
  - **A failed webhook delivery is kept 30 days, its secret encrypted.** The secret is stored as the key store stores it (AES-256-GCM, `encryptSecret`), and a replay decrypts it. An entry is neither listed nor replayed after 30 days from its failure, and the sweep removes it.
  - **An account is erased by `node dist/erase-account.js` in the worker container** (docs/deploy-oci.md, "Deleting an account"). It lists by default and deletes with `--apply`: the account's jobs (live ones cancelled first, BullMQ's `Queue.remove`, which refuses an active job), their stored files through the retention ledger, its API keys and their webhook secrets, its dead letters, its counts and every Redis key tagged with its id, and the account record last, only once no job is left.
- **Why**:
  - **The privacy policy promises it.** It says that file content goes minutes after the conversion and that signing secrets are encrypted at rest; a job record kept the inline input (up to 32 MiB) and the plaintext secret with no expiry, and a dead letter kept the plaintext secret forever.
  - **The engine's own semantics.** `{ age }` follows BullMQ's KeepJobs (`src/interfaces/keep-jobs.ts`; `moveToFinished-14.lua` and `includes/removeJobsByMaxAge.lua`, which remove the ended jobs older than `timestamp - age * 1000` when a job finishes), and the sweep is BullMQ's `Queue.clean(grace, limit, type)`, which the engine already had.
  - **30 days for dead letters.** Webhook delivery services keep a failed delivery for a manual redelivery for 2 to 90 days; 30 days is within that range, and the download link a letter carries expires long before.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **A job's record and its account's history last 25 hours after the job.** After that the job answers 404, and a download of its deleted result answers 404 instead of 410.
  - **The first sweep removes ended jobs older than 25 hours that were stored before this change.** This is the retention taking effect; no migration step is needed.
  - **The removal at the end of a job scans the set of its end state.** The engine keeps ended jobs in sets, not in a sorted set by end time as BullMQ does; a scan per ended job is cheap at the present volume and would need a sorted index (a data layout change) at a much larger one.
  - **A job queued before this change keeps its inline input and secret until it is removed.** The option is stored with the job, and a job lives at most 25 hours after it ends.
  - **The in-process queue keeps the data of an ended job.** It shares one job object with its worker and listeners, and it serves development only.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **A Redis expiry on the job hash.** The ids would stay in the state sets and the user index without their hash, and the counts would be wrong.
  - **Dropping the keys inside the Lua transition with `cjson`.** Re-encoding the data changes it (an empty array becomes an object).
  - **Dropping the secret from a dead letter.** A replay needs it.
  - **Removing a job when its result goes.** A download of the deleted result could no longer tell its owner that it was deleted.
- **Verified by**: `tests/job-record-retention-redis.test.ts` (the data dropped at each end, kept while retried, the age removal of completed and failed jobs and their dead letters, `clean` of cancelled jobs, a conversion job's webhook still signed after its secret was dropped, and the sweep removing a job no later job removes), `tests/queue-keep-jobs.test.ts` (KeepJobs in the in-process queue), `tests/job-graph-redis-e2e.test.ts` (an ended graph empties its secret and its keys expire), `tests/webhook-dlq-retention.test.ts` (the sealed secret, a replay signed with it, the 30 days), `tests/erase-account.test.ts` (the plan changes nothing, the erasure removes every family of one account and nothing of another, and in Redis mode every key tagged with its id).
- **Revisit when**: the volume makes the scan of the ended sets slow (move them to a sorted index with a migration), the result retention changes (the age follows it), or a dead letter needs a longer life for a business customer.

## 148. The nightly regression corpus runs on eight shards, divides per-page OCR concurrency across worker processes, normalizes single-page leaf PDF catalogs, and records empty inputs in the regression manifest

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #655 and #671), decided 2026-11-05. Amended 2026-11-06 (regression corpus run 42206606493): the page budget of a job server grows by the parallelism it gives up.
- **Decision**:
  - **Eight shards in the nightly regression corpus workflow.** `.github/workflows/regression-corpus.yml` and `bench/realworld/regression/schedule.ts` raise `NIGHTLY_SHARDS` (`SHARDS.nightly`) from `4` to `8`, so each Monday-to-Saturday run partitions the daily seventh of the corpus plus the canary across eight 60-minute shards instead of four.
  - **Per-worker OCR page and band concurrency bounded by host CPUs.** `childOcrPageConcurrency(workers, cpus)` in `bench/realworld/pool.ts` computes `Math.max(1, Math.floor(cpus / Math.max(1, workers)))` and passes `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY` to each forked worker process unless the caller already set it. `ocrPageConcurrency(poolCapacity)` in `src/lib/conversions/ocr-page-batch.ts` clamps `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY` to `[1, Math.min(poolCapacity, OCR_MAX_INFLIGHT_PAGES)]`, and `src/lib/conversions/ocr.ts` disables intra-page band splitting (`bandsAllowed`) when `concurrency <= 1` and bounds `planPageBands` by `ocrPageConcurrency()`.
  - **The OCR page budget of a job server grows by the parallelism it gives up.** `childOcrPageBudgetMs(workers, cpus)` in `bench/realworld/pool.ts` multiplies the page budget of the converter (`OCR_PAGE_BUDGET_MS`, `10` s, `src/lib/conversions/ocr-work-budget.ts`) by `ceil(OCR_MAX_INFLIGHT_PAGES / childOcrPageConcurrency(workers, cpus))` (`4` for 3 workers on 4 vCPUs) and passes it as `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_BUDGET_MS` to each forked job server unless the caller set it; `scaledDeadlineMs` takes the same budget (`JobPool.ocrPageBudgetMs`) so that the deadline of a job that is read by OCR follows it. The converter's default is not changed.
  - **Single-page leaf PDF catalog normalization.** `normaliseLeafPageCatalog` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-page-geometry.ts` wraps a catalog whose `/Pages` entry is a single `/Type /Page` leaf (`PDFPageLeaf` without `/Kids`, such as `cc-2800657.pdf`) in a 1-kid `PDFPageTree` (`/Type /Pages /Kids [pagesRef] /Count 1` with `/Parent` on the leaf) right after `PDFDocument.load`, so `readPdfPageFrames`, `createLosslessSandwichPdfFromPdf`, and `JpegCatalog` all traverse the page without throwing, while any other non-page-tree `/Pages` entry (including a `/Type /Page` dictionary that also carries `/Kids`) is refused.
  - **Verified empty inputs recorded and preserved in the regression manifest.** `bench/realworld/regression/manifest.ts`, `scripts/regression-corpus-manifest.ts`, and `bench/realworld/regression-manifest.json` serialize, parse, and carry forward `emptyInputs` across `select` runs when a file's `sha256` is unchanged, marking `cc-6200151.pdf` (a 1-page `/Subtype /3D` `U3D` annotation PDF whose page content stream is 0 bytes and has no extractable 2D text or raster content).
- **Why**:
  - **Halve per-shard nightly work and prevent CPU oversubscription.** A nightly run with 3 worker processes on a 4-vCPU runner previously allowed each worker to run up to 4 concurrent OCR pages or intra-page bands (up to 12 concurrent Tesseract workers), causing severe contention and shard timeouts; giving each of the 3 workers `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY=1` and doubling `NIGHTLY_SHARDS` to `8` keeps each shard well within the 60-minute limit.
  - **Support real-world single-page leaf catalogs across `pdf-lib` callers.** `cc-2800657.pdf` points `/Root /Pages` directly at its single `/Type /Page` dictionary (`4 0 R`, `/MediaBox [0 0 842 1191] /Rotate 90`); normalizing the catalog into a 1-kid `PDFPageTree` lets `doc.getPages()`, `doc.getPageCount()`, and `doc.save()` work uniformly in `readPdfPageFrames`, `createLosslessSandwichPdfFromPdf`, and `JpegCatalog`.
  - **Judge verified 3D-only empty PDFs as expected empty refusals.** `cc-6200151.pdf` contains only a `/Subtype /3D` `U3D` stream with an empty appearance dictionary and a 0-byte page content stream, so `pdftotext` and `pdfimages` extract nothing and `pdftoppm` renders a blank white page; recording it in `emptyInputs` lets the corpus runner expect `empty_input` refusal per policy #124 and #671.
  - **The converter's OCR time limit is about the pace of a production worker, and the job servers of the corpus run were slowed to a third of that.** The four OCR refusals of run 42206606493 (`cc-4400051.pdf` to HOCR, `cc-4600613.pdf` to PDF, `cc-6600788.pdf` to ALTO, `cc-6200064.pdf` to EPUB) came with #960, which gave each job server one page at a time and no bands: the same files converted on the 2026-11-01 run in 29.2, 44.7, 95.8 and 93.7 s against budgets of 70, 70, 130 and 280 s, and now ran out of them. Nothing in the OCR code changed in between (`ocr-work-budget.ts`, `ocr.ts` apart from the concurrency switch of #960). Measured on one host with `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY` unset and set to 1: 15.8, 14.7, 9.1 and 37.7 s against 37.2, 26.1, 24.5 and 128.3 s, 1.8 to 3.4 times as long, which on a shared runner passes the budget. A refusal for the pace of the harness is no finding about the file.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Four additional matrix jobs on Monday-to-Saturday regression corpus runs.** Eight nightly shards run instead of four, trading CI matrix slots for half the wall-clock time per shard.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Raising `OCR_PAGE_BUDGET_MS` for every caller.** The budget bounds a production worker, which has the cores; only the corpus run takes them away.
  - **Taking the OCR refusals as known failures.** The list holds crash, hang and bad-output verdicts only, and a refusal for the pace of the harness would hide a real one on the same files.
  - **Auto-accepting empty outputs on `pdf -> txt` or `pdf -> md`.** Violates policy #124 and #671, which require an explicit refusal unless the input is a verified empty corpus file.
  - **Hard-coding `OCR_MAX_INFLIGHT_PAGES = 1` globally.** Would serialize multi-page OCR even for a single worker process on a multi-core host.
- **Verified by**: `tests/realworld-corpus.test.ts` (the budget by the share of the cores and the deadline by it), `tests/pdf-page-frames-root.test.ts`, `tests/ocr-pdf-concurrency.perf.test.ts`, `tests/regression-corpus-manifest.test.ts`, `tests/regression-corpus-manifest-real.test.ts`, `tests/regression-corpus-workflow.test.ts`, and `tests/realworld-corpus.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: nightly shard duration approaches 35 minutes on `ubuntu-latest` or runner vCPU counts change.

## 149. Zero-downtime `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` rotation with lazy rehash and PDF/A-1b `/Info` and XMP timestamp synchronisation

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #761, #582, and #443), decided 2026-11-05 (QA request).
- **Decision**:
  - **Zero-downtime API key pepper rotation via `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS`.** `src/lib/config/schema.ts` adds the optional secret `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` (minimum 32 characters when non-empty, or omitted/empty), and `deploy/oci/env-allowlist.txt` and `docker-compose.prod.yml` pass `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` through to the web service. `src/lib/api-keys/key-store.ts` (`hashApiKeySecret`, `apiKeyHashCandidates`, `KeyStore.verifyApiKey`, `KeyStore.migrateKeyHash`, `KeyStore.rotateApiKey`, `KeyStore.updateApiKey`) and `src/lib/api-keys/redis-key-store.ts` (`RedisKeyStore.verifyApiKey`, `RedisKeyStore.recordVerifiedKeyInRedis`, `RECORD_VERIFIED_KEY_LUA_SCRIPT`, `RedisKeyStore.deleteApiKey`) verify incoming API keys against `HMAC-SHA256(KEY_HASH_PEPPER, secret)` first, fall back to `HMAC-SHA256(KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS, secret)` and legacy `SHA-256(secret)`, and atomically migrate the Redis hash index (`apikey_hashes` and `apikeys:<id>`) and in-memory `keyHashIndex` on a non-grace hit.
  - **Symmetric webhook secret decryption fallback and re-encryption.** `getDecryptionCandidateKeys`, `decryptSecret`, and `reencryptSecretIfNeeded` in `src/lib/api-keys/secret-encryption.ts` attempt AES-256-GCM decryption with the primary key (`KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `KEY_HASH_PEPPER`, or `JWT_SECRET`) first and fall back to distinct keys derived from `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS`, `JWT_SECRET`, and the non-production development salt, while `encryptSecret` seals with the active primary key and `verifyApiKey`, `rotateApiKey`, and `updateApiKey` re-encrypt any fallback-decrypted `webhookSecret` under the active primary key before persisting.
  - **`/Info` and XMP timestamp synchronisation for `pdfa-1b`.** `normalisePdfADates` (`parsePdfDate`, `parseXmpDate`, `formatPdfDate`, `formatXmpDate`) in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/pdfa-dates.ts` is called by `convertToPdfA` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/pdfa.ts` and `postProcessNativePdf` in `src/lib/conversions/dispatch.ts` before `verifyPdfA` when `conformance === 'pdfa-1b'`. When LibreOffice 24.2 on Ubuntu 24.04 exports documents without `docProps/core.xml` timestamps to PDF/A-1b (`SelectPdfVersion=1`) and writes `<xmp:CreateDate>0000-00-00T00:00:00+HH:MM</xmp:CreateDate>` in XMP while writing the export timestamp to `/Info /CreationDate`, or when PDF 1.4 `/Info` timestamps omit an explicit timezone offset, `normalisePdfADates` reconciles the `/Info` and XMP timestamps, rewrites uncompressed `/Metadata` XMP packets in place by adjusting `<?xpacket` padding so no object or xref offset moves when `/Info` already carries valid timezone-qualified dates, and preserves the `%PDF-1.4` header when falling back to `doc.save({ useObjectStreams: false })`.
- **Why**:
  - **Prevent global API key and webhook outage on secret rotation.** Rotating `KEY_HASH_PEPPER` without a previous-pepper verification and decryption window immediately invalidated issued `ec_live_*` keys and broke AES-256-GCM decryption of stored `webhookSecret` ciphertexts when `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` was unset.
  - **Satisfy ISO 19005-1:2005 clause 6.7.3 (`6.7.3-1`) on bundled LibreOffice exports.** LibreOffice 24.2 writes zeroed XMP dates (`0000-00-00T00:00:00+HH:MM`) when source Office documents omit creation metadata and omits timezone offsets from `/Info` in PDF 1.4 mode unless paired with XMP, causing `verapdf --flavour 1b` to fail rule `6.7.3-1`. Synchronising `/Info` and XMP timestamps before `verifyPdfA` makes `pdfa-1b`, `pdfa-2b`, and `pdfa-3b` all pass the strict veraPDF gate.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **One extra candidate hash lookup on an unmigrated or invalid API key while `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` is set.** Once a valid key is verified after rotation, its `keyHash` and `webhookSecret` are migrated to the active primary key.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Unconditionally re-saving every `pdfa-1b` file with `pdf-lib`.** Unconditional `doc.save()` rewrites `/Info` and streams even when `/Info` already has valid timezone-qualified dates and only the uncompressed XMP packet needs in-place timestamp replacement.
  - **Rejecting `pdfa-1b` in the API schema.** Withdraws a documented ISO conformance level that callers request.
- **Verified by**: `tests/api-key-pepper-rotation.test.ts`, `tests/config-schema.test.ts`, `tests/oci-deploy.test.ts`, `tests/pdfa-1b-dates.test.ts`, `tests/pdfa-verapdf-gate.test.ts`, and `tests/dispatch-pdf-postprocess.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: LibreOffice upstream stops emitting `0000-00-00` XMP dates on `SelectPdfVersion=1` exports, or `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` becomes mandatory in production independently of `KEY_HASH_PEPPER`.

## 150. The API documentation is a written multi-topic reference generated from the OpenAPI 3.1 contract, and README format and conversion counts are enforced by a generated registry snapshot

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #467, epic #762), decided 2026-11-05 (QA request).
- **Decision**:
  - **Topic-based `/api-docs` reference backed by `buildOpenApiDocument()`.** `/api-docs` (`IntroductionGuide`) and `/api-docs/[topic]` (`quickstart`, `convert`, `jobs`, `uploads`, `downloads`, `formats`, `ocr-languages`, `archives`, `usage`) render a three-column written reference (`TopicNav`, prose + `OperationSection` + `FieldList` + `CodeBlock`, and `TableOfContents`) directly from the public operations of `buildOpenApiDocument()`. Operations serving only the web interface or account settings (`x-internal`, API key CRUD, storage credentials, and webhook dead-letter replay) are excluded from `/api-docs`, and every request sample targets the site's own origin with `$EASYCONVERT_API_KEY`.
  - **Shared synchronous conversion and inline data-URI byte bounds.** `SYNC_CONVERSION_MAX_BYTES` (`10 MiB`) and `DATA_URI_MAX_BYTES` (`5 MiB`) live in `src/lib/api/file-size-limit.ts` and are shared by `src/app/api/v1/convert/route.ts`, `src/lib/api/openapi/paths/conversion.ts`, `src/lib/api/openapi/components.ts`, and `src/components/api-docs/IntroductionGuide.tsx`.
  - **Deterministic registry stats snapshot and README drift guard.** `scripts/registry-stats.ts` (`npm run docs:generate`) computes category counts, total format counts, and directed conversion pair counts from `FORMAT_REGISTRY` (`src/lib/registry.ts`), writes `docs/generated/registry-stats.json`, and updates the `<!-- registry-stats:start -->...<!-- registry-stats:end -->` tables and headline figures in `README.md` and `README.ko.md`. `tests/readme-registry-drift.test.ts` fails if `docs/generated/registry-stats.json`, `README.md`, or `README.ko.md` drift from `FORMAT_REGISTRY`, reference non-existent `/api/...`, `/api-docs/...`, or `src/...` paths, or reintroduce stale counts or `BullMQ` claims.
- **Why**:
  - **Keep public API documentation and README claims locked to the code.** Generating operation sections from `buildOpenApiDocument()` and gating README format/pair counts against `FORMAT_REGISTRY` prevents documentation drift as formats and schemas evolve.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Adding or removing a format in `src/lib/registry.ts` requires running `npm run docs:generate`.** Caught immediately by `tests/readme-registry-drift.test.ts` in CI.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Client-side interactive API console with editable server URL and token inputs on `/api-docs`.** Clutters the reference layout and duplicates the dashboard and `curl` snippets.
- **Verified by**: `tests/api-docs-pages.test.ts`, `tests/api-docs-curl-builder.test.ts`, and `tests/readme-registry-drift.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a new public `/api/v1/*` operation is added to `buildOpenApiDocument()` (add it to `API_DOC_TOPICS` in `src/components/api-docs/topics.ts`).

## 151. LibreOffice PDF/A conversion runs asynchronously inside the process sandbox and every PDF/A output is gated on veraPDF validation

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #448 and #761), decided 2026-11-05.
- **Decision**:
  - **Asynchronous sandboxed LibreOffice execution in `convertToPdfA`.** `convertToPdfA` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/pdfa.ts` spawns `soffice` through `await executeSandboxedBinary` (`timeoutMs: SOFFICE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `cwd: workDir`, `env: { SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN: 'svp' }`, `networkIsolated: true`) instead of synchronous `resolveSandboxedCommand` + `execFileSync`, and calls `rethrowSandboxUnavailable(err)` in the catch block before mapping conversion failures to `PdfPostprocessError`.
  - **Fail-closed veraPDF validation gate across CI and the worker image.** Every PDF/A export (`pdfa-1b`, `pdfa-2b`, `pdfa-3b`, default `pdfa-2b`) from both direct Office exports (`postProcessNativePdf` in `src/lib/conversions/dispatch.ts`) and PDF-to-PDF/A Draw round-trips (`convertToPdfA` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/pdfa.ts`) requires `verapdf` (`requireVerapdf` and `verifyPdfA`), failing with `EngineUnavailableError` (HTTP 503) when `verapdf` is absent or cannot start and with `PdfAValidationError` (HTTP 422 with `profile` and `failedRules`) when any ISO 19005 rule check fails.
- **Why**:
  - **Keep the Node.js event loop responsive during PDF/A conversions.** Running `soffice` via `execFileSync` blocked the worker or web server thread for up to `SOFFICE_TIMEOUT_MS` (60 seconds), stalling health probes, timers, and concurrent requests on the same process; `await executeSandboxedBinary` yields to the event loop while enforcing the same sanitized environment, `prlimit` memory and CPU bounds, and network namespace isolation as `runVerapdf`.
  - **Propagate sandbox unavailability consistently.** Calling `rethrowSandboxUnavailable(err)` ensures that a missing Linux namespace sandbox in production surfaces as `SandboxUnavailableError` (HTTP 503) rather than being misclassified as a document-level `PdfPostprocessError` (HTTP 422).
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **None on output bytes or latency.** Process arguments, timeout (`60_000` ms), isolated profile directory (`-env:UserInstallation=file://...`), and downstream `normalisePdfADates` + `verifyPdfA` checks are unchanged.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Keeping `execFileSync` in `convertToPdfA`.** Blocks the Node.js event loop for the entire LibreOffice Draw import/export duration and bypasses `executeSandboxedBinary`'s async timeout and buffer management.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdfa-validator-execution.test.ts`, `tests/pdfa-validator-failure-detail.test.ts`, `tests/pdfa-fail-closed.test.ts`, `tests/pdf-header-offset-tools.test.ts`, `tests/pdfa-verapdf-gate.test.ts`, and `tests/pdfa-1b-dates.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: LibreOffice PDF/A conversion moves to a persistent pre-warmed worker pool or an in-process PDF/A writer replaces the Draw round-trip.

## 152. PDF page rasterization is bounded by page dimensions, `/UserUnit`, `/Rotate`, and DPI before Poppler starts (`100` MP per page, no sum over the pages of a request)

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #515 and #761), decided 2026-11-05. Amended 2026-11-06 (regression corpus run 42206606493): the `400` MP sum over the pages of a request is removed and a damaged file's page boxes are read one frame for each page object.
- **Decision**:
  - **Pre-spawn PDF page rasterization pixel budgets.** `readPdfPageFrames`, `displayedSizePoints`, `renderedSizePixels`, `assertPdfRasterPageBudget`, and `checkPdfRasterPageBudget` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-page-geometry.ts` compute the rendered pixel dimensions of each selected PDF page from its effective `/CropBox` (or `/MediaBox`), `/Rotate` quarter turn, and `/UserUnit` multiplier (ISO 32000-1 section 7.7.3.3, positive `PDFNumber`, floored at `1.0` so `/UserUnit < 1` cannot understate the unscaled `/CropBox` rasterized by `pdftoppm`) at the requested `dpi` (`Math.ceil((widthPt * Math.max(1, userUnit) * dpi) / 72)` by `Math.ceil((heightPt * Math.max(1, userUnit) * dpi) / 72)`).
  - **A per-page pixel cap, and no sum over the pages.** Every selected page must stay within `MAX_RASTER_PAGE_PIXELS` (`100_000_000` pixels, `DEFAULT_MAX_INPUT_PIXELS` in `src/lib/conversions/image-input-limit-config.ts`, or `maxInputPixels()` when lowered via `EASYCONVERT_MAX_INPUT_PIXELS`). The first version of this entry also held the sum of the pixels of all selected pages to `400_000_000`; that sum is removed. Exceeding the page cap throws `InputPixelLimitError` (HTTP 413) before `pdftoppm` is spawned in both `executePopplerRender` (`src/worker/engines.ts`) and `planPageRender` (`src/lib/conversions/pdf-page-render.ts`), and `renderPdfToImageWithPoppler` validates `resolvePdfRasterDpi(options)` (`72` to `600` DPI) before checking binary availability or spawning `pdftoppm`.
  - **A damaged file's boxes are read one frame for each page object, the CropBox first.** The raw scan that serves a file `pdf-lib` cannot load (`extractRawPdfBoxes`) groups the `/MediaBox` and `/CropBox` entries of one object (up to its `endobj`) and takes the CropBox where there is one, the MediaBox otherwise; it counted every entry as a page of its own, so a scanner's sheet (`/MediaBox [0 0 2672 4072] /CropBox [0 0 641 977]`, `cc-1200358.pdf`) was charged for the cut-away sheet, 11,134 by 16,967 pixels at 300 DPI, as a second page.
- **Why**:
  - **Prevent large-page or high-`/UserUnit` PDFs from allocating multi-gigabyte rasters inside `pdftoppm`.** An architectural PDF (`14,400` by `14,400` pt, 200 by 200 inches) or a normal page with `/UserUnit 25` rendered at `600` DPI expands to `120,000` by `120,000` (`14.4` GP) or `125,000` by `125,000` (`15.625` GP), which previously started `pdftoppm` before hitting output file or memory limits.
  - **The pages of a request are drawn one after another, so the bound is the largest page, not their sum.** `pdftoppm` draws one page at a time into one bitmap and writes it out before the next, and the OCR renderer draws one page for each call (Poppler's behaviour, read from its documented options and measured; its GPL source is not followed); pdf.js bounds the pixels of one canvas (`maxCanvasPixels`, `2 ** 25`, `web/app_options.js` and `web/pdf_page_view.js`, Apache-2.0) and never the pixels of a document; Apache PDFBox renders one page to one image with `PDFRenderer.renderImageWithDPI` on the CropBox (`pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/rendering/PDFRenderer.java`, Apache-2.0); Stirling-PDF's PDF to image caps the DPI (`maxDPI`) and reports an oversized page, one page at a time (`PdfUtils.java`, read for behaviour only: its licence is not a plain permissive one). The pages of a request are bounded by `PAGE_IMAGE_MAX_PAGES` (`500`) and the job deadline. The sum refused 28 real files that converted before it (regression corpus run 42206606493, 2026-11-06; a 29th was refused by the double count above): a 489-page spreadsheet to JPEG at 150 DPI (1.06 GP in total, 2.2 MP a page), a 137-page PDF to AZW3 at 300 DPI (1.15 GP, 8.4 MP a page).
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Large-format engineering drawings must be rendered at a lower DPI (`72` to `150` DPI) or converted to vector targets (`svg`, `dxf`).** The error message states the page number, rendered pixel dimensions, and pixel limit so callers can lower `dpi` or select a smaller page range.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **A cap on the pixels of all pages together.** No step holds the pages at once (above), so the sum bounded no memory, and its value could not separate a long ordinary document from many large pages: any figure that refuses a crafted request also refuses a real 489-page workbook. A request of many large pages is bounded by the per-page cap, the page count and the deadline.
  - **Relying only on `PPM_PAGE_MAX_BYTES` or `prlimit --as` after `pdftoppm` starts.** Wastes worker CPU and memory on pages whose geometry already proves the raster exceeds the image pixel budget.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdf-raster-page-budget.test.ts` (a 489-page document at 150 and 300 DPI, 40 A4 pages at 600 DPI, a giant page among ordinary ones, and the CropBox of a damaged file), `tests/pdf-page-rasterization.test.ts`, `tests/pdf-page-frames-root.test.ts`, and `tests/poppler-ppm-png.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: streaming tiled PDF page rendering is introduced for large-format architectural sheets.

## 153. Native-engine input pixel gates before LibRaw, LibreOffice, and FFmpeg spawn and bounded NeuQuant and 8-bit BMP palette quantization

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #572 and #761), decided 2026-11-05.
- **Decision**:
  - **Pre-decode RAW sensor pixel check (`assertRawSensorPixels`).** `convertWithNativeRaw` in `src/worker/engines.ts` calls `assertRawSensorPixels(inputPath)` in `src/worker/raw-dng-image-data.ts` (re-exported by `src/worker/raw-decoded-tiff.ts`) before spawning `dcraw_emu`, checking every TIFF IFD and `SubIFD` (`walkDirectories(reader, true)`), `ActiveArea` (`bottom - top` and `right - left`), and `DefaultScale`-stretched dimensions against `maxInputPixels()` (`100` MP default) and `RAW_SENSOR_PIXEL_BUDGET` (`64` MP) and throwing `InputPixelLimitError` (HTTP 413). Post-decode `assertWithinPixelCap` in `src/worker/raw-decoded-tiff.ts` keeps `RAW_DECODE_MAX_PIXELS` (`150` MP, `RawDecodeError`) first for non-TIFF or stubbed intermediate outputs and enforces `maxInputPixels()` and `RAW_SENSOR_PIXEL_BUDGET` before reading decoded pixels into memory.
  - **Pre-spawn LibreOffice embedded picture pixel check (`assertOfficeEmbeddedImagesWithinLimit`).** `runHeadlessOffice` in `src/worker/engines.ts` calls `assertOfficeEmbeddedImagesWithinLimit(input)` in `src/worker/office-input-checks.ts` before invoking `libreOfficePool.convert` or spawning `soffice`. For ZIP-backed Office packages (`word/media/`, `ppt/media/`, `xl/media/`, `pictures/`, `data/`, `thumbnails/`, `media/`, and entries with image extensions), each media entry is streamed through `readZipEntryBytes` with a per-document `InflateBudget(maxDocumentMediaBytes())` and checked with `assertBmpHeaderWithinLimit` (for BMP/DIB), `assertEmbeddableImageWithinLimit` (for PNG and JPEG), and `sharp(..., { limitInputPixels: false }).metadata()` + `assertInputPixels` (for WebP, GIF, and TIFF).
  - **Pre-spawn FFmpeg image and video stream pixel checks (`assertMediaImageWithinLimit`, `probeInput`, `probeStreamLayout`, `probeMediaDuration`).** `convertWithNativeFfmpeg` (`src/worker/engines.ts`) and `convertMedia` (`src/lib/conversions/media.ts`) call `assertMediaImageWithinLimit` when `isEncodedImageMediaSource(src)` holds (`gif`, `webp`, `webpvideo`, `png`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `tif`, `tiff`, `bmp`, checking BMP headers via `assertBmpHeaderWithinLimit`) and rethrow `InputPixelLimitError`. `probeInput` and `probeStreamLayout` in `src/lib/conversions/media-ffprobe.ts` and `probeMediaDuration` in `src/lib/conversions/media.ts` (called across transcode, thumbnail, and packaging routes before `options.duration` is returned) check every video stream's `width` and `height` from `readMp4Layout` and `ffprobe` against `assertInputPixels` before `ffmpeg` starts.
  - **Palette quantizer pixel budget and bounded NeuQuant training (`quantize.ts`, `image.ts`).** `quantizeNeuQuant`, `quantizeMedianCut`, `quantizeXiaolinWu`, `applyFloydSteinbergDither`, and `applyBlueNoiseDither` in `src/lib/conversions/quantize.ts` and the 8-bit/palette `bmp` branch in `src/lib/conversions/image.ts` (checked before and after decode) enforce `assertPixelBudget(width, height, QUANTIZER_PIXEL_BUDGET)` (`16` MP). `quantizeNeuQuant` caps training samples at `MAX_NEUQUANT_SAMPLES` (`100,000` via `effectiveSampleFactor = Math.max(1, sampleFactor, Math.ceil(length / MAX_NEUQUANT_SAMPLES))`, clamping the learning-rate decay factor to `30`), and `applyFloydSteinbergDither` and `applyBlueNoiseDither` cache nearest-palette lookups in a 65,536-slot direct-mapped 24-bit RGB table (`createPaletteLookup`).
- **Why**:
  - **Stop decompression bombs before external native binaries allocate multi-gigabyte rasters.** A few kilobytes of GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF/DNG, MP4, or OOXML/ODF media declaring a `15,000` by `15,000` (`225` MP) or `16,383` by `16,383` (`268` MP) canvas previously bypassed the sharp still-image gate when routed to `dcraw_emu`, `soffice`, or `ffmpeg`, and direct calls to `quantizeNeuQuant`, `quantizeMedianCut`, `quantizeXiaolinWu`, or 8-bit `bmp` output lacked the `16` MP `QUANTIZER_PIXEL_BUDGET` guard enforced on `gif` and `png`.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **ZIP-backed Office documents incur header metadata inspection on embedded media parts before `soffice` runs.** Bounded by `maxDocumentMediaBytes()` and header-only metadata reads without decoding pixels.
  - **Direct-mapped 24-bit RGB cache in `createPaletteLookup` allocates `384` KiB (`Int32Array(65536)` + `Uint16Array(65536)`) per dithering pass.** Preserves exact 24-bit RGB palette matching with zero colour aliasing.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Relying only on `prlimit --as` inside the process sandbox.** Returns a generic process crash or timeout after CPU and memory have already been spent instead of a deterministic `413` `InputPixelLimitError` with the declared dimensions and limit.
- **Verified by**: `tests/native-engine-pixel-gate.test.ts`, `tests/image-input-pixel-limit-embedded.test.ts`, `tests/image-pixel-budgets.test.ts`, and `tests/raw-native-limits.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: LibreOffice or FFmpeg exposes a native flag that enforces a maximum decoded pixel count across all input codecs and embedded media parts.

## 154. Edge OCR engine, WebAssembly core, and language data are served from SHA-256-verified first-party assets with zero third-party CDN requests

- **Status**: Implemented (issues #530 and #761), decided 2026-11-05.
- **Decision**:
  - **First-party worker, core, and traineddata options on `Tesseract.createWorker`.** `recognizeImage` in `src/lib/edge-ocr/index.ts` passes `workerPath: EDGE_OCR_WORKER_PATH` (`/_assets/ocr/7.0.0/worker.min.js`), `corePath: EDGE_OCR_CORE_PATH` (`/_assets/ocr/7.0.0`), `langPath: EDGE_OCR_LANG_PATH` (`/_assets/ocr/7.0.0/tessdata`), `gzip: false`, `workerBlobURL: false`, and `cacheMethod: 'none'` to `Tesseract.createWorker`, overriding `tesseract.js` default URLs (`node_modules/tesseract.js/src/worker/browser/defaultOptions.js:11`, `src/worker-script/browser/getCore.js:14`, `src/worker-script/index.js:130`) that otherwise fetched from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/...`.
  - **Pinned SHA-256 manifest and traineddata component table verification.** `src/lib/edge-ocr/ocr-assets.manifest.json` pins `tesseractVersion` (`7.0.0`), `coreVersion` (`7.0.0`), and the exact byte size and SHA-256 digest of `worker.min.js` and all six `tesseract-core*.wasm.js` bundles in `node_modules/tesseract.js-core/`. `loadVerifiedOcrAsset` and `verifyTraineddataBuffer` in `src/lib/edge-ocr/assets.ts` (sharing `isValidTraineddataHeader` in `src/lib/conversions/ocr-language-data.ts` with `OcrWorkerPool`) verify the byte size and SHA-256 digest of every JS/WASM asset against the manifest, bound `.traineddata` size and decompression to `MAX_TRAINEDDATA_BYTES` (`128` MiB), verify the Tesseract traineddata component offset table (`1 <= entries <= 64`, `tableEnd = 4 + entries * 8 <= bytes.length`, every non-`-1` 64-bit offset inside `[tableEnd, bytes.length)`, and at least one present component) of installed language packs resolved via `resolveOcrLanguages` and `locateLanguageData`, memoize verified assets by `(path, size, mtimeMs)`, and throw `EdgeOcrError` on any mismatch or corruption.
  - **Immutable first-party asset route and worker CSP.** `next.config.mjs` rewrites `/_assets/ocr/:version/:asset+` to `/api/ocr-assets/:version/:asset+` (`src/app/api/ocr-assets/[version]/[...asset]/route.ts`), and `isApiPath` in `src/middleware.ts` treats `/_assets/ocr/:version/:asset+` as an API path (enforcing rate-limiting and client IP trust without a locale rewrite, while routing non-asset `/_assets/...` paths through `pageLocaleAnswer` so they answer 404 cleanly). Successful asset responses carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `ETag: "sha256-<digest>"` (answering `304 Not Modified` on matching `If-None-Match`), while missing or corrupted assets fail closed with RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` (HTTP 404 or 500) and reject `Tesseract.createWorker` via `errorHandler` so `runClientEdgeOcr` either escalates to L4 or blocks in client-only mode.
  - **Transitive browser-bundle import guard.** `tests/edge-ocr-browser-imports.test.ts` walks all reachable `src/` modules from both `src/lib/edge-ocr/index.ts` and `src/lib/conversions/ocr-pdf-combiner.ts` and forbids both Node built-ins (`builtinModules` from `node:module`) and server-only native packages (`sharp`, `ioredis`, `pdfkit`, `harfbuzzjs`).
- **Why**:
  - **Eliminate third-party CDN dependencies and runtime supply-chain exposure in client-side Edge OCR.** Fetching worker scripts, WebAssembly cores, and language models from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` leaked OCR usage and requested language codes to a third-party CDN, broke air-gapped or strict-CSP environments, and lacked cryptographic digest verification before executing worker scripts.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Upgrading `tesseract.js` or `tesseract.js-core` requires updating `src/lib/edge-ocr/ocr-assets.manifest.json` and `EDGE_OCR_ASSET_VERSION`.** Enforced by `tests/edge-ocr-first-party-assets.test.ts`.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Keeping `cdn.jsdelivr.net` with Subresource Integrity.** Web `new Worker(url)` and `importScripts(url)` inside a Worker do not support HTML `integrity` attributes, so only first-party serving with server-side SHA-256 verification and `script-src 'self'` CSP enforces both origin and digest integrity.
- **Verified by**: `tests/edge-ocr-first-party-assets.test.ts`, `tests/edge-ocr-browser-imports.test.ts`, `tests/edge-ocr-fail-closed.test.ts`, and `tests/ocr-language-propagation.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: Web Workers and `importScripts()` standardize native SRI enforcement across all supported browsers.

## 155. Complete startup configuration schema coverage across literal and computed environment variables

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #564 and epic #761), decided 2026-11-06.
- **Decision**:
  - **Ten computed environment variables added to `CONFIG_SCHEMA` (`src/lib/config/schema.ts`).** `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX` (`runtime`, integer `1..INT32_MAX`), `SANDBOX_LAUNCHER` (`security`, enum `auto` or `off`, default `auto`), `VIPS_CONCURRENCY` (`limits`, integer `1..INT32_MAX`, computed default), `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY` (`limits`, integer `1..INT32_MAX`, default `4` matching `OCR_MAX_INFLIGHT_PAGES`), `FLUIDSYNTH_PATH` (`tools`, executable), `MIDI_SOUNDFONT_PATH` (`tools`, path), `LBZIP2_PATH` (`tools`, executable), `LIBDEFLATE_GZIP_PATH` (`tools`, executable), `XZ_PATH` (`tools`, executable), and `QPDF_RUNNER_LIB` (`tools`, path for `qpdf-runner --lib`) are declared in `CONFIG_SCHEMA` and generated into `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/configuration.example.env` via `npm run config:docs`.
  - **Automated source scan for computed environment variable names (`tests/config-schema.test.ts`).** Instead of maintaining a manual `computed` list, `tests/config-schema.test.ts` scans `src/` and `scripts/worker-healthcheck.js` for literal `process.env.NAME` reads and scans all `src/` files for scalar, array, and object `*_ENV`, `*_VARIABLE`, `*_ENV_VARS`, and `*_VARIABLES` initializers, direct helper calls (`resolveBinaryPath`, `readPositiveIntEnv`, `readVar`, `configuredValue`, `readIntegerSetting`), `(process.)?env['NAME']` subscript accesses, and `env.NAME` property accesses, asserting that every discovered variable is present in `CONFIG_SCHEMA`, alongside `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` secret and `EASYCONVERT_OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY` default assertions.
- **Why**:
  - **Prevent computed environment variable constants from bypassing startup validation and generated documentation.** Modules that stored an environment variable name in a module constant (`SANDBOX_LAUNCHER_ENV`, `IMAGE_THREADS_ENV`, `MALLOC_ARENA_ENV`, `OCR_PAGE_CONCURRENCY_ENV`, `QPDF_RUNNER_LIB_ENV`, `LBZIP2_ENV`, `LIBDEFLATE_GZIP_ENV`, `XZ_ENV`, `PROGRAM_PATH_VARIABLE`, `SOUNDFONT_PATH_VARIABLE`) were not matched by the literal `process.env.NAME` regex, allowing ten operational and tool variables to remain undocumented in `docs/configuration.md` and `docs/configuration.example.env` and unparsed by `parseConfig`.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Any new `*_ENV`, `*_VARIABLE`, `*_ENV_VARS`, or `*_VARIABLES` declaration or helper read in `src/` must be registered in `src/lib/config/schema.ts` and regenerated with `npm run config:docs`.** Enforced by `tests/config-schema.test.ts` and `tests/config-docs-drift.test.ts`.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Maintaining a manual list of computed environment variable names in `tests/config-schema.test.ts`.** Manual lists drift whenever a new module defines an `*_ENV` constant without updating the test.
- **Verified by**: `tests/config-schema.test.ts`, `tests/config-docs-drift.test.ts`, `tests/config-startup.test.ts`, and `tests/oci-deploy.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a new pattern for reading environment variables is introduced in `src/`.

## 156. OAuth canonical origin, webhook SSRF and redirect refusal, atomic registration rate limiting, bounded thumbnail timestamps, and DAG, LibreOffice, qpdf, and bzip2 stream hardening

- **Status**: Implemented (epic #761), decided 2026-11-06.
- **Decision**:
  - **OAuth callback state verification and canonical origin resolution (`src/app/api/auth/oauth/route.ts`, `src/lib/auth/oauth-state.ts`, `src/lib/security/origin.ts`).** `GET /api/auth/oauth` resolves its public origin via `resolvePublicOrigin(req)` (`NEXTAUTH_URL` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in production, failing closed with HTTP 500 if unset) instead of trusting raw `x-forwarded-host` or `x-forwarded-proto` headers, and verifies `state` against the single-use `easyconvert_oauth_state` cookie (`verifyOAuthStateCookie`, `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, cleared on response) before creating or signing in the user.
  - **Synchronous webhook URL validation and redirect refusal (`src/lib/webhooks/dispatcher.ts`, `src/lib/security/url-fetcher.ts`, `src/app/api/keys/route.ts`, `src/app/api/keys/[id]/route.ts`, `src/app/api/v1/jobs/route.ts`).** `assertPublicWebhookUrl` validates `webhookUrl` synchronously when an API key is created or updated and when a job is submitted (returning HTTP 400 on invalid or private/loopback/link-local targets), `dispatchWebhook` delivers via `redirect: 'manual'` and treats any `3xx` response as a delivery failure without following redirects, and `safeFetchUrl` unwraps `err.cause` so `SSRFBlockedError` thrown inside Undici's pinned connector surfaces with its typed error class instead of a generic `fetch failed` error.
  - **Atomic per-IP registration rate limiting (`src/lib/security/rate-limiter.ts`, `src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts`) and thumbnail timestamp array cap (`src/lib/api/contracts/schemas.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media-thumbnails.ts`).** `POST /api/auth/register` enforces `consumeRegistrationRateLimit` (10 requests per 15-minute window per verified client IP via atomic Redis Lua sliding window or memory fallback, answering HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`), and `options.thumbnail.at` is capped at `MAX_THUMBNAIL_TIMESTAMPS = 16` in both `ConversionOptionsSchema` (`maxItems: 16`) and `validateThumbnailRequest`.
  - **Allow-listed `libreOfficeFilter` and bounded `LibreOfficePoolManager` spawning (`src/lib/conversions/pdf-export-options.ts`, `src/lib/api/contracts/schemas.ts`, `src/worker/libreoffice-pool.ts`, `src/worker/engines.ts`, `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts`, `src/lib/jobs/graph.ts`).** `options.libreOfficeFilter` is restricted to `ALLOWED_LIBREOFFICE_FILTERS_BY_TARGET` (`writer_pdf_Export`, `calc_pdf_Export`, `impress_pdf_Export`, `draw_pdf_Export` for `pdf`; `MS Word 2007 XML`, `Office Open XML Text` for `docx`; `MS Word 97` for `doc`; `writer8` for `odt`; `Rich Text Format` for `rtf`; `Text`, `Text (encoded)`, `Text (encoded):UTF8,LF,,,false` for `txt`; `HTML (StarWriter)`, `XHTML Writer File`, `HTML (StarCalc)`, `XHTML Calc File`, `impress_html_Export`, `draw_html_Export` for `html`; `Calc MS Excel 2007 XML` for `xlsx`; `MS Excel 97` for `xls`; `calc8` for `ods`; `Text - txt - csv (StarCalc)` for `csv`; `Impress MS PowerPoint 2007 XML` for `pptx`; `MS PowerPoint 97` for `ppt`; `impress8` for `odp`; `draw8` for `odg`), validated upfront in `convertWithinImageSession`, `runHeadlessOffice`, `LibreOfficePoolManager.convert` (before acquiring a pool worker), and `validateJobGraph` (`convert` nodes), cleared on intermediate PDF page-chain steps (`withOfficePageChainLimits`), and throwing `UnsupportedOptionError` (HTTP 400) on any other string or target mismatch. `LibreOfficePoolManager` tracks `spawningWorkers` in `init()`, `acquireWorker()`, and `recycleWorker()` so concurrent spawns never exceed `maxWorkers`, and rejects queued waiters when cold or replacement worker creation fails.
  - **Allow-listed `pdf.protect` options (`src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/protect.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/index.ts`, `src/lib/jobs/graph.ts`).** `validatePdfProtectOptions` validates `permissions.print` (`none | low | full`), `permissions.modify` (`none | assembly | annotate | form | all`), `permissions.extract` / `permissions.annotate` (boolean), `keyLength` (`128 | 256`), and `userPassword` / `ownerPassword` (`<= 256` characters, no `\r`, `\n`, or `\0`) in `protectPdf`, `assertPdfPostProcessOptions`, and `validateJobGraph` (`pdf.protect` and `convert` nodes) before building the `qpdf` `@-` argument file.
  - **DAG storage key ownership, filename sanitization, `.tar.gz` extraction, response stream cancellation, and `getFormatByExtension` lookup (`src/lib/queue/graph/node-jobs.ts`, `src/lib/queue/graph/node-url-import.ts`, `src/lib/api-keys/owner-access.ts`, `src/lib/queue/graph/node-executor.ts`, `src/lib/registry.ts`, `src/lib/jobs/graph.ts`).** `nodeOutputKey` and intermediate node storage writers sanitize filenames through `sanitizeNodeOutputFilename` (preserving the file extension when truncating to 255 characters and falling back on control-only names), `resolveObjectOwnership` resolves `results/<graphId>/...` keys via `graphScheduler.getGraphState(classified.jobId)` when no single-job record exists, `DAG archive.extract` detects `.tar.gz` before `path.extname` and sanitizes entry names, `exportArtifactToUrl` cancels the response body stream (`response.body?.cancel()`) instead of buffering `response.arrayBuffer()`, and `getAvailableTargetFormats` and `checkConversion` use `getFormatByExtension` (`Object.hasOwn`) instead of indexing `FORMAT_REGISTRY` directly.
  - **Pre-decode ratio cap on `bzip2Payload` (`src/lib/conversions/archive-wrapper-sources.ts`).** `bzip2Payload` passes `unpackedBytesCap(archive.length, limits)` (`Math.min(limits.MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE, Math.max(ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR_BYTES, Math.floor(archive.length * limits.MAX_RATIO)))`) to `decompressBzip2(archive, cap)` and rethrows `DecompressionLimitError` (HTTP 413) with `unpackedBytesCapError(archive.length, limits).message`.
- **Why**:
  - **Close pre-launch authentication, SSRF, resource-exhaustion, and argument-injection gaps identified in the #761 security audit.** Unvalidated `x-forwarded-host` headers, missing OAuth `state` verification, late webhook URL checks, unbounded `options.thumbnail.at` arrays, unvalidated `pdf.protect` permission strings in `qpdf @-`, arbitrary `libreOfficeFilter` strings, and `bzip2Payload` defaulting to a `500` MiB cap before `enforceUnpackedSizeAndRatio` ran exposed the API and workers to avoidable attack surfaces.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Callers cannot pass undocumented custom LibreOffice filter names via `options.libreOfficeFilter`.** All supported Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, Math, HTML/XHTML, Text, CSV, RTF, and legacy binary Office export filters remain allow-listed per target format.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Validating `webhookUrl` only at delivery time in `dispatchWebhook`.** Accepts unusable or private webhook targets at key creation and job submission time and wastes job execution before failing webhook delivery.
  - **Relying only on post-decode `enforceUnpackedSizeAndRatio` for `bzip2Payload`.** Allows a small bzip2 bomb to allocate up to `500` MiB in memory before the `32` MiB ratio floor is checked.
- **Verified by**: `tests/oauth-and-session-redirect.test.ts`, `tests/webhook-delivery.test.ts`, `tests/safe-fetch-ssrf.test.ts`, `tests/auth-register-login.test.ts`, `tests/media-thumbnails.test.ts`, `tests/libreoffice-pool-manager.test.ts`, `tests/storage-download-access.test.ts`, `tests/pdf-watermark-protect-pdfa.test.ts`, and `tests/archive-single-stream-typed-errors.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a new target format or LibreOffice export filter is added to the conversion registry.

## 157. Fail-closed binary format signature checks, CGM and HTML table span bounds, CSS at-rule token validation, qpdf sandbox memory cap, Format 12 cmap bounds, and unified `openPackage` ZIP reading

- **Status**: Implemented (epic #761), decided 2026-11-06.
- **Decision**:
  - **Fail-closed signature checks for binary-only extensions and dedicated `.lwp`, `.wpd`, `.lrf`, `.pdb`, and `.mobi`/`.azw`/`.azw3`/`.azw4`/`.prc` signatures (`src/lib/compound-file-kind.ts`, `src/lib/format-signatures.ts`, `src/lib/registry.ts`, `src/lib/security/file-guard.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office.ts`, `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts`).** `OWN_SIGNATURE_CHECKS` in `src/lib/format-signatures.ts` registers dedicated header verifiers for `.lwp` (`WordPro\0` and `WordPro\r` at offset 0), `.wpd` (`\xFFWPC` at offset 0 or CFBF with WordPerfect 7+ root class ID `519873FF-2DAD-0220-1937-0000929679CD` via `isCompoundFileOfKind('wpd', buf)`), `.lrf` (`L\0R\0F\0\0\0` at offset 0), `.pdb` (78-byte Palm Database header with a 32-byte printable ASCII name padded with NULs when shorter than 32 bytes, `nextRecordListID === 0`, `numRecords >= 1`, no conflicting offset-0 header signature, and a recognized e-book/document `type+creator` identifier `TEXtREAd`, `DataPlkr`, `TEXtTlDc`, `zTXTGPlm`, `PNRdPPrs`, `PNRdPPr2`, `DataSprd`, or `ToGoToGo` at bytes `60..68`), and `.mobi`/`.azw`/`.azw3`/`.azw4`/`.prc` (78-byte Palm Database header with the same invariants and `BOOKMOBI` or `TEXtREAd` at bytes `60..68`), `sniffFixedSignature` also recognizes RFC 8878 Zstandard skippable frames (`0x184D2A50..0x184D2A5F`), standalone BIFF2-BIFF8 `BOF` streams (`isBiffStream`), pre-OLE2 Word binary headers (`PRE_OLE2_WORD_SIGNATURES`), and Hancom HWP 3.0 headers (`HWP Document File V3.00 \x1a\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05`), `ownSignatureVerdict` refuses `isDjvu`, `isLotusWordPro`, `isSonyLrf`, `isPalmDocPdb`, `isMobiPalmDb`, `\xFFWPC`, and non-Office CFBF kinds (`isNonOfficeCompoundFile`) under any other extension, and `src/lib/security/file-guard.ts` verifies CFBF `.wpd` directory sectors beyond the initial 64 KiB window when `.wpd` is declared and the initial window is `'unreadable'`. `isFormatCompatibleWithMagicBytes` in `src/lib/registry.ts` enforces `refusedWithoutSignature(cleanExt, buffer) || STRICT_SNIFFED_ONLY_EXTENSIONS.has(cleanExt)` for all buffers regardless of whether `buffer.length < 8`, restricts non-CFBF `'application/x-hwp'` to `.hwp`, non-CFBF `'application/msword'` to `.doc`/`.dot`, and non-CFBF `'application/vnd.ms-excel'` to `.xls`/`.xlt`, requires `sniffed === 'application/pdf'` when a signature is sniffed (and `hasPdfHeader` within the first 1,024 bytes when `sniffed` is `undefined`) for `.pdf`, maps `font/woff`, `font/woff2`, `font/otf`, and `font/ttf` only to their respective font extensions, and ends with `return false` instead of `return true`.
  - **Clear-text CGM input cap (`src/lib/conversions/vector-cad.ts`).** `parseCgmToSvg` and `convertVectorCad` (`src === 'cgm'`) enforce `MAX_CGM_INPUT_CHARS = 16 * 1024 * 1024` (`16` MiB) and throw `PayloadLimitError` (HTTP 413) when exceeded.
  - **CSS `@` token validation (`src/lib/conversions/css-references.ts`).** `CssScanner.next()` throws `ConversionFailedError('HTML CSS may not contain "@" unless followed directly by an at-rule name')` whenever an `@` outside strings, comments, and `url(...)` is not immediately followed by an identifier start (`startsIdentifier(css, this.i + 1)`), blocking `@/**/import` or `@ import` comment/whitespace splitting of `@import`.
  - **Sandbox memory limit on `qpdf` (`src/lib/conversions/pdf-postprocess/qpdf-run.ts`, `src/worker/pdf-decrypt.ts`).** `runQpdf`, `runQpdfWithPassword`, and `launchWithStdinPassword` pass `memoryLimitMb: QPDF_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB` (`512` MiB) to `launchQpdf`, and `toQpdfError` and `toDecryptError` map `SandboxedMemoryLimitError` to `PdfPostprocessError` and `ConversionFailedError(PDF_DECRYPT_TOO_LARGE_MESSAGE)`.
  - **HTML table covered-cell budget (`src/lib/conversions/html-model.ts`).** `HtmlModelBuilder` caps cumulative spanned cells (`colSpan * rowSpan - 1`) across the document at `HTML_MAX_TABLE_COVERED_CELLS = 250_000` and throws `PayloadLimitError` when exceeded.
  - **OpenType `cmap` Format 12 range and codepoint budget (`src/lib/conversions/font.ts`).** `parseCmapTable` validates every Format 12 group (`prevEndCharCode < startCharCode <= endCharCode <= 0x10ffff`, `startGlyphID + (endCharCode - startCharCode + 1) - 1 <= 0xffff`, and subtable byte bounds) and caps total mapped codepoints across the subtable at `MAX_CMAP_FORMAT12_CODEPOINTS = 262_144`, throwing `CorruptStreamError` on violation.
  - **Unified `openPackage` and shared `InflateBudget` across Office, e-book, comic, and HWPX readers (`src/lib/conversions/package-access.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office/pptx-media.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/epub-reader.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/docx-model.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/ooxml-variants.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/hwpx.ts`).** `parseAllXlsxWorksheets`, `readWorksheetCharts`, `readOdfChartPackage`, `parsePptxSlideSceneGraph`, `convertPotxSource`, `convertCbzSource`, and `assertOpenDocumentGraphic` in `src/lib/conversions/office.ts` and `isHwpxContainer` and `parseHwpxDocument` in `src/lib/conversions/hwpx.ts` open ZIP containers via `openPackage` (accepting an optional `packageKind` label) instead of raw `JSZip.loadAsync`, and `openEpubPackage`, `readDocxModel`, `ooxmlVariantAsPlainPackage`, and the Office/comic/HWPX readers share per-package `InflateBudget` instances across entry reads.
- **Why**:
  - **Eliminate permissive fallback paths and unbounded parser allocations identified in the #761 launch-blocking review.** Unsigned binary extensions (`< 8` bytes or unrecognized headers), font headers uploaded as `.pdf`, `@/**/import` in HTML `<style>`, unbounded `rowspan` maps in `HtmlModelBuilder.table`, unbounded `cmap` Format 12 ranges in `parseCmapTable`, `qpdf` invocations without `memoryLimitMb`, and direct `JSZip.loadAsync` calls without shared `InflateBudget` instances left gaps in the spoof and resource-budget gates.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Format 12 `cmap` subtables mapping more than `262,144` codepoints are rejected in the in-process subsetter.** Covers more than double the entire Unicode character repertoire (`~150,000` assigned characters across Unicode 16.0) while preventing a 16-byte group from iterating 4 billion times.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Stripping CSS comments before scanning `@import`.** Refusing any `@` not immediately followed by an identifier in `CssScanner.next()` blocks both comment-split (`@/**/import`) and whitespace-split (`@ import`) at-rules in a single linear pass without allocating a rewritten CSS string.
- **Verified by**: `tests/spoof-and-parser-bounds.test.ts`, `tests/spoof-check-variants.test.ts`, `tests/unbounded-inflate-scan.test.ts`, `tests/font-astral-cmap-format12.test.ts`, `tests/cgm-source-redos.test.ts`, and `tests/qpdf-runner-qpdf.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a new binary container format without a magic-byte signature in `sniffMimeTypeFromMagicBytes` is added to the registry.

## 158. A Hangul document written as `.doc` is the office suite's Word 97 export of the DOCX the in-process converter writes of it

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #761 follow-up), decided 2026-11-06 (nightly run 42197893883: `filet-hwp2016.hwpx` to DOC, "output bytes do not match doc").
- **Decision**:
  - **`hwp` and `hwpx` to `doc` go through the office suite.** `convertHancomDocTarget` in `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts`, called by `convertWithOfficeSuiteRoutes` in `src/worker/engines.ts`, convert the Hangul source to a DOCX with the in-process converter (the same conversion as `hwp`/`hwpx` to `docx`, which reads the text, the tables and the pictures) and have LibreOffice export that DOCX with its `MS Word 97` filter, the way every other Word document is written as `.doc`. The DOCX is not written to the output path of the request and is discarded after the export.
