  - **Why the bullet rows and not the indentation.** The indentation rule (a line more than 0.9 em right of the flow's left edge opens a paragraph) is what separated the continuation lines. Letting every line that starts where the line above starts continue it was tried and rejected: it joined the entries of a table of contents and of an index (`2.5.1 Avoid Early Obsolescence . . . 7 2.5.2 Provide ...` in one paragraph) in `gd-499819.pdf`. Tied to the start of the item's text, which only a row of this kind has, it joins the item's lines and nothing else (the real-world texts that change: 478 with the indentation rule loosened for every item, 214 once it is tied to the start of the item's text, 121 once a run must be at least half bullet items to stop being a table).
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **Word-level F1 against Poppler**: of the 1,264 real-world PDFs that read (8 more are refused as before), 121 texts change; F1 up on 7, down on 13, within 0.00005 on 101. Every drop is a running header or footer that was part of a table and is out as furniture now (`govdocs1-002667.pdf` 0.9792 to 0.9575, the 9 words of `Copyright © 2003 Fair Isaac Corporation. All rights reserved. 3` of a 3-page file; `govdocs1-003038.pdf` 0.9959 to 0.9912, `MLN Matters Number: MM3280 Related Change Request Number: 3280`; `govdocs1-002449.pdf` 0.9694 to 0.9663, the footer; `gd-499819.pdf` 0.9775 to 0.9768, the 6 footers of `© 1999 – 2002 AASHTO/ITE/EMA NTCIP 9001 v03.02 (Draft)`; `govdocs1-003280.pdf` five of the `Word-searchable version – Not a true copy` stamps (29 lines carry it on main, 24 on the change)). Poppler prints them, the layout takes recurring lines out of the text of every other file.
  - **A slide whose bullet has a heading line and a smaller line under it** (`govdocs1-002667.pdf`) reads `• Age.` and, after a blank line, `Other types of scores may consider your age, but FICO scores don't.`; before it read `•\tAge. Other types of scores may consider your age, but FICO scores don't.` as two cells. The size changes by more than 12 % and the layout opens a paragraph at a change of size, as it does for a heading above its text.
  - **The two files with a bullet that prints nothing do not change from main**: their lists stay paragraphs, each with a blank line before the next when the items are spaced by more than 1.35 line pitches (19.8 against 13.8 points in `gd-326174.pdf`), where Poppler's blocks have the items on consecutive lines.
  - **A bullet row of 3 or more segments** (a bullet, a bold lead-in and a line of text) is a row of cells as before.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Printing the left-out glyph as `•` or as U+FFFD**: a made up marker; Poppler prints nothing for it (entry 104), and entry 49 says a glyph that no table maps is left out.
  - **A bullet-aware indent for every line that starts where the one above starts**: the table-of-contents entries above.
  - **Giving the codes past the glyphs, and the codes of a non-Identity font, a range of "no text" first**: the cost above, the `usecmap` rule and the one-byte codes.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdf-layout-bullet-rows.test.ts` (a hand-written page with a header of two pieces, three bullet items one of which wraps and a line of prose: no tab, `• text` for each item, the wrapped item one line, the header a line of its own and the words equal to `pdftotext`'s; a table whose first column holds a dash stays a table; the real `gd-499819.pdf` has no `•` followed by a tab, no tab in its page header and the wrapped items whole; `gd-326174.pdf` the heading, the sentence and the items as lines with no tab; `gd-070040.pdf` the names under `California` as lines with no tab; red on origin/main for the hand-written page and `gd-499819.pdf`: 3 of 7 failed there) and `tests/pdf-text-cff-partial-tounicode.test.ts` (the three open rows, each against `pdftotext`).
- **Measured**: text of the 1,264 PDFs of the real-world corpus that read, origin/main against the change, in-process, one pass each (changed texts and F1 above). The tests with `pdf` in their file names (Mac host, `ORACLE_STRICT_MODE` off): 1,744 passed, 5 tests and the import of `tests/qpdf-runner.test.ts` failed, and the same fail on origin/main on this host (`docx-pdf-structure`, `pdf-page-render-cost`, `pdf-unicode-text-writers`, `pdf-text-geometry-bidi`, `pdf-text-geometry-layout`, `qpdf-runner`). `bench:quality -- --parity --quality-only --quick --family document` on the Linux VM (the strict run needs `epubcheck`, which is not installed on the host or the VM): parity PASS, 92 rows evaluated, 0 failing, 12 not evaluated for want of `epubcheck`. Speed, `--parity --speed-only --quick --family document --base-root` on the VM (4 cores, head against base interleaved): `pdf-text->txt` 1.0055 over 24 pairs (upper bound 1.0364), `report.docx->pdf` 0.9959 (18 pairs), `complex-script txt->pdf` 1.0096 (18 pairs); both below the reference on base as well, as the gap file records.
- **Revisit when**: a corpus file draws a printable code past the glyphs of a CFF font, a non-Identity CFF font or a map with `usecmap` and a partial map; pdf.js's CMap reader maps a range at a lower cost per code or keeps a later entry over `usecmap`; or the layout takes list items made of an unprinted glyph as a list.

## 176. A developed camera picture on its way to JPEG or WebP is taken through the exact 16-bit curve lookup and reduced to the nearest 8-bit level, not through the native 8-bit ICC transform

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #686, the rows `raw/raw-canon-r5-raw.cr3->jpg/psnr|bd_rate_psnr` and `raw/class-canoncr3->jpg/psnr|bd_rate_psnr`), decided 2026-11-07 (QA request: close the tracked Canon CR3 JPEG gap or prove its cause is outside the pipeline). It completes entry 25 for the 8-bit targets.
- **Decision**:
  - **A 16-bit picture that carries a matrix profile with sRGB primaries and a tone curve other than IEC 61966-2-1 (the curve LibRaw's `dcraw_emu -o 1` writes) is mapped through the 65,536-entry lookup of entry 25 for `jpg`, `jpeg` and `webp` too**, and the lookup writes the 8-bit level nearest to the exact value in the same pass (`applyDevelopmentCurve` in `src/lib/conversions/image-development-curve.ts`, which `preserveMetadata` in `src/lib/conversions/image.ts` calls; the tables of the last curve are kept, since a camera decoder writes the same profile for every picture). The encoder is given 8-bit sRGB samples with no profile, as before. `gif`, and a picture with an alpha plane (the camera decoder writes none), keep the native 8-bit transform.
  - **Development is unchanged**: the same `dcraw_emu -T -6 -w -o 1` run, the same size (5087 x 3391 for the CR3), the same camera white balance and the same curve as the reference. No development parameter was wrong.
- **Why**:
  - **The stages, measured on the Canon R5 CR3** (Linux VM, LibRaw's `dcraw_emu` on both sides): the development is the same file (one command, same dimensions); the product's 16-bit sRGB picture and the reference's (ImageMagick `-profile`) agree at 88.5 dB PSNR (mean absolute error 2.8e-5 of full scale); the 8-bit picture the encoder was given did not. The native ICC transform to 8-bit sRGB (LittleCMS inside the image library) differs from the nearest level of the exact value on 36 % of the samples (-1 on 27 %, +1 on 9 %), with a mean error of -0.2 to -0.3 level below level 96, +0.27 to +0.30 above level 192 and -0.18 overall. The reference's JPEG writer reduces to the nearest level. The mean level of the decoded JPEG at quality 70 against the 16-bit source (82.713): reference 82.595, product 82.365; at quality 100 with full chroma the decoded JPEG reads 49.70 dB (reference) and 48.42 dB (product) against the source before the quantiser has done anything.
  - **The encoder is not the cause.** Fed the same nearest-level picture, the product's JPEG settings (table 3, no trellis, optimal Huffman tables, overshoot deringing) read -7.2 % BD-rate in PSNR against the reference's curve and -7.3 % in SSIM; fed the 8-bit picture of the native transform they read +1.0 % in PSNR. The 0.4 level of error is a noise of the same size as the quantisation noise at quality 70 (PSNR 44.3 dB is a mean squared error of 2.4 levels squared), so it moved the curve by 9 percentage points and put the row 0.43 dB under the reference at a size 17 % smaller.
  - The row is judged on PSNR in 4:2:0 against the 16-bit picture the reference developed (`bench/families/raw.ts`), so a reduction that is half a level dark scores below one that rounds, as the entry on 16-bit reduction (`src/lib/conversions/image-depth.ts`) already found for a picture that carries no profile.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A picture with such a profile is read at 16 bits into memory once (`raw` output, 6 bytes a pixel) and the lookup writes 3 bytes a pixel: the same pass the PNG, TIFF and AVIF targets already take. On the 17.3 million pixels of the CR3 the read takes 25 ms, the lookup 30 ms and the encode 80 ms on the VM, against 309 ms for the native transform and encode in one pipeline; inside the product the whole conversion of the CR3 reads 198 ms against 192 to 199 ms (base), and a 5 megapixel picture 53 ms against 45 ms, because the native pipeline overlaps its stages on four threads and the lookup does not. The `->jpg` speed rows read 0.93 to 0.98 of the base (below).
  - The 8-bit picture no longer passes through the content classifier at 16 bits; a developed photograph is classified from its 8-bit pixels, as every JPEG source is.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Changing the JPEG settings for camera pictures** (trellis quantisation, other quantisation tables): the encoder was not behind; trellis alone reads -15 % but costs about half as much again in encode time, and nothing in the settings could return the half level.
  - **Passing the reduction to the 16-bit pipeline** (`pipelineColourspace('rgb16')` or `toColourspace('rgb16')` with the profile attached, then the rounding of entry 25's family): the first applies the profile as a gamma-2.2 picture (99.7 % of the samples wrong), the second is correct (5.8 % off by a level of rounding at the half) but takes 459 ms; the lookup is exact and takes 80 ms.
  - **A mean offset on the 8-bit output**: the error is about +0.3 in the highlights and -0.3 in the shadows, so no constant removes it.
  - **Changing the development** (white balance, matrix, demosaic, crop, highlight mode): all are the decoder's, are the same on both sides, and the 16-bit pictures agree at 88.5 dB.
- **Verified by**: `tests/icc-srgb.test.ts` (4,096 grey patches over the 16-bit range through the development curve to a JPEG at quality 100: the decoded level is the nearest one for all but under 2 % of the patches and the mean error is under 0.05; 34 % of the patches were off a level before the change) and the `raw` quality rows below.
- **Measured**: on the Linux VM (aarch64, 4 cores, the worker's one-tile libvips), `ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1 npm run bench:quality -- --parity --quality-only --family raw`: parity PASS, 355 rows, 0 failing, the four tracked rows now at parity and removed from `bench/parity-gaps.json`. `raw-canon-r5-raw.cr3->jpg`: BD-rate PSNR +1.93 % to -7.14 %, BD-rate SSIM to -7.29 %, PSNR at quality 70 44.297 dB to 44.482 dB (reference 44.735 dB, within the 0.3 dB allowance, and judged by the curve because the sizes differ), bytes 658,486 to 655,217 (reference 796,950). The other `->jpg` rows of the family, all at or above the reference in BD-rate PSNR: dng -5.20 %, arw -1.93 %, eos450d cr2 -1.47 %, eos5d3 dng -3.42 % and -5.73 %, d90 nef -5.88 %, d70 nef -5.56 %, olympus -7.72 %, panasonic -5.73 % and -6.75 %, pentax pef -9.73 % and dng -8.26 %, fuji -10.77 %, sony arw -5.92 %, g1 -7.16 %, r6 cr3 -4.11 %, apple dng -4.08 %, samsung dng -5.36 %.
  Speed, `--parity --speed-only --family raw --base-root` on the same VM (head against base interleaved, 12 rows): parity PASS, 0 failing. The `->jpg` rows, head against base: `dng` 0.928 over 240 pairs (upper bound 0.950), `arw` 0.932 over 30 pairs, `raw-canon-eos5d3-compress.dng` 0.976 over 18 pairs; against the reference they read 10.27 against 10.79 MB/s, 33.2 against 29.1 and 15.9 against 15.7. The png, avif and gif rows read 0.98 to 1.07 of the base. A first version that wrote the lookup back as a 16-bit picture and let the encoder round it read 0.84 to 0.87 on the three `->jpg` rows and failed the gate (more than 10 % slower than the base); writing the nearest level directly and keeping the tables of the last curve brought it to the figures above.
- **Revisit when**: the image library's ICC transform rounds 16-bit input to 8 bits to the nearest level; or a development curve other than a matrix profile with sRGB primaries reaches an 8-bit target (it takes the native transform, as `gif` does).

## 177. The convert routes answer an error by its class and never by the words of its message, the batch route answers and logs as the other two do, and every 503 says when to try again

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #671, the rows "Remove the untyped word list", "Move batch onto `typedFailureOf` with one answer helper", "Send `Retry-After` on the 503" and "`/api/convert/batch` writes no outcome line"), decided 2026-11-07 (QA request: close the open rows of the convert-route error contract).
- **Decision**:
  - **An error answers by its class.** `POST /api/convert` no longer reads the message of a plain `Error` for the words `Unsupported`, `Cannot convert`, `Failed to parse`, `PDF OCR`, `compression`, `Fail-Closed` or `payload is empty` to turn it into a 400. Every throw site that used those words now throws a typed class: `UnsupportedTargetError` (400, `unsupported_pair`) for a source or target no engine of the family writes, and `ConversionFailedError` (400, `conversion_failed`) for an empty payload, an office source with no text reader, a channel layout the in-process Ogg encoders do not write, a spreadsheet function the evaluator does not know and a PDF that the OCR rasteriser cannot decode. The status of each is the 400 it answered before. An error that still arrives as a plain `Error` is a fault of the server (500, a fixed sentence, the error in the outcome line), as it already was on `/api/v1/convert`.
  - **The batch route answers a conversion error as `/api/v1/convert` does**, through one helper (`typedFailureProblem`, `src/lib/api/typed-failure-response.ts`) that reads `typedFailureOf`: the status and code the class declares, 503 for a missing tool, and a fixed sentence for a 5xx or an untyped error. It used to answer every typed failure 400 whatever its class declared and an untyped error with its own message.
  - **The batch route writes the one outcome line** of a refusal or failure (`[convert/batch] refusal|failure`), with the redaction of the other routes. The names of all the files of the batch and the passwords of its options are cut out of the message.
  - **A 503 of the convert routes carries `Retry-After: 5`**: the answer for a missing tool and the answer while the quota store is offline, which had none. The storage-full, queue-unavailable and client-address 503 answers already had one. Neither case has a known recovery time (another worker may have the tool at once), so the value is the short fixed wait the queue and storage 503 answers use.
  - `TraceOutOfTimeError`, a subclass that only renamed `CpuTaskTimeoutError`, is gone; the tracer throws the base class with its message.
- **Why**:
  - **Words are not a contract.** A message changed by a library or by a reworded sentence moved a conversion between a 400 and a 500 without a test failing; a class cannot drift that way. The refusal-code inventory test already lists every class and its code.
  - **A client that retries needs the wait.** A 503 without `Retry-After` leaves a client to guess; the queue and the upload routes already answer with it.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A plain `Error` that a library throws for a bad input now answers 500 where its words used to make it a 400. No first-party throw site is left that does this; a library error that reaches the route is found in the outcome line and given a class then.
  - The batch route answers 500 with a fixed sentence where it used to quote the message of an untyped error.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Keeping the list for library errors**: it is the matching by words this entry removes.
  - **A `Retry-After` computed from the queue backoff**: the 503 here does not come from a queue attempt, so the number would be invented.
- **Verified by**: `tests/convert-error-contract.test.ts` (a plain `Error` with each of the words answers 500; the empty-payload and unsupported-pair sites are typed; the 503 of both convert routes and the batch route carries `Retry-After`; the batch route answers a fault class 500, a typed refusal with its code, logs one failure or refusal line free of the file name, and logs a refusal no error decided), `tests/raster-vectorize.test.ts` (the tracer's time-out is the base class), `tests/convert-error-boundaries.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a library error that reaches the route as a plain `Error` is a bad input in practice; give its throw site a class at that point.

## 178. The core pages are audited against WCAG 2.1 AA in the test suite with axe-core, with no baseline of tolerated violations

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #903, phase 1: the automated check)
- **Decision**:
  - **The tool is axe-core** (MPL-2.0), a development dependency used only by the test suite and in no image or build output (`docs/licensing.md` section 6.4). It runs the rules tagged WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 level A and AA, and the best-practice rules for heading order, landmarks and regions.
  - **The harness is the existing vitest and jsdom one**, not a browser. `tests/a11y-axe.test.ts` mounts each page as the browser does and audits the document: the home page in English and Korean, the converter pair page `/pdf-to-docx`, the format page `/pdf-converter`, the 404 page, the terms page, and the conversion queue with no target chosen, converting, done and failed. It runs in the `tests` shards of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so no job was added.
  - **There is no baseline.** Any violation of the rules above fails the test; a finding is fixed in the pull request that brings it. A finding that cannot be fixed without changing colours, sizes, spacing or layout is not hidden in an ignore list: it is named as an audit row of #903 and decided with the screenshots the design review asks for.
  - **Not covered by this check, and open in #903:** colour contrast in light and dark (WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11) and target size (the 2.5.5 of WCAG 2.1 level AAA and the 2.5.8 of WCAG 2.2 AA), because jsdom loads no stylesheet and lays nothing out; keyboard focus order and visible focus (2.4.3, 2.4.7); zoom to 200 % and reflow (1.4.4, 1.4.10); the VoiceOver pass.
  - **Translation completeness** is held by `tests/i18n-messages.test.ts` (same keys, same arguments and no empty message in every offered language, and the Korean register); this entry adds no second test for it.
- **Why**:
  - **The page views already render in jsdom**, and the repo tests them there; a browser run would add a browser install and minutes to a job for the same structural rules, and the structural rules (names, roles, labels, `lang`, landmarks, heading order, ARIA validity, live regions) are what axe decides from the DOM alone.
  - **A baseline lets the count grow unseen.** The pages pass today, so the honest gate is zero.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - The rules that need pixels are not enforced until a browser-driven pass is added (a later phase of #903); until then contrast and target size are checked by hand.
  - The audited states are the ones the test mounts; a state it does not mount (an options dialog, a format picker open) is not audited.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Playwright against a built server in CI**: it would cover contrast and target size, but needs a browser download and a running build, and its cost belongs with the visual work that would act on the findings.
  - **A recorded baseline of current violations**: there are none to record, so it would only be a place to hide later ones.
- **Verified by**: `tests/a11y-axe.test.ts` (each page and queue state has no violation; a control page with an unnamed button and an image without alternative text is reported, so the audit is shown to see).
- **Revisit when**: a browser-driven accessibility pass is added for contrast, target size and focus; or axe-core's rule set changes what the tags mean.

## 179. The service is measured by process metrics that each process serves on a port of its own, with closed labels and the registry's family, and its objectives are written down as starting values

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #899, phase 1: the metrics and `docs/slo.md`; the alerts and the runbook entries are the next phase), decided 2026-11-08 (QA request: service metrics and written objectives, open-source only, no new long-running service, metrics internal only).
- **Decision**:
  - **The library is `@prometheus-io/client` 0.16.1.** It is the package `prom-client` was renamed to in August 2026: the same repository (`prometheus/client_js`), now a project of the Prometheus organisation, with the same API (`Registry`, `Counter`, `Gauge`, `Histogram`, `collectDefaultMetrics`) and the same two dependencies. npm marks `prom-client` 15.1.3 deprecated in favour of it. Its licence is Apache-2.0 (not MIT), which `licenses.allow.json` allows; `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists it with its dependencies (`@opentelemetry/api`, `tdigest`, `bintrees`).
  - **Each process serves `GET /metrics` on a listener of its own, not through the web application.** The web process opens it from the Next.js `register` hook (`src/instrumentation.ts`) on port 9464, the worker on port 9465 (`src/worker/index.ts`), both through `src/lib/metrics/server.ts`. `METRICS_PORT` changes the port (`0` turns the listener off) and `METRICS_HOST` the address; the default address is the loopback one, and `docker-compose.prod.yml` sets `0.0.0.0` so that a scraper on the stack's networks can reach it. Neither port is published by the compose file, no route of the web application answers `/metrics`, the nginx site has no route to the ports and refuses `/metrics` and `/api/metrics` with 404 as well. A path other than `/metrics` is 404 on the listener, a method other than GET is 405, and a failure while rendering is a 500 with no body.
  - **The worker's metrics reach a scrape directly.** A scraper reads the listener of every worker container; nothing is pushed to Redis and the web process aggregates nothing. A listener that cannot take its port (a second process of the same host in development) warns and the process serves without metrics.
  - **The metrics.** Web, per convert route (`convert`, `convert/batch`, `v1/convert`) and family: `easyconvert_http_requests_total` and `easyconvert_http_request_duration_seconds` (a histogram with buckets at 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, 60, 120 and 180 s) with the labels `route`, `family`, `outcome`. Worker, per family: `easyconvert_jobs_total` and `easyconvert_job_duration_seconds` (buckets from 0.1 s to 3600 s) with `family`, `outcome`; `easyconvert_queue_jobs{queue,state}` (waiting, active, delayed) and `easyconvert_queue_oldest_waiting_age_seconds{queue}` for the five queues, read from the queue engine when scraped; `easyconvert_queue_sample_failures_total`, which counts the scrapes in which the queue could not be read (the readings are dropped then, so an old depth never passes for a current one). Both processes: `easyconvert_sandbox_spawn_failures_total{reason}` (`spawn_error`: the system refused to start the program; `sandbox_unavailable`: the host cannot confine it, so it was not started) and the default process metrics, among them `process_start_time_seconds`, from which a restart is derived (`changes()`), and the uptime (`time() - process_start_time_seconds`).
  - **Labels come from closed lists** (`src/lib/metrics/labels.ts`) and a value that is not on its list is recorded as the list's fallback (`other`, `unknown`, `failed`, `default`, `spawn_error`): the family is the category of the source format in the format registry (twelve categories and `unknown`), the outcome is `ok` (status below 400), `refused` (4xx, also a 499), `failed` (5xx) or `timed_out` (504, the status of `JobTimeoutError`; for a job, the status its failure answers on the synchronous API). A file name, a user, a job, a request id or an option never becomes a label.
  - **The metrics reuse the outcome log; there is no second logger.** `loggingOutcomes` (`src/lib/api/conversion-outcome-log.ts`) counts every answer of a convert route, the 401 and 429 that it does not log included; `attachJobLifecycleListeners` counts a job once, when it ends. The log lines are unchanged.
  - **The age of a Redis queue is read from its waiting set without reading a job.** The set is ordered by priority first (`score = rank * 10^12 + time`), so its head is the best-ranked job, not the one that waited longest; `oldestWaitingSince` reads the head of each priority band and takes the wait from the time part of its score.
  - **The objectives are in `docs/slo.md`** as starting values, with how each is computed from these metrics.
- **Why**:
  - **The default is the maintained form of the library the issue named.** Adopting a package that npm already calls deprecated at launch would make the first dependency update a migration; the successor is the same code under the same maintainers.
  - **A listener of its own keeps the metrics off the public path by construction.** A route in the web application sits behind the nginx `location /`, so keeping it private would depend on one more `location` block staying in place; on a port that nothing publishes there is no path to guard, and the nginx refusal and `tests/metrics-exposure.test.ts` only keep it so. The same listener serves the worker, which has no HTTP server, so both processes are scraped the same way.
  - **Pulling from each worker is the simplest design that works with the compose network.** Pushing to Redis would add a write for every job, would leave the figures of a dead worker in place until a time-to-live ran out, and would need an aggregating endpoint in the web process; the standard scrape gives the figures of each replica and an `up` of 0 for a dead one.
  - **Outcomes follow the status the service already answers.** The refusal and failure classes of the routes are the contract of entry 177; the metric adds no second classification that could drift from it.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - Nothing reads the metrics until a scraper is set up; that is the next phase. Until then an operator reads them on the host with `docker compose exec -T web node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:9464/metrics').then(r=>r.text()).then(console.log)"` (and 9465 in the worker container).
  - The counters are per process and start from 0 at a restart; `rate()` and `increase()` handle that, a single reading does not.
  - The queue gauges come from the workers only, every worker reports all five queues, so a query takes `max by (queue)`. With no worker running there are no queue gauges; a worker that cannot be scraped is the signal then (`up == 0`), which is what the alert of the next phase uses.
  - Only the three convert routes are timed. The upload routes, the job submission and the page routes are not, and an answer that an outer wrapper gives before the convert handler runs (a body declared too large, a full disk) is not counted. The families of a batch are those of its first file.
  - Any process that can reach the container networks of the host can read the listener. It holds counts and timings under closed labels and nothing of a request.
  - The default metrics add about thirty series per process.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **OpenTelemetry for JavaScript**: it has no closed-label support of its own, its Prometheus exporter is still a 0.x package, and the text format would need the SDK, the exporter, `core`, `resources` and `semantic-conventions` (about 1.1 MB unpacked, against 185 KB for the client) plus the choice of an exporter and a collector that nothing in this deployment runs. Its strength is traces and a push to a collector, which this deployment has none of. Revisit when traces are wanted.
  - **`prom-client` 15.1.3**: deprecated, see above.
  - **A route `/api/metrics` in the web application**: reachable through the public proxy unless a block keeps it out; rejected for the reason above.
  - **A push to Redis with an aggregating web endpoint**: see above.
  - **A Prometheus server or Grafana in the compose file**: a long-running service the host does not have, out of scope for QA's request.
- **Verified by**: `tests/metrics-labels.test.ts` (the families equal the registry categories, the status-to-outcome map, a hostile value falls back), `tests/metrics-requests.test.ts` (the real `/api/convert`, `/api/v1/convert` and `/api/convert/batch` handlers move the counters by outcome, and no file name, password or file byte is in the scrape), `tests/metrics-jobs.test.ts` (real jobs through the worker, node processor and listeners count as ok, refused, failed and timed out; the queue gauges, the unreadable queue), `tests/metrics-server.test.ts` (the listener), `tests/metrics-sandbox-failures.test.ts`, `tests/metrics-exposure.test.ts` (the nginx site, the compose file and the routes of the application), `tests/queue-oldest-waiting-redis.test.ts` (the age against Redis, with a better-ranked newer job at the head).
- **Revisit when**: a scraper and the alerts are set up (the next phase), the host is no longer the only one (the queue gauges and the process figures then need a `max by` or a `sum by` per rule), traces are wanted, or the objectives of `docs/slo.md` have 28 days of production traffic to be set against.

## 180. The session read answers 200 for a visitor without a session, a format list names each format by its id, and a page that does not convert words its upload card for what it does

- **Status**: Implemented (site review, text and wiring only; no layout, size, colour or spacing changed).
- **Decision**:
  - **`GET /api/auth/me` answers 200 with `{ success: false, authenticated: false, user: null }` when there is no session**, and the signed-in answer gains `authenticated: true`. The callers (the header's plan read and the dashboard) already took an answer without a user as signed out, so none changed.
  - **A list of formats labels each format by its id** (`formatChipLabel`), with a name for the three ids that run two words together (`ultrahdr` is Ultra HDR, `webpvideo` Animated WebP, `svgfont` SVG Font). The file extension is no label: an Ultra HDR image has the extension of a JPEG and an ALTO document that of XML.
  - **The upload card and the file input of the merge, compress and OCR pages say combine, compress and read text**, not convert. The format tiles of those pages still show the one format twice; changing them would change the layout.
  - **The home API sample posts to the origin the API documentation shows** (`APP_ORIGIN`), read on the server.
- **Why**: A 401 for an expected state is logged by the browser as an error on every page. A list that shows two formats under one label cannot be told apart. A merge page that asks to "convert" misdescribes the action, and a sample on a host that is not ours fails when copied.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Keeping the 401 and hiding the log**: the browser logs a failed request whatever the script does.
  - **Labelling by name in the registry**: the full names are long and the picker and the format cards already use the id.
- **Verified by**: `tests/site-review-copy.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: the tiles of the operation pages may change layout; then they name the operation and not the format twice.

## 181. Password reset and email verification mail go out over SMTP with STARTTLS, answer opaquely, store only token hashes, and are off without SMTP

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-08 (QA request: add password reset for email and password accounts, over SMTP as the operator's other service does; QA addition: verify the address of an email sign-up on the same sender).
- **Decision**:
  - **Mail is configured by `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_PORT` (587) and `MAIL_FROM` (the account by default).** The user is the full account address and the password an application password. STARTTLS is required on 587 (a server that does not offer it fails the send, never falls back to plain text) and the certificate is checked; port 465 connects over TLS. Without the host, the account, the password and a public origin (`APP_ORIGIN`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` or `APP_URL`), password reset and email verification are **off**: the sign-in page shows no link, the routes answer 404 `mail_unavailable`, sign-up sends nothing, and nothing else changes.
  - **A send is bounded.** The connection (5 s), greeting (5 s), DNS (4 s) and socket (8 s) timeouts all sit inside one hard 10 s deadline; a send that outlives it is abandoned and its connection closed. At most 16 sends run at once; the next is dropped. The mail is plain text in the page's language (`en`, `ko` in the polite form), carries one link and no image, no tracking and no HTML part.
  - **A failure is logged as one allow-listed category and nothing else**: `auth_mail_failure category=<timeout|authentication|tls|dns|connection|configuration|busy|transport|store>`. The category is read from the error's code (and its causes' codes), never from its text, so the provider's reply, the host, the account, the password and the recipient cannot reach a log line.
  - **The link host is the configured origin.** A request's `Host`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `Origin` are never read for it. The token travels in the URL fragment (`/auth/reset-password#token=...`), which no server log and no `Referer` carries; the page reads it, removes it from the address bar and sends it in a POST body. The pages are `noindex` and send no referrer.
  - **Asking for a reset is opaque.** `POST /api/auth/password-reset/request` answers the same 202 `{"success":true}` after the same 1.5 s for a known address, an unknown one, a Google-only account and an unverified one. The work behind a known address (a token and a mail) is queued and not awaited, so the duration does not depend on the address. Only an account that signs in with a password, was not linked to Google, and has a verified address is mailed.
  - **Tokens are 256 random bits, stored as a hash, single use.** The hash is HMAC-SHA256 under `KEY_HASH_PEPPER` (the previous pepper also verifies during a rotation) with a purpose label, in Redis at `{user}:auth_token:<purpose>:<hash>` with a TTL, plus a pointer per account so only the newest token of a purpose is valid. A reset token lives 10 minutes, a verification token 24 hours. Using a token deletes it in the same Lua script that reads it, so two requests with one token cannot both succeed. Erasing an account deletes its tokens (`scripts/erase-account.ts`).
  - **A reset sets the password under the registration rules (8 to 1024 characters), ends every session of the account and clears the failed sign-in count.** The password is checked before the token is touched, so a typo does not cost the link. Sessions end through the session version the session check already compares: the reset raises it above the version of every issued token.
  - **Rate limits**, per window of 10 minutes and the same for known and unknown addresses: 3 mails per address (reset) or account (verification resend), 10 per client address, 30 uses of a link per client, one coarse counter for clients that cannot be attributed. A refusal is 429 `mail_rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.
  - **Email verification.** A sign-up with mail configured is mailed a 24-hour single-use link, sent in the background so the sign-up neither waits nor fails on it; the address is confirmed by a button on the page the link opens, so a scanner that opens links cannot confirm it. A Google account counts as verified (Google vouches for the address; new Google accounts record it). Until an email account is verified, **sign-in works and nothing else is withheld, but password reset mails are not sent to it**; the dashboard shows a notice with a resend link (`POST /api/auth/email-verification/resend`, signed in, opaque, limited as above). Accounts made before this entry have no flag and count as unverified: they keep working and confirm their address from the dashboard when mail is on.
  - **`nodemailer` (MIT-0) is the SMTP client**, and `MIT-0` joins the licence allow list (`licenses.allow.json`, `docs/licensing.md`).
- **Why**:
  - **A reset mail is a way into the account**, so what the answer tells an outsider matters as much as the link: the same status, body and time for every address leaves no enumeration through this route, and the rate limit counts unknown addresses too so it tells nothing either.
  - **A reset to an unverified address would let whoever registered an address first take its later owner's account over**; verifying first closes that, and withholding only the reset (not sign-in) leaves every existing account working.
  - **A hash under the pepper** means a copy of the store (a backup, a replica) holds no working link, as for API keys. The token is random and long, so a fast hash is enough.
  - **The fragment** keeps the token out of access logs, proxies and `Referer` headers; a query string would put it in all three.
  - **The session version did not work in Redis mode**: the first revocation of a new account set the version to 1, which the account's tokens already carry, so a reset would have left every session alive. The revocation now starts from the record's version (atomic Lua script); a test against Redis fails without it.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A person who requests a reset for an address does not learn whether a mail was sent, and a person with an unverified address gets no mail and no message saying why. The sign-in page's hint is the dashboard notice, shown only once signed in.
  - The per-address limit means a third party can use up the 3 mails of someone's address for 10 minutes. The limit protects the mailbox and the sender's reputation; the owner can try again after the window.
  - The mail is sent from the web process in the background, so a restart in the 10 s window loses a mail; asking again sends it. A rotation of `KEY_HASH_PEPPER` without `KEY_HASH_PEPPER_PREVIOUS` voids the links in flight.
  - The in-memory fallback of the store (no Redis, development) is per process.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **A token in the query string**: it reaches logs and `Referer` headers.
  - **Awaiting the send and padding to a minimum time**: a slow server makes a known address slower than the floor, and the difference is the leak; the answer here leaves at the floor whether or not the send has finished.
  - **A six-digit code instead of a link**: needs a failed-attempt count per code and a second screen; a 256-bit single-use link needs neither.
  - **Blocking sign-in until the address is verified**: breaks every existing account; the QA decision is to keep sign-in working.
  - **Revoking sessions one by one by their `jti`**: the store keeps no list of an account's sessions; the version raises all at once.
- **Verified by**: `tests/password-reset.test.ts` (the same status, body and virtual-clock time for known, unknown, Google-only and unverified addresses; off without SMTP; the link host from configuration whatever `Host` says; `en` and `ko` mail; single use, simultaneous use, 10-minute expiry, newest token only; the registration password rules; sessions ended; the rate limits; the messages in both languages), `tests/email-verification.test.ts` (sign-up mails a link in the background; sign-in unchanged for unverified and older accounts; no reset mail to an unverified address; Google counts as verified; resend is opaque and limited; 24-hour expiry), `tests/auth-mail.test.ts` (STARTTLS and certificate settings, timeouts inside the deadline, the deadline, every category, a log line with no provider text, host, account, password or recipient, the in-flight cap), `tests/auth-token-store-redis.test.ts` (against Redis: lifetimes, only a hash stored, one winner among 25 simultaneous uses, replacement, previous pepper, the first revocation of a new account), `tests/erase-account.test.ts` (tokens erased with the account).
- **Revisit when**: the reset mail needs HTML or a list of devices; the operator changes mailbox provider (a change of `SMTP_*` only); abuse of the per-address limit shows up in the logs.

## 182. E-book pairs added: RTF and the Palm, Kindle, Sony and Open eBook targets from EPUB, FB2, MOBI, AZW, AZW3, PRC, CBZ and CBR, with LIT, CHM, SNB and TCR left out

- **Status**: Implemented (QA request 2026-11-08: offer the e-book pairs that the reference's public formats list has and the registry lacked, wherever a writer exists), epic #671.
- **Decision**:
  - **41 pairs are added** to the registry, so the pair pages, the sitemap and `/api/formats` list them:
    - **EPUB** and **FB2** to AZW3, LRF, MOBI, OEB and PDB (10 pairs) and to RTF (2);
    - **MOBI**, **AZW** and **AZW3** to RTF (3);
    - **PRC** to AZW3, EPUB, LRF, MOBI, OEB, PDB, PDF, RTF and TXT (9);
    - **CBZ** to AZW3, EPUB, LRF, MOBI, OEB, PDB, RTF and TXT (8; CBZ to PDF existed);
    - **CBR** to AZW3, EPUB, LRF, MOBI, OEB, PDB, PDF, RTF and TXT (9).
  - **36 pairs are left out**: LIT, CHM, SNB and TCR to AZW3, EPUB, LRF, MOBI, OEB, PDB, PDF, RTF and TXT. The project has no reader of these four containers, in process or in the office suite, and this change writes none. Calibre reads all four; handing them over would extend the boundary of entry 118 (a source calibre reads itself is handed over as it is) and is a decision of its own. CHM needs more than the other three: its reader follows the links between its HTML pages, so it needs the containment probe that entry 118 asks of EPUB. The options are in "Revisit when". `tests/parity-audit.test.ts` and `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts` keep the 36 pairs withdrawn.
  - **Routing per source** (no new parser or writer):
    - **RTF** is written from the text of the book by the writer that HTMLZ, TXTZ, PML, RB and CBC already use (`writeEbookTargetFromText`): the text of the EPUB spine, of the FB2 bodies with their tables, of the MOBI records. Headings, lists and pictures are not kept, as for those sources.
    - **EPUB to the five calibre targets**: the uploaded package is never given to calibre. The worker reads it with the project's EPUB reader (`readEpubModel`, which confines every path to the package and refuses a manifest that leaves it) and writes the book again with the project's EPUB writer (`rewriteEpubFromModel`); calibre converts that EPUB. The model carries web, mail and bookmark links and the pictures the package holds, so a link, style sheet or picture that names a file of the host is not in the book calibre reads. This settles the EPUB item of entry 118's "Revisit when" without a probe of calibre itself: the file calibre reads cannot name a host path.
    - **FB2 to the five targets**: the worker's FB2 to EPUB conversion (the structure reader and the EPUB writer) is the book calibre reads, as for every source that is not an e-book of calibre's own families.
    - **PRC** is a Mobipocket book under its Palm name (the upload check already treats it as one): the in-process engine reads it with the MOBI reader for EPUB, PDF, TXT and RTF, and calibre reads it as it is, under a name with its extension, for the five targets.
    - **CBZ and CBR** are read as page images in natural name order (the readers of CBC moved to `src/lib/conversions/comic-book.ts`, with a CBR read by the archive reader that CBC uses). PDF binds the pages as before. EPUB is an **image book**: one picture per page in page order, the first page as the cover, no text of its own; it is also what calibre is given for the five targets. TXT and RTF read the lettering of the bound pages with OCR, as CBC does, and a comic whose pages have no recognisable lettering is the typed 400 error of the PDF converter, never an empty file.
  - Where calibre's own output for a comic to text could not be measured in this change (no calibre was available on the test hosts), the pair is kept on the rule that its output is real text or a typed error. Nothing is written when OCR finds nothing.
  - **The quality benchmark** (`bench/families/ebook.ts`) gets rows for the pairs with a source it can build: EPUB, FB2 and the MOBI as PRC, and a CBZ of three pictures of the corpus; those books to RTF and to the five calibre targets, PRC also to TXT, PDF and EPUB, the CBZ to PDF and EPUB, and RTF for the public samples. RTF is read back by the office suite, the calibre targets by the reference tool (as text, or as an EPUB for the pictures), the pictures of a comic by `pdfimages` and the EPUB reader of the benchmark. For the five calibre targets both sides are the same program, so the row measures what the product's route (its own EPUB of the source) loses against the program reading the source directly; they have no throughput row, because that ratio has no measurement on the runner yet. CBR has no row: the benchmark has no RAR writer to build one and no CBR sample in its corpus (the real CBR files of the real-world corpus are read by `tests/ebook-added-pairs-real-samples.test.ts`).
- **Why**:
  - **The reference offers these pairs and every target already had a writer.** What was missing was a route from each source, and the sources with a reader already decode to a structure (EPUB, FB2, MOBI) or to page images (CBZ, CBR).
  - **calibre must not read an uploaded EPUB.** Its reader follows the paths of the manifest and the references of the content, and the worker has no mount namespace to stop a path that leaves the package. Writing the book again keeps the content and drops the references.
  - **A comic is pictures.** The reference's own comic input makes an image book; reading lettering into a text book (as CBC does for its e-book targets) is what a reader of a comic expects only for the text targets.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **An EPUB loses what the model does not carry** on its way to a calibre target (fonts, scripts, fixed layout, style sheets); the benchmark rows measure the loss in text and pictures, not in style.
  - **RTF is plain text**: headings, lists, tables and pictures are not kept.
  - **A comic as a calibre target is a book of pictures**, as large as its pages; the book limit of entry 118 (256 MiB) applies to the EPUB staged for calibre, so a comic above it is refused with 413.
  - **PRC that is not Mobipocket** (eReader, Plucker, zTXT books also use that extension) is refused with a typed error by the MOBI reader, and calibre reads whatever it recognises when it is handed the file.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Handing the uploaded EPUB to calibre**: faster and exact, and the exposure entry 118 names.
  - **RTF through the office suite from a DOCX of the book**: keeps structure, but it is native-only (a worker without LibreOffice would answer 503 for a book the in-process engine reads), and the other e-book sources write RTF from text.
  - **OCR text books for the comic targets EPUB, MOBI and the others**: a book of lettering that OCR guessed instead of the pages.
  - **Adding LIT, CHM, SNB and TCR as native sources of calibre now**: see the first bullet; it is a decision about the boundary of entry 118, left to the owner.
- **Verified by**: `tests/ebook-added-pairs.test.ts` (the registry lists the 41 pairs; RTF of EPUB, FB2, MOBI, AZW, AZW3 and PRC read back by LibreOffice with a word F1 against the text of the corpus book above 0.97; PRC to TXT equal to MOBI to TXT, to EPUB and to PDF; CBZ and CBR to PDF in natural page order by `pdfimages`, to an image book with one picture per page and the cover, to TXT and RTF by OCR in page order, and the typed error for blank pages; what calibre is given, against a stand-in program: a PRC as it is, the EPUB the project writes from an FB2 book and an image book from a CBZ, and for a crafted EPUB with `file://` links, style sheets and pictures a book with none of them, while a manifest that leaves the package is refused before calibre starts), `tests/ebook-added-pairs-real-samples.test.ts` (two real Kindle books and a public Kindle edition to RTF; real CBZ and CBR comics to PDF, to an image book with the pages counted by 7-Zip, and to the five targets read back by calibre), `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts` (the 41 pairs are reachable, the calibre targets answer the unavailable engine without the program), `tests/parity-audit.test.ts`, `bench/families/ebook.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: calibre is run over the new rows and any is below the reference (the rows were written without a calibre on the machines of this change; they have not run); a reader of LIT, SNB or TCR is wanted (options: hand the container to calibre as a source, as for MOBI, with a probe on the VM that a crafted container cannot read a host path, then write EPUB, PDF, TXT and RTF from calibre's EPUB; or write a reader of each container; TCR and SNB are small, LIT is calibre's own reader only); CHM is wanted (it needs a reader that confines its links to the archive, or calibre with that probe); a throughput ratio of the calibre targets is measured on the runner (add the throughput row then); a CBR sample or a RAR writer enters the benchmark corpus.

## 183. Document and PDF pairs the office suite, Poppler and the in-process writers already serve are offered: Word macro files, templates, AbiWord, Pages, text and markup to Word 97, RTF and page pictures, and PDF to Word 97 and the raster, PostScript, DXF and drawing formats

- **Status**: Implemented (a row of the conversion parity work, issue #783), decided 2026-11-08 (QA request: offer the document and PDF pairs the reference service offers and this product does not, by wiring writers and readers it already has, and leave out any pair that needs a new parser or writer).
- **Decision**:
  - **The pairs, by class and route.** The reference service's formats API (read on 2026-11-08, `include=options`) lists every one of them; the engines it names are in brackets.
    - **Word macro-enabled files and templates** `docm`, `dot`, `dotx` to `doc`, `rtf`, `jpg` and `png`, and `docm` to `docx` and `odt` (office): the office suite writes Word 97 and RTF in the one pass that opens the source, as it does for `docx`; the page images are its PDF drawn by Poppler, as for `docx`. Macros are removed before the suite opens the file (entry 8). `docm` to `docx` and `odt` keep the in-process route when the suite is missing.
    - **AbiWord** `abw` and `zabw` to `doc`, `rtf`, `jpg` and `png` (LibreOffice): the same suite routes. `abw` joins `zabw` in the table of formats only the office suite reads (entry 40, `office-suite-sources.ts`), so the pairs it already offered change route: the in-process text extractor returned the file's XML markup as the text (`lo-hello.abw` to `txt` was the 2,615 bytes of the file, now 12 bytes, `hello world`), and `docx`, `html` and `md` were written from that markup. Without the suite every `abw` pair is an unavailable engine (503), as for `zabw`.
    - **Apple Pages** `pages` to `doc`, `docx`, `epub`, `jpg`, `pdf`, `png` and `txt` (iwork): the suite's libetonyek importer opens a Pages document as a word processor, so it is a source of the same table; the suite writes `doc`, `docx`, `pdf` and `txt`, the page images come from its PDF, and `epub` is written from its DOCX by the in-process converter. Real Pages 4, 5 and 2013 files convert (`lo-pages_4.pages`, `lo-pages_5.pages`, `tika-testpages2013.pages`, with a table).
    - **Palm database and reStructuredText** `pdb` and `rst` to `rtf` (calibre, pandoc): the suite writes RTF from `pdb` itself; for `rst` the in-process converter writes the DOCX and the suite exports it as RTF.
    - **Text, Markdown and HTML** `txt`, `md` and `html` to `doc` and `rtf` (LibreOffice, office): the in-process converter writes the source as a DOCX and the suite exports it with its `MS Word 97` or `Rich Text Format` filter, the way a Hangul document is written as `.doc` (entry 158). An HTML page is not opened by the suite, so the pictures it names are fetched through the converter's guarded session (entry 40). To `jpg` and `png` (LibreOffice; a browser for `html`): the pictures are the pages of the PDF the same source converts to (written by whichever engine writes that PDF), drawn by Poppler, one picture for each page and a ZIP of them for a document of several pages; `multiPageOutput: first` gives page one, and a `pages` selection belongs to the pictures, not to the PDF. Without Poppler the answer is an unavailable engine; without the suite the PDF is the in-process one.
    - **PDF** to `doc` (pdftron): the in-process converter writes the DOCX of the PDF (with its password, `pages` and OCR options) and the suite exports it as Word 97, as the `.xls` of a PDF is written (entry 120). To `avif`, `bmp`, `gif`, `ico`, `psd` and `webp` (ImageMagick): `pdftoppm` draws each page and the in-process image encoder writes it, the route PostScript, XPS and DjVu pages already take; to `odd` (ImageMagick) the encoder's drawing package with the page as a full-page picture; to `eps` and `ps` (Ghostscript, Inkscape) `pdftops`; to `dxf` (pstoedit) `pdftocairo` and the DXF writer of entry 99, which leaves the pictures of a page out with a warning (entry 129) and refuses a page that is only a picture (entry 133). The default is every page, as for `pdf` to `png`: one file for a page and a ZIP of per-page files for several (the reference's `pages` has no default either), `multiPageOutput: first` for page one, and one run of consecutive pages for `ps`.
    - **XPS** `xps` to `odd` (ImageMagick): GhostXPS and the same encoder.
    - **Word and OpenDocument text to the e-book targets** `docx` and `odt` to `azw3`, `lrf`, `mobi`, `oeb` and `pdb` (calibre): the route of the e-book pairs of entry 182, which writes the document as an EPUB with the in-process converters and hands that to `ebook-convert`, as `rtf` and `html` already take it.
  - **The pairs left out, and why.**
    - `pages` to `ppt` and `xls` (iwork): the office suite has no export from a text document to a presentation or a spreadsheet (entry 40 for `numbers` to `doc` and `ppt`, entry 113 for `pages` to `xls`), and no writer of ours turns a Pages document into either.
    - `pdf` to `ppt` (pdftron): measured and not offered. On `latin.pdf` the word recall against the text it was set from is 0.9798, against 1.0 for the office suite's own PDF import saved as `.ppt` (worse by 0.0202 where 0.02 is allowed): the PDF to PPTX text path joins `well-known` at the end of a line into `wellknown`, where the PDF to DOCX path of `pdf` to `doc` keeps it (recall 1).
    - `pdf` to `emf` and `wmf` (Inkscape): the metafile writers refuse a picture, a mask, a pattern fill and a clip that is not one convex polygon (entries 42 and 99), as for PostScript and EPS pages, which stay withdrawn. Run over 60 real government PDFs of the corpus, 26 convert to EMF and to WMF and 34 are refused with a typed answer (19 for a picture, the rest for a mask, a bitmap-font glyph, a skewed pen, a pattern, a filter or a dash the format cannot carry). DXF over the same 60: 48 convert and 12 are refused (a page of only a picture, a mask, a pattern fill), so DXF is offered. A rasterising metafile writer would be a new writer.
    - `docx` to `xps` (office): the XPS writer lays out plain text only (entry 40), so a Word document would lose its layout, tables and pictures, and the in-process engine turns it down on purpose (`tests/office-suite-typed-failures.test.ts` pins the set of text-only targets against the registry); no writer of ours turns a Word document or a PDF into a faithful XPS. The XPS that `doc`, `docm`, `dot`, `dotx` and `rtf` already offer are text as well and are not changed here.
    - `htm` pairs are not part of this change (the registry offers `html`).
- **Why**:
  - **Each pair is the route of its sibling.** `docm`, `dot` and `dotx` read as the Word formats the suite writes `doc`, `rtf` and page images from; the markup sources have a DOCX and a PDF writer already and the suite is the only writer of Word 97 and RTF; PDF pages to the encoded rasters, PostScript and DXF are what XPS, PostScript and DjVu sources already take after their own render. Nothing here is a new parser or writer.
  - **The reference's defaults decide the shape.** Its `pages` option has no default, so every page is converted (`pdf` to `png` and these pairs write a ZIP of per-page files); the default of its `ico` is 32 by 32 and ours is the 256 pixel canvas of the shared image writer, as for XPS and DjVu pages.
  - **`abw` is a suite source because the alternative is wrong output.** A format the registry accepts is converted by a reader of that format or refused (entry 40); the plain XML of AbiWord is the same format as `zabw` and has the same importer.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - A Word 97 or RTF file from text, Markdown, HTML, RST or PDF costs the in-process DOCX and one suite run (0.6 to 3.3 s measured on a warm pool, Apple silicon); the formatting is that of the DOCX the converter writes, not of the suite's own import of the markup.
  - `html` to `jpg` and `png` are the pages of the PDF and not a screenshot of one long page, which the reference (a browser) writes without options. A page is the unit every other document source gives, and `multiPageOutput: first` returns the first one.
  - `abw` pairs that converted before now need the suite: a worker without LibreOffice answers 503 where it returned markup as text.
  - The icon of `pdf` to `ico` is 256 by 256 and not the reference's 32 by 32.
  - A Pages document is read by libetonyek (0.1.10 on the Lima VM): a document of a release newer than the importer may lose what it does not read.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Letting the suite open HTML for `doc` and `rtf`**: it opens a page without the image fetch guard of the staged HTML path (entry 40) and has no export from its web writer without naming the filter.
  - **Plain text import of Markdown and RST by the suite**: the headings and lists would be lost; the in-process DOCX keeps them.
  - **Writing `pdf` to `ppt` from the PPTX as it is**: it fails the parity row by one word; the cause is in the PPTX text path, a change outside this one.
  - **A raster writer behind `pdf` to `emf` and `wmf`**: a new writer.
- **Verified by**: `tests/document-pairs.test.ts` (real and authored files through the dispatcher, each read back by a program that is not the converter: LibreOffice printing the output and `pdftotext`, Tesseract on the page pictures, ImageMagick and the image library on the rasters, Ghostscript on PostScript and EPS, the office suite's own DXF import for DXF, the package parts of the drawing; the registry lists the pairs of this entry and none of those left out), `tests/office-suite-real-samples.test.ts` (rows for `abw`, `zabw`, `dot`, `pages` and `pdb`, and the check that every target of an office suite source is converted from a real file), `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts` (the missing-engine answer and the real conversion of every new native pair), `tests/parity-audit.test.ts`, and the document family of the quality benchmark (`ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1 npm run bench:quality -- --parity --quality-only --family document` on the Lima VM, Ubuntu 24.04, LibreOffice 24.2.7: 28 new rows, `lanterns.<source>-><target>` for text, Markdown, HTML, RST, AbiWord, `docm` and `dotx` as `doc`, `rtf` and `png`, `latin.pdf->doc`, and `multipage.pdf->webp|avif|gif|bmp|psd|ps`, all at or above the reference: word recall 1 against 1 for each). The new targets rotate the real-world plan again: the five Word documents without body text are no longer planned for PowerPoint, so their PPTX rows leave `bench/realworld/known-refusals.json` (the refusal itself stays pinned by `tests/docx-to-slides-text.test.ts`); their planned pairs run through the real-world judge on the Lima VM (calibre 7.6.0, LibreOffice 24.2.7) and all convert but one, `office-document-59378.docx` to LRF, which calibre refuses for the EPUB without a content page and is a new row; three of the files (`59378`, `issue_51265_3`, `emptydocumentwithheaderfooter`) are marked `emptyInput` after their parts were read for `w:t` elements with `unzip`.
- **Revisit when**: the PDF to PPTX text path keeps hyphenated compounds (`pdf` to `ppt`), a metafile writer can carry pictures (`pdf` to `emf` and `wmf`), the reference's default for `ico` is wanted, or the suite's Pages importer reads a format the real files of users need.

## 184. The site has a pricing page that states the free plan's limits and no price, the home page picks a pair from the registry, and the mobile menu is a full-screen sheet

- **Status**: Implemented (QA approved the visual changes on 2026-11-08; before and after screenshots go to QA before the merge).
- **Decision**:
  - **`/pricing` (and `/ko/pricing`) shows one plan, Free, at no cost.** Its limits are read from `src/lib/plan-limits.ts`: the daily conversions (`FREE_DAILY_CONVERSIONS`, and the anonymous allowance the server reads), the largest file (`PLAN_MAX_FILE_BYTES.free`), the simultaneous conversions (`DEFAULT_FREE_CONCURRENCY`), the processing time (`FREE_PROCESSING_MINUTES`) and the retention after a download (`DELIVERED_FILE_RETENTION_MINUTES`). The last two are new constants, and the defaults of `JOB_DEADLINE_MAX_MS_FREE` and `RESULT_DELIVERED_GRACE_SECONDS` in the configuration schema now read them, so the page and the server cannot drift. The page says that no paid plan is on sale and names no price; `PAID_PLANS_ON_SALE` stays false.
  - **"Pricing" joins the header and the footer (Resources column).** The header's mobile menu lists the same links.
  - **The mobile menu is a full-screen modal sheet.** Tools and API are collapsed groups, Log in and Sign up sit above the fold, focus stays inside the sheet, Escape closes it and focus goes back to the menu button.
  - **The home hero has a pair of format tiles.** Choosing a source and a target that the registry converts it to opens the page of that pair; the list of targets is the registry's, not a list of the page. A "High-Quality Conversions" card states only what is measured or counted: the nightly comparison with reference converters, the options that follow the format, and the number of formats and categories of the registry.
  - **The copy button of the home API sample sits in the sample's title bar,** so it no longer covers the first line on a narrow screen. The gap between the upload card and the catalog is narrower.
- **Why**: The launch is free only (QA decision of 2026-10-30); a visitor who looks for prices needs the limits and the plain statement that nothing is for sale. The reference sites it follows have a pricing page, a sheet for the mobile menu and a format picker on the home page.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **Writing the limits into the page copy**: the numbers would drift from the ones the server enforces.
  - **A pricing page with placeholder paid plans**: it would state prices that do not exist.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pricing-page.test.ts`, `tests/mobile-menu.test.ts`, `tests/home-format-picker.test.ts`, `tests/a11y-axe.test.ts` (the pricing page in both languages).
- **Revisit when**: a paid plan goes on sale (the page then lists it and `PAID_PLANS_ON_SALE` turns on), or the format tiles of the home page change layout.

## 185. Presentation, workbook and table pairs that the office suite, Poppler and the in-process writers already serve are offered: page pictures, PostScript pictures and Markdown of presentations, the presentation formats of templates, slide shows, macro presentations and Keynote files, and page pictures of Excel macro workbooks and CSV tables

- **Status**: Implemented (a row of the conversion parity work, issue #783), decided 2026-11-08 (QA request: offer the presentation, spreadsheet and data pairs the reference service offers and this product does not, by wiring writers and readers it already has, and leave out any pair that needs a new parser or writer).
- **Decision**:
  - **The pairs, by class and route.** The reference service's formats API (read on 2026-11-08, `include=options`) lists every one of them; the engines it names are in brackets. Its `pages` option has no default for a picture, so every page is converted: one file for a page and a ZIP of per-page files for several, as `pptx` to `png` already writes, and `multiPageOutput: first` gives page one.
    - **Page pictures** `pot`, `potx`, `ppsx`, `pptm` and `key` to `jpg` and `png` (office, iwork), and `xlsm` to `jpg` and `png` (office): the same route as `ppt`, `pptx` and `xlsx`. The office suite prints the PDF and Poppler draws the pages. `pot`, `ppsx`, `potx` and `pptm` are read as the plain format they are a layout of (entry 40), and a macro project is never run (entry 8). `csv` to `jpg` and `png` (LibreOffice): the pictures are the pages of the PDF the same table converts to (the in-process table writer's), drawn by Poppler, so that the pictures show what `csv` to `pdf` shows; a table of several pages arrives as a ZIP. The PDF carries no page selection, which belongs to the pictures; without Poppler the answer is an unavailable engine.
    - **PostScript pictures** `dps`, `odp`, `pps`, `ppsx`, `ppt`, `pptm` and `pptx` to `eps` (LibreOffice): the PDF chain of `xps` and `ps` pages to `eps` (`pdftops` on each page), one encapsulated picture for each slide and a ZIP for a deck of several.
    - **Markdown** `dps`, `odp`, `pps`, `ppsx`, `ppt`, `pptm` and `pptx` to `md` (LibreOffice): the office suite prints the deck to a PDF, as for every presentation page route, and the in-process PDF reader writes the Markdown of that PDF, which is how a PDF becomes Markdown anywhere in the product. A slide is a page, so the slides keep their order and a title is a heading when the reader sees it as one. The suite itself has no Markdown filter for a presentation (its filter belongs to the word processor), so there is no suite export to follow.
    - **Presentation formats** `key` to `ppt` (iwork), `pot` and `ppsx` to `ppt`, `potx` to `odp` and `ppt`, and `pptm` to `odp`, `ppt` and `pptx` (office): the suite writes the Office formats of the application that opened the source (entry 40); `pptm` to `pptx` is the package with its macro project removed and its main part retyped, as every OOXML variant is read by the reader of the plain format. `pptm` to `pdf`, `html` and `txt` (office, LibreOffice) take the routes of `pptx`.
  - **The pairs left out, and why.**
    - `swf` from every presentation (`dps`, `odp`, `pps`, `ppsx`, `ppt`, `pptm`, `pptx`; LibreOffice): the registry's `swf` is a video format that FFmpeg reads and writes, and the dispatcher turns a presentation away from the media transcoder on purpose (`isMediaTranscoderMisroute`, pinned in `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts`). The office suite has no Flash export either: `soffice --convert-to swf` on the three-slide deck of the benchmark answers "no export filter" on LibreOffice 24.2.7 (the Lima VM) and on 26.8 (the host). A Flash writer would be a new writer.
    - `emf` from `pot`, `potx`, `ppt`, `pptm` and `pptx` (office): the suite's own export draws the first slide only (2,612 bytes for the three-slide deck on 24.2.7), and the metafile encoders of the product refuse a page that carries a picture, a mask or a clip that is not one convex polygon (entries 42 and 99), as for every other page source; a page chain to EMF stays withdrawn there.
    - `xps` from `pot`, `potx`, `ppt`, `pptm`, `pptx`, `xls` and `xlsx` (office): the suite has no XPS export (`soffice --convert-to xps` answers "no export filter" on 24.2.7), and the only XPS writer of the product lays out plain text (entry 40), so a deck or a workbook would lose its layout, shapes, tables and pictures. Entry 40 withdrew the presentation-to-XPS pairs for that reason.
    - `key` to `doc` and `xls`, `numbers` to `doc` and `ppt` (iwork): the suite converts a document only into the formats of the application that opened it (entry 40, and entry 113 for spreadsheets): a Keynote presentation is a presentation and a Numbers workbook a workbook, and no writer of ours turns one into a text document, a spreadsheet or a deck.
  - **The benchmark scores the words that survive**, not the pixels: 30 new rows of the document family (`bench/families/document-slide-pairs.ts`) against the office suite's own export of the same source, and for Markdown against the text of the suite's PDF of it (the only reading the suite offers). Keynote files have no authored source and are converted from a real file by `tests/presentation-pairs.test.ts`; Kingsoft files have no public sample, so `dps` is a deck the suite saved as PowerPoint 97 under that name (entry 164), converted by `tests/office-suite-real-samples.test.ts` and the benchmark.
- **Why**:
  - **Each pair is the route of its sibling.** A template, a slide show and a macro presentation are the plain presentation under another content type; the suite already writes `pptx` page pictures and Office formats from it. PostScript pictures of pages are what `ps`, `xps` and PDF pages already take. Markdown of a PDF is an existing route. Nothing here is a new parser or writer.
  - **The reference's defaults decide the shape of the pictures** (every page, a ZIP for several), the same as for the pairs the product already offers.
  - **The Markdown of a deck is the PDF text because the alternative is a second text reader for six deck formats.** The product's in-process readers of `ppt`, `pptx` and `odp` write text, HTML and PDF only; a Markdown writer on top of each would be new code, and the PDF of the suite is what the page pictures and every other Impress route already use.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - **`eps` is one picture for every slide; the suite's own EPS is the first slide only** (38,753 bytes for the three-slide deck on 24.2.7), so a deck of several slides arrives as a ZIP where the reference's engine writes a single picture. `multiPageOutput: first` returns slide one. The benchmark row compares the first picture with the suite's.
  - **The Markdown reads a slide whose text is drawn twice (a shadow) twice, and may join the glyph runs of the two drawings.** On `govdocs1-000133.ppt` 34 of the 315 distinct words of the suite's PDF text are missing from the Markdown (recall 0.892); on `govdocs1-000160.ppt` (29 slides) none is. `pdftotext` merges the two drawings; the PDF reader of the product does not. A picture, a table's grid and a chart are not in the Markdown. The benchmark row cannot see a Markdown worse than the suite's PDF text, only that no word is lost on a plain deck.
  - **A CSV table's pictures are the pages of the product's table PDF, not of LibreOffice's Calc layout**: the page count and the cut between pages can differ from the reference's. The words survive (recall 1 against 0.9817 for the suite on a 90-row table).
  - **The EPS pages of one request may hold 256 MiB together**, a limit this entry sets for every PDF-to-EPS request (`src/worker/postscript-page-limit.ts`). Each page is its own file and the ZIP is built in memory, so a 34-page deck of full-page pictures (about 70 MB of EPS for each page, 2.4 GB in all) ran ten minutes and ended in a 2 GiB file-size crash. Past the limit the request is refused (413) with the way to narrow it (`pages`, or `multiPageOutput: first`). A request of ordinary decks, a few hundred kilobytes for each page, is nowhere near it.
  - A deck to Markdown or PostScript costs one suite run and one Poppler run (0.7 to 4.1 s on Apple silicon for the real decks of the tests, the largest being a 23-slide deck of 3.9 MB of EPS).
  - A macro presentation is read without its macros; `pptm` to `pptx` drops the macro project and says so by its content type.
- **Alternatives rejected**:
  - **The suite's EPS and EMF exports of the first slide**: they write one slide and are not the pages of the deck; the page chain gives every slide.
  - **Writing Markdown from the in-process slide readers** (`# Slide n` and the text runs, as the DOCX target does): a second writer for each of the formats, and the PDF route already carries the layout order the suite prints.
  - **A text-only XPS for decks and workbooks**: it would offer a pair the suite and the reference render fully.
  - **Offering `csv` pictures through an XLSX workbook and Calc's layout**: a second route for the same table, and pictures that differ from the `csv` to `pdf` the product shows.
- **Verified by**: `tests/presentation-pairs.test.ts` (real files of the real-world corpus and files the suite saved under the name of a format without a public sample, through the dispatcher, each read back by a program that is not the converter: Tesseract on the page pictures and on the pages Ghostscript draws from the PostScript pictures, LibreOffice printing the Office outputs and `pdftotext`, the compound-file streams of the PowerPoint 97-2003 outputs, the package parts of `pptx` and `odp`, and the words of the suite's PDF for the Markdown; the registry lists the pairs of this entry and none of those left out), `tests/office-suite-real-samples.test.ts` (`dps` to `eps` and `md`, and the check that every target of an office suite source is converted from a real file), `tests/native-office-targets.test.ts`, `tests/registry-engine-conformance.test.ts` and `tests/parity-audit.test.ts` (the missing-engine answer and the real conversion of every new native pair; the pairs this entry leaves out stay withdrawn), and the document family of the quality benchmark (`npm run bench:quality -- --parity --quality-only --family document` on the Lima VM, Ubuntu 24.04, LibreOffice 24.2.7; epubcheck is not installed there, so strict mode stops at the 12 `rich-structure.docx` rows, which were not evaluated and which this change does not touch): 30 new rows, all at or above the reference: `deck.ppsx|potx|pptm|pot->png` 0.8298 against 0.8298, `workbook.xlsm->png` 0.9704 against 0.9704, `table.csv->png` 1 against 0.9817, `deck.<pptx|ppt|odp|ppsx|pptm|pps|dps>->eps` 0.8462 against 0.8462, `deck.<same seven>->md` 1 against 1 (the suite's PDF text), and `deck.pot->ppt`, `potx->odp`, `potx->ppt`, `ppsx->ppt`, `pptm->odp|ppt|pptx|pdf|html|txt` 1 against 1.
- **Revisit when**: the presentation readers write Markdown themselves, a Flash or metafile writer can carry a deck's pages, the suite gains an XPS export, the shadow reading of the PDF text reader is fixed (the 34 missing words), or the reference's pictures of a CSV table are wanted at the page cuts of Calc.

## 186. Redis is backed up every 6 hours to the host's data volume for 7 days, an account is erased within 2 days, and the status of the service is the Uptime workflow's public run history

- **Status**: Implemented in the repository (issue #900, phase 1: `docs/operations/`, `deploy/oci/redis-backup.sh`, its two systemd units and the restore drill); decided 2026-11-08 (QA request: an operations runbook with Redis backup and restore, no paid service, no new billable resource). The units are not installed on the host yet; `docs/operations/backup-and-restore.md` has the install steps. The privacy wording is settled (QA 2026-11-08, see the last trade-off) and takes effect with version 2026-11-08; the timer is installed on or after 2026-12-08, 30 days after that version, because the terms (section 9) give 30 days' notice of a change unfavourable to users.
- **Decision**:
  - **A backup is a `BGSAVE` of the stack's Redis, copied out of the container.** `deploy/oci/redis-backup.sh` asks for a save through `docker compose exec`, waits until `rdb_saves` rose and no save runs, has `redis-check-rdb` verify `/data/dump.rdb` in the container, copies it with `cat`, compares the SHA-256 of the copy with the one computed in the container, and writes `redis-<UTC time>.rdb` with a `redis-<UTC time>.rdb.sha256` file (mode 0600, directory 0700, under `/var/lib/easysubway-data/easyconvert/redis-backups/`). The stack runs with `--save ""`, so only the script writes `dump.rdb`. The password never leaves the container: `redis-cli` reads `REDIS_PASSWORD` from the container's own environment through `REDISCLI_AUTH`. The server itself starts from `/tmp/redis.conf`, a file the start command writes (umask 077, mode 0600, on the container's tmpfs, owned by the redis uid) with a `requirepass` line, not from a `--requirepass` flag, so the password is not in `ps`, `docker top` or `docker inspect`; an empty `REDIS_PASSWORD` still stops the start before the file is written.
  - **Every 6 hours, kept 7 days, at most 28.** `easyconvert-redis-backup.timer` runs at 00:17, 06:17, 12:17 and 18:17 UTC (`Persistent=true`). `BACKUP_MAX_AGE_DAYS` (7) is applied first and on every run, also when the new backup fails; `BACKUP_KEEP` (28 = 4 a day for 7 days) only bounds the disk. The script stops when less than 1 GiB is free.
  - **An account is erased within 2 days of the request, then the append-only file is rewritten.** The privacy policy promises deletion within 10 days of the request (section 4; terms 9). A backup taken before the erasure still holds the account, for at most 7 days: 2 days + 7 days + up to 6 hours until the next run that prunes + its 2 minutes of random delay is about 9 days 6 hours, inside the promise. After `erase-account.js --apply` the operator runs `BGREWRITEAOF`, because the append-only file keeps the commands that created the account and the ones that deleted it until the next rewrite (at the 16 MB minimum and 100 percent growth that may be far away).
  - **A restore applies the erasures again.** After a restore from a backup, every account whose erasure finished after the backup's time is erased again before the service is trusted (restore step 8), including a request that was still open when the backup was taken: a request made before the backup and erased after it is in the backup, so the time of the erasure decides, not the time of the request. The record of that time is the notice mail to the requester, sent at once after `--apply` and the rewrite, from the mailbox that already holds the request; no list of erased accounts is kept on the host. A backup is never edited.
  - **The restore** puts `dump.rdb` into an empty `/data`, loads it in a throwaway server (no network, no password) with the append-only file off, switches the file on with `CONFIG SET appendonly yes` (which writes it from memory), stops that server, and starts the stack with `deploy.sh release` and `reconcile`. A Redis that starts with `appendonly yes` loads the append-only file and ignores `dump.rdb`, which is why the dump cannot simply be copied in.
  - **No object storage is backed up, because none exists.** Files are deleted minutes after delivery; the privacy policy says uploaded files and results are not backed up.
  - **No status page is built.** The public status of the service is the run history of the Uptime workflow (entry 173): a red run is an outage seen from outside. Users who write to the support mailbox get a personal answer; a SEV1 notice is drafted by the operator and approved by QA (`docs/operations/incidents.md`).
- **Why**:
  - **Redis is the only state that matters, and it is on one disk.** An append-only file covers a restart or a crash. A backup covers a damaged file, a bad Redis upgrade, a mistaken command or a removed volume.
