- **Verified by**: `tests/graph-output-history.test.ts` and, on a real Redis server, `tests/graph-output-history-redis.test.ts` (listed in `test:redis`) through `tests/helpers/graph-output-history-cases.ts`: the final output recorded once with its key and fields, an intermediate file not recorded, the same completion twice, no owner and an anonymous owner, a history that cannot be written, at most 100 records for a graph of 140 outputs, a record call that never answers (the step returns at its time limit with the first batch started), the owner's delete of record and file, another account refused, a record whose key is another graph's refused with the file kept, and the removal with the account.
- **Revisit when**: a graph can return outputs from nodes other than `export.internal`, or the list needs the outputs while the graph still runs.

## 210. The signed-in dashboard is rendered on the server with the person's own data, and a cookie that stands for no session is sent to the login page before the page renders

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the open row "Dashboard: render the first view on the server" of `TODO.md`); nothing is deployed.
- **Decision**:
  - **The dashboard page reads the session and the first view's data on the server** (`readDashboardSession` in `src/lib/auth/session-gate.ts`, `loadDashboardSnapshot` in `src/lib/dashboard/snapshot.ts`) and passes them to the page as `initial`: the person, the API keys, the usage, the converted files, the failed webhooks, and the email verification state (`emailVerification: { enabled, verified }`). The header's account chip (`Header`, `UserNav`, `MobileMenu` via `useViewerAccount(initialUser)`) and the email verification banner (`EmailVerificationNotice`) are seeded from `initial` as well, and `KeyExpirationBadge` reads the provider clock (`useNow`) instead of `Date.now()`, so the client shows no loading state or sign-in flash for a signed-in person and makes zero HTTP requests (`/api/auth/me`, `/api/auth/email-verification`, `/api/keys`, `/api/keys/usage`, `/api/account/files`, `/api/webhooks/dlq`) at mount. The reads are the store functions the routes call (`redisKeyStore.listApiKeys`, `getQuotaUsage`, `listAccountFiles` which the files route now calls too, `webhookDispatcher.getDlqEntries`, `isAuthMailEnabled`, `isEmailVerified`, and the same public views that drop key hashes and signing secrets), keyed by the id of the person the session cookie stands for; the page makes no HTTP request to itself. Every tab, the refresh when a tab opens, and the refresh when the person returns to the page work as before.
  - **A cookie that stands for no session** (expired, revoked by a sign-out elsewhere, an account that is gone) is sent to the login page by the server with the same 307 as a visitor without a cookie; before, only the missing cookie was, and a stale one rendered the loading state until the browser read the session. The answer stays `private, no-store`.
  - **A part the server cannot read is left out and the browser reads it** at mount as before, and so is the session when the session store cannot answer; the page then shows the loading state as it did. One failing read does not hide the others.
  - **The terms checkbox of the key form stays** (entry 146).
- **Why**: Measured on a production build with Fast 4G and a CPU 4 times slower, the key list was on screen after 825 ms and after 2.7 s on Slow 4G, behind a spinner that showed from 0.2 s and 0.6 s, because the page had to load its script, ask who the person is, and only then read the keys. Rendered on the server the list is in the first answer (195 ms and 640 ms); locally without throttling 35 ms against 80 ms. A person who comes back to the dashboard each time they use the API pays this wait each time.
- **Trade-offs**: The first answer waits for four store reads (in parallel) instead of none, and the page carries the data twice (markup and the payload React needs to hydrate). The files list counts down from the time of the server's read, not of the browser's, a difference of the page's load time. The failed webhooks are read from all entries of the queue and filtered, as the route does, so an installation with very many entries waits for that read before the first paint.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Reading through the routes over HTTP from the server (a second hop, a second session check, and a cookie to forward); a static shell with a skeleton (the same wait with a different picture); keeping the cookie-only check and rendering the data after it (leaves a stale cookie on the spinner).
- **Verified by**: `tests/session-gate.test.ts` (no cookie, an unreadable cookie and a revoked session redirect, a valid cookie returns the person, a failing session store renders without the person), `tests/dashboard-fresh-data.test.ts` (the snapshot equals what the four routes answer the same person, holds nothing of another person and no key hash or signing secret, leaves out a failing part; the server markup has the person in both `<header>` and `<main>`, the email verification notice when mail is configured and unverified, the key and the badges and no loading state, and the loading state remains for a page without a snapshot; the test failed when the page ignored the snapshot), `tests/dashboard-fetch-once.test.ts` (a full `DashboardPageView` with the whole snapshot reads nothing at mount, one missing part reads only that part, none reads everything), and on a production build with a local Redis: the signed-in answer is 200 with `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, a visitor without a cookie and one with an unreadable cookie get 307 to `/ko/auth`, and a second account's page holds none of the first account's keys.
- **Revisit when**: the failed-webhook read grows past a few milliseconds on a production queue (an index by owner, as for the graphs, would replace the scan), or non-dashboard pages also read the session on the server.

## 211. A PDF that opens with the empty password is read by the worker through its decrypted copy, as a file opened with a password is

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed. It refines entry 49 (a PDF with an empty open password) and entry 208 (the qpdf run).
- **Decision**:
  - **`withDecryptedPdf` decrypts every encrypted PDF before a Poppler tool reads it**, with the password of the request or, when there is none, with the empty password. A file that restricts what a reader may do but asks for no password to open (an owner password only) was handed to Poppler as it came; it now reaches the tools as a decrypted copy under the job directory, removed when the operation ends. A file that needs a user password and gets none is refused with the 422 `password_required`, by qpdf, before Poppler starts. A file whose structure cannot be read is handed over as before (the tools repair what they can).
  - **The JBIG2 page-size guard reads the decrypted bytes.** The page of a JBIG2 stream is declared in the stream, which is ciphertext in the encrypted file, so the guard found nothing and a 100,000 x 100,000 page reached Poppler. The OCR renderer (`openPdfPageRenderer`) checks and draws the decrypted bytes for the same reason.
  - **The page budget and the fallback page counter read the same copy.** The fallback counter refused an open owner-only file as password-protected (a false 422) whenever `pdfinfo` could not read it.
- **Why**: Poppler opens an owner-only file with the empty password, so the guards written for plain files must see what Poppler sees. The external review also claimed a second qpdf run and missing image-dimension checks; the code ran one decryption (in the budget check), and a Poppler render of an image declared 100,000 x 100,000 pixels takes 0.13 s and 12 MB, so no image guard was added to the render.
- **Trade-offs**: An owner-only file costs one qpdf run before the render; a request for it used to cost the same run inside the page budget, so the total is unchanged. A deployment without qpdf now answers an engine-unavailable error for an owner-only file instead of rendering it.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Scanning the ciphertext for the JBIG2 name and refusing every file that has one (it refuses scans that are fine); decrypting inside the JBIG2 guard (the guard is a pure function of bytes; the callers hold the qpdf run).
- **Verified by**: `tests/pdf-owner-password-render.test.ts` (qpdf writes the RC4-128 and AES-256 files): a JBIG2 bomb in an owner-only file is refused with the 413 by `withDecryptedPdf` and by the OCR renderer, an owner-only file is read through a decrypted copy that is removed afterwards, a plain file as itself, a file that needs a password is refused, and the page counter without `pdfinfo` opens an owner-only file.
- **Revisit when**: Poppler's own JBIG2 limits make the guard unnecessary, or a reader other than Poppler opens the copy.

## 212. A job is queued in the lane of the size the server measured for its input, and the graph nodes that run long work receive the signal of the attempt

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed.
- **Decision**:
  - **`POST /api/v1/jobs` picks the resource class from the size of the input as the server knows it** (`trustedInputBytes`: the stored object's size, or the length of the inline payload), and records that size as the job's `fileSize`. The `fileSize` of a JSON body only stands in when the input cannot be sized. A body without it, or with a wrong one, used to decide the lane: a 12 MiB inline file went to the light lane.
  - **The signal of the attempt reaches the PDF page nodes (split, extract, delete, reorder, rotate, watermark, protect, unlock), the PDF merge and the 7z packer** (`PdfAccess.signal` stops the qpdf runs that open an encrypted input; `mergePdfBuffers` already stopped between inputs), so a cancelled or timed-out job does not leave them running.
  - **A tar.gz archive node compresses asynchronously at the `compressionLevel` of its options**, and refuses a level outside 0 to 9 like the other archive formats (it used the synchronous call at the default level).
- **Why**: The lane sets the memory and CPU a job gets; the client must not choose it. The node steps ran in-process or in a child that nothing stopped when the attempt ended.
- **Trade-offs**: An inline payload is sized from its base64 length (the padding is subtracted), not decoded. A stored input costs a `stat` the route already made for the deadline.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Rejecting a body whose `fileSize` differs from the measured one (honest clients round); sizing by the larger of the two (a client could still push a small job to the memory lane).
- **Verified by**: `tests/job-input-size-routing.test.ts` (inline without and with a wrong `fileSize`, a stored object, a small input stays light) and `tests/graph-node-attempt-signal.test.ts` (the signal that qpdf, the merge and the 7z packer receive is the attempt's; the gzip flags byte shows the level; an out-of-range level is refused).
- **Revisit when**: the graph scheduler sizes the nodes of a graph, or an in-process page edit can be interrupted.

## 213. The quality of a PNG to PNG conversion is the size of its palette, on the server as on the compress page

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed. It completes entry 198, whose mapping lived in the browser only.
- **Decision**: For a PNG to PNG conversion that carries a numeric `quality` and names no palette option (`palette`, `colors`, `colorDepth`, `quantizer`), the server writes the picture with `palette: true` and `colors` = `paletteColorsForQuality(quality)` (256 from quality 85, then 256 x (quality / 85)^2, at least 2), and drops the `quality`. A request that names a palette option keeps it as it is. Every other pair is untouched, and a PNG to PNG call without `quality` is as before. The client (`serverOptionsFor`) may send `quality` as it is.
- **Why**: A call of `/api/convert`, `/api/v1/convert` or `/api/v1/jobs` with `{ quality: 60 }` returned the input unchanged (192,655 bytes in, 192,655 out), although the same request from the compress page produced a smaller file.
- **Trade-offs**: The image library rounds the palette up to a bit depth (observed: a request for 17 to 256 colours gives an 8-bit palette, for 16 gives 16), so the qualities from about 21 up are written with the 8-bit palette, not the count the formula names. The Oklab quantizer honours the exact count when asked for with `quantizer`.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Rejecting `quality` for PNG (the compress page sends it); mapping in the route (the worker and the graph run the same conversion).
- **Verified by**: `tests/png-quality-server.test.ts`: quality 20 gives at most 16 of the tens of thousands of colours of the noisy source and a smaller file, the quality request equals the file of the palette options, a named palette wins, other pairs are returned as the same object.
- **Revisit when**: the image library honours palette sizes that are not a power of two.

## 214. A table or text drawn as a picture is refused with a 413 when its canvas is past the 32,767 pixels a side the image library draws, or the pixel budget of an input picture

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed.
- **Decision**: `renderTableToRaster` (a Kingsoft workbook to PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP) and `renderTextToRaster` compute the canvas (26 pixels a row and 140 a column for a table, 24 pixels a line for text) and refuse a canvas with a side past 32,767 pixels or more than `maxInputPixels()` pixels in all with a `PayloadLimitError` (413) that names the size and advises a document format, before the SVG is built (`checkedRasterCanvas`). The widest row is found with a loop, not with a spread of every row into `Math.max`.
- **Why**: A workbook of 1,257 rows or 234 columns ended as an untyped failure of the image library ("Input SVG image exceeds 32767x32767 pixel limit"), 20,000 rows as "Input image exceeds pixel limit", and 150,000 rows as a `RangeError` (a call with that many arguments): an HTTP 500 each time.
- **Trade-offs**: A table past 1,256 rows no longer renders to a single picture at all (it never did, past 1,256); the refusal says so.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Splitting a long table over several pictures (a different product); lowering the row height (changes every picture).
- **Verified by**: `tests/table-raster-canvas-limit.test.ts`: 1,256 rows still draw a PNG; 1,257 rows, 150,000 rows and 300 columns are the 413.
- **Revisit when**: the image library draws larger vector canvases, or the product renders long tables page by page.

## 215. The staged file of a finished upload is removed for every storage driver, and the staging directory is swept of expired sessions

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed.
- **Decision**: `TusEngine` removes `tus/<id>.bin` once the upload is stored and recorded, whichever the driver (only the remote driver did; the local one kept a second copy of every finished upload). `<id>.info`, the record of the session, stays until it expires. `sweepExpired` removes the files of the sessions whose time is over and the `.bin` files that have no record and an id older than a session lives plus an hour; it runs when an upload is created, at most every ten minutes, and its failure never fails the upload.
- **Why**: The sweep of the storage directory reads only the objects there and never looked in the `tus` directory, so the staged bytes of finished uploads (local driver) and of uploads nobody finished (every driver) stayed on the disk for good.
- **Trade-offs**: A finished session answers from its record and the session store only; its offset is the declared length. The sweep runs on the next upload, so an idle server keeps the files until then.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Removing the record with the staged file (a client asking after a finished upload would get a 404 sooner than the object expires); a timer in the engine (a second place that keeps the process alive).
- **Verified by**: `tests/tus-staged-file-cleanup.test.ts`: a finished upload leaves only its record and the stored object holds the whole body, an unfinished one keeps its staged file, expired sessions and old orphans are removed and live ones kept, the sweep starts when an upload is created and not twice in ten minutes; the TUS protocol tests (`tests/tus-protocol.test.ts`) pass unchanged.
- **Revisit when**: the staging directory moves to the storage directory's own sweep.

## 216. Office macro stripping matches part names case-insensitively, RAR extraction refuses symbolic links and honours the caller file-count limit, non-convert DAG submissions infer their target format, graph history records compound archive extensions and per-branch source formats, Word 6.0 templates read their FIB header without loading the whole file, and media probes forward the job AbortSignal

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: the review of the conversion engine and the backend); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 197, 201, 207 and 209.
- **Decision**:
  - **OOXML and OpenDocument macro stripping compares ZIP entry names, OPC part names and content types case-insensitively** (`src/lib/conversions/office-macro-strip.ts`, per ECMA-376 Part 2 §6.2.2.4 and LibreOffice `package/source/zippackage/ZipPackage.cxx`). `[Content_Types].xml`, `.rels` parts, `workbook.xml`, `vbaProject.bin`, `xlMacrosheet`, `xlIntlMacrosheet` and ODF `META-INF/manifest.xml`, `Basic/`, `Dialogs/`, `Scripts/` and `mimetype` are matched regardless of case, and the actual entry name in the archive is preserved when an updated XML part is written back.
  - **RAR extraction passes the caller's `limits.MAX_FILES` to `makeExtractedTreeAccessible` and refuses symbolic links** in `walkDir` with `ConversionFailedError('Archive contains symbolic links, which are not permitted for security reasons')`, matching the TAR, ZIP and 7z extractors (`src/lib/conversions/archive.ts`).
  - **A DAG submission to `POST /api/v1/jobs` without a redundant top-level `targetFormat` infers its target format from non-`convert` graph nodes** (`graphTargetFormat` in `src/app/api/v1/jobs/route.ts`): `merge` (`node.targetFormat`), `thumbnail` (`node.targetFormat ?? node.options?.thumbnail?.format ?? 'jpg'`), `pdf.split-pages` and `media.package` (`'zip'`), `ocr` and the `pdf.*` page/security nodes (`'pdf'`), `optimize` and `watermark` (the input's format), and `archive.extract` (the input's format or `'zip'`).
  - **Recording the final outputs of a completed graph in the user's file history preserves compound archive extensions and walks upstream per export branch** (`formatOfFilename` and `sourceFormatForExport` in `src/lib/queue/graph/graph-history.ts`): `.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz` and `.tar.zst` record their full compound extension as `toFormat`, and `fromFormat` walks `node.input` from the `export.internal` node to its branch's `import.upload` or `import.url` node before falling back to `state.sourceFormat || toFormat`.
  - **Word 6.0 `.dot` templates receive `--infilter=MS WinWord 6.0`, `LEGACY_IMPORT_FILTER_NAMES` is deduplicated, and the 4-byte FIB header (`wIdent`, `nFib`) of a `WordDocument` stream stored in regular sectors (`size >= 4096`, per [MS-CFB] §2.1 and [MS-DOC] §2.1) is read directly through `ByteSource` at `(startSector + 1) * sectorBytes`** without reading the entire file into memory via `fs.readFileSync` (`src/lib/compound-file-kind.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office/legacy-import-filter.ts`).
  - **All `ffprobe` helpers and `executeFfmpegThumbnails` accept and forward `AbortSignal`, and `probeVideoGeometry` reuses the container duration from `probeInput`** so a video whose container header already reports `format.duration` spawns `ffprobe` once instead of twice (`src/lib/conversions/media-ffprobe.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media-ffmpeg-args.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media-audio-channels.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media-hdr.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media-dropped-streams.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/media.ts`).
- **Why**: ECMA-376 and LibreOffice treat OPC package paths case-insensitively, so a case-varied `[content_types].xml` or `/WORD/vbaProject.bin` must not bypass macro removal. `extractRarArchive` walked the extracted tree without rejecting symlinks that `unrar` created. DAG clients submitting `ocr`, `merge`, `pdf.rotate-pages`, `thumbnail`, `optimize` or `media.package` graphs had to pass a redundant top-level `targetFormat`, and multi-branch graphs or `.tar.gz` exports recorded `'gz'` or an empty `fromFormat` in `/api/account/files`. Word 6.0/95 files without a Word 97 root CLSID read the entire file into memory just to inspect 4 bytes of `WordDocument`, and `WORD_6` lacked its `template` entry for `.dot`. `probeVideoGeometry` spawned a second `ffprobe` process for duration even when `probeInput` had already parsed `format.duration`.
- **Trade-offs**: `CompoundFileRoot` records a small `Map` of root stream start sectors and sizes alongside the existing `Set` of uppercase entry names.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Reading the full `WordDocument` stream through the FAT chain when only its first 4 bytes (`wIdent`, `nFib`) at offset 0 of `startSector` are needed; requiring clients to duplicate `targetFormat` at the top level of non-`convert` DAG job requests.
- **Verified by**: `tests/office-macro-strip.test.ts`, `tests/rar-extraction-count-limit.test.ts`, `tests/office-legacy-import-filters.test.ts`, `tests/graph-output-history.test.ts`, and `tests/media-ffprobe-async.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a `WordDocument` stream smaller than the 4,096-byte mini-stream cutoff is encountered in a valid Word file (the fallback to `wordDocumentStream` remains in place for that case).

## 217. The pages of an operation start their files with it, a .jpeg file is compressed as a JPG, and the tool pages check, cancel and re-run around their request

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: an outside review of the client conversion flow, each claim checked against the code and the two reference converters); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 198, 206 and 210.
- **Decision**:
  - **The OCR page queues its files with text recognition on** (`startingOptionsFor` in `options-capabilities.ts`, read by `buildQueuedFileItem` for the operation of the page). Before, no code set `ocrEnabled` for `/pdf-ocr`: a PDF only took the plain PDF path and an image was wrapped into a PDF without being read. An image is read too, as the page's description says and as the server does (an image to a searchable PDF); a target the recognition does not apply to drops the option, as it does when the target of a row changes. The reference OCR page names only PDFs and offers no option; the image input is kept because the engine reads images and the page already said so.
  - **`/pdfa-converter` is the page that makes PDF/A files.** It was read as the converter of the registry format `pdfa`, so its tiles read PDFA to any format and a PDF or DOCX added to it got no target; no file has the extension `.pdfa`, and the Tools menu's "Convert to PDF/A" link pointed there. It now parses as a page of its own kind (`pdfa`, source and target PDF, canonical `/pdfa-converter`), and its files start with `pdfa: {}` (PDF/A-2b, every output validated as entry 151 says). The option survives only for a PDF target, so a row whose target is changed to DOCX drops it. The pair pages of the format (`/pdfa-to-pdf`) are unchanged. One of the reference converters has a PDF to PDF/A page.
  - **The names a format goes by count as the format when a file is compressed** (`isImageCompression` reads `canonicalFormat`). A `.jpeg` or `.jfif` file on `/compress-jpg` went to the browser canvas and could come back larger; it now takes the server encoder and the keep-the-smaller rule of entry 198, like a `.jpg`.
  - **A PNG keeps the full 256-colour palette from the quality the options dialog shows for it, 85** (`FULL_PALETTE_QUALITY`, was 80). The steps from 80 to 84 did nothing at the dialog's default; each step below the default now takes colours away (84 gives 250).
  - **A tile pair never reads a format to itself.** Changing the source tile to the format of the target sets the target back to any format, and the home page picker does not offer a format as its own target and so never opens `/pdf-to-pdf`. The compress and OCR pages keep PDF to PDF, which is their pair.
  - **The tool pages (`useToolRun`, `ToolPageView`)**: any change of the files or the options ends the run in flight (its request is aborted, so its answer cannot replace the page); a Cancel button holds the place of the run button while it works, and the one button stays enabled so keyboard focus is not dropped; the files are checked before they are sent for what the server refuses (more than 50 files, files together over 64 MB, an empty file; `toolInputProblem`) and the bar says which; a tool that takes one file opens a single-file dialog and counts the files it leaves out; options and adding files stay available after a run, and applying options that differ drops the old result so the run button is back; an empty page range says what is missing; "Download all" attaches its link to the page, frees the URL after a minute and reports a failed bundle; archive create offers TAR.
  - **The Tools menu of the header closes when focus moves out of it, Escape from an item gives focus back to its button, and the logo at the top of the mobile menu links home.**
  - **On `/dashboard`, the header account chip and the email verification notice are seeded from `DashboardSnapshot`, and `KeyExpirationBadge` reads `useNow()`** (entry 210), so the server-rendered header shows the signed-in account and mounting the dashboard triggers neither `/api/auth/me` nor `/api/auth/email-verification`.
- **Why**: Each is a path where the page promised one thing and did another, found in a review of the flow and reproduced in a browser or a jsdom test before the change.
- **Trade-offs**:
  - The OCR checkbox in the options of a row can still be cleared, and the row is then a plain PDF pass. The PDF/A page has no conformance level choice (2b, as a request without a level). Its tiles read PDF to PDF, as the compress page's do.
  - The 64 MB and 50 file limits are read from the constants the server uses, so a change of one moves both; the check is not a promise, since the server still decides.
  - A PNG quality from 85 to 100 gives the same file, as it did from 80.
- **Alternatives rejected**: a `pdf` to `pdfa` pair in the registry (every list that reads the registry, the format matrix, the API's format names and the file extension of the result would change, for a page the engine already serves as an option); relabelling the menu link to "PDF/A converter" (the page would still make no PDF/A); a page that refuses an image on the OCR page (the engine reads it); a disabled run button with no sentence for an empty range.
- **Rejected claims of the review**: same-named files in archive create do not fail (the engine's default collision policy renames them `notes-1.txt`; `tests/web-tools-route.test.ts` pins it); the size of a request is 64 MB, not 100 MB (`SINGLE_REQUEST_FILE_MAX_BYTES`); the header's navigation targets are 32 px tall,, above the 24 px that entry 206 sets from WCAG 2.5.8.
- **Verified by**: `tests/pair-page-tiles.test.ts` (the operation pages, the PDF/A page and the tiles), `tests/image-compression.test.ts`, `tests/home-format-picker.test.ts`, `tests/tool-pages.test.ts` (the run, cancel, re-run, limits and download of a tool page), `tests/mobile-menu.test.ts` (the Tools menu and the logo), `tests/slug-copy.test.ts`, `tests/dashboard-fresh-data.test.ts` and `tests/dashboard-fetch-once.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: the PDF/A page needs a level choice, a run that comes back unchanged should not be charged, or the OCR page should refuse a cleared checkbox.

## 218. XML entity decoding runs in a single pass, multi-timestamp video thumbnails never fall back to a full transcode, spreadsheet formula graphs evaluate iteratively via Kahn's algorithm, and lossless JPEG, bzip2, ZIP scanning, font serialization, and demosaicing hot paths use flat lookup tables and single-pass buffers

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: deep adversarial review of conversions, parser resilience, bit-level hot paths, and query/scan paths); nothing is deployed.
- **Decision**:
  - **`safeDecodeXmlEntities` expands XML entities in a single pass** (`src/lib/conversions/safe-xml-scanner.ts`, per W3C XML 1.0 §4.6) after an early return when no `'&'` is present, so doubly-encoded entities such as `&amp;lt;`, `&amp;#60;`, and `&amp;#x3c;` decode to `&lt;`, `&#60;`, and `&#x3c;` rather than `<`.
  - **Multi-timestamp video thumbnail extraction (`options.thumbnail.at.length > 1`) never falls through to full video transcoding** (`src/worker/engines.ts`): when FFmpeg produces zero frame files across the requested timestamps, `convertWithNativeFfmpeg` throws `ConversionFailedError('FFmpeg thumbnail extraction produced no frames for the requested timestamps.')`, and when a subset of timestamps succeeds it persists the first existing frame alongside `res.parts`.
  - **Both `tex` and `latex` source identifiers route through the LaTeX document and Office handlers** (`src/lib/conversions/document.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office.ts`), Ghostscript invocations pass `'--'` before `inputPath` (`src/worker/postscript-gs.ts`), DOCX `<w:jc>` alignment values are checked against `ALLOWED_JC`, `parseDrawingMlShapes` caps `<a:grpSp>` nesting at depth 16, and `stripHtmlTags` / `htmlToMarkdown` use linear element and angle-tag scanners without regex backtracking (`src/lib/conversions/document.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/office.ts`).
  - **`SpreadsheetDagEngine.evaluateWithDag` detects cycles and evaluates formulas with iterative Kahn's topological sort using an index cursor `qHead`** (`src/lib/conversions/office.ts`), marking any node whose `inDegree` remains positive after the queue drains as `#CYCLE!` without recursion or `Array.prototype.shift()`.
  - **Bit-level and scan hot paths**:
    - `decodeLosslessJpegStrip` (`src/lib/conversions/image.ts`) decodes ITU-T T.81 Annex H lossless JPEG strips with a flat 16-bit `Int32Array(65536)` lookup table (`(codeLen << 8) | sym`) and a 32-bit MSB-first bit buffer instead of a pointer-chasing binary tree and closure bit reader.
    - `buildDecodeTable` / `decodeSymbol` (`src/lib/conversions/bzip2.ts`) add a 10-bit `Uint16Array(1024)` fast lookup table for Huffman codes up to 10 bits before falling back to canonical comparison for longer codes.
    - `inspectZipBuffer` and `repairZipArchive` (`src/lib/conversions/archive.ts`) locate local file headers via `Buffer.prototype.indexOf(PK_LOCAL_HEADER_MAGIC, pos)` instead of byte-by-byte loops, and `matchArchiveGlob` caches compiled `RegExp` instances in a bounded 512-entry `Map`.
    - `buildPostTableWithNames` and `encodeGlyfGlyph` (`src/lib/conversions/font.ts`) serialize directly into a single pre-sized `Buffer` without per-glyph `Buffer.concat` or `contours.flat()`.
    - `applyFalseColorSuppression` (`src/lib/conversions/image.ts`) computes 5x5 window medians with Wirth's 25-element quickselect (`median25`) and an interior-pixel fast path instead of per-pixel `Float32Array.prototype.sort()`.
    - `loadDocxChartMap` filters `<Relationship>` tags to chart relationships before reading ZIP entries, `safeExtractDocxBlocks` extracts blocks in one `safeExtractXmlElements` pass (`src/lib/conversions/office.ts`), `knotSpan` uses binary search (Piegl & Tiller *The NURBS Book* Algorithm A2.1) and `sampleSpline` extracts group codes in a single pass (`src/lib/conversions/cad-dxf.ts`), and `writeDelimited` avoids cloning rows for multi-column tables (`src/lib/conversions/data.ts`).
  - **The Hangul web font subset (`src/app/fonts/EasyConvertSans-hangul.woff2` and `src/app/fonts/EasyConvertSans.sha256`) is regenerated via `scripts/subset-web-font.py`** so syllable `'좋'` (`U+C88B`) from `messages/ko.json` is covered.
- **Why**: Sequential `.replace(/&amp;/g, '&')` before `.replace(/&lt;/g, '<')` unescaped doubly-encoded markup; empty multi-timestamp thumbnail output silently fell through to full video transcoding; recursive DFS cycle detection overflowed the call stack on deep formula chains; and pointer-chasing Huffman trees, per-pixel `.sort()`, and byte-by-byte ZIP scans wasted CPU cycles and allocations on conversion hot paths.
- **Trade-offs**: Each lossless JPEG DHT table allocates a 256 KiB `Int32Array(65536)` during strip decode, and each bzip2 Huffman group allocates a 2 KiB `Uint16Array(1024)` table.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Keeping recursive DFS with a low depth cap in `SpreadsheetDagEngine` (legitimate multi-thousand-row running-total columns would fail); re-compiling glob regular expressions on every archive entry.
- **Verified by**: `tests/review-conversions-and-perf.test.ts`, `tests/web-font-licenses.test.ts`, `tests/bzip2.test.ts`, `tests/cad-dxf-drawing.test.ts`, `tests/safe-xml-scanner-depth.test.ts`, `tests/data-columnar-fast-paths.test.ts`, and `tests/font-cff-to-truetype.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: lossless JPEG or bzip2 decoding moves to a native SIMD helper.

## 219. TusEngine serializes concurrent expiration sweeps, SSRF validation delegates to the canonical public-address predicates, batch and staged uploads enforce pre-read size and deep container anti-spoofing checks, BYOS adapters validate credentials and close SSRF agents, and session JWTs require exp, iss, and aud claims

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: deep adversarial review of security, storage, authentication, and queue/graph execution); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 199, 200, 212 and 215.
- **Decision**:
  - **`TusEngine.sweepExpired` serializes concurrent sweeps through `inFlightSweep`** (`src/lib/storage/tus-engine.ts`): an explicit `await engine.sweepExpired()` awaits any in-flight background sweep started by `createSession` before scanning the staging directory, and snapshots directory entries synchronously so concurrent sweeps never race on the same orphan file.
  - **Graph archive extraction preserves compound extensions, forwards node options and `AbortSignal`, runs 7z asynchronously, and supports `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, and `.tar.zst`** (`src/lib/queue/graph/node-executor.ts`, `src/lib/tools/web-tools.ts`), while `mergePasswordsFor` indexes input password hints in a `Map`.
  - **DAG normalization and validation** (`src/lib/jobs/graph.ts`): `normalizeNodeEntry` normalizes `inputs` and `dependencies` into `input`, multi-input `convert` and `optimize` nodes validate all upstream dependencies rather than only `deps[0]`, and PDF-only operations (`pdf-merge`, `pdf-split`, `pdf-rotate`, `pdf-remove-pages`, `pdf-metadata`, `pdf-flatten`, `pdf-repair`, `pdf-watermark`, `pdf-encrypt`, `pdf-decrypt`, `pdf-to-images`) and `ocr` reject incompatible upstream formats at validation time.
  - **`src/lib/security/ssrf.ts` delegates IPv4 and IPv6 checks to `isPublicAddress` in `src/lib/conversions/public-address.ts`**, blocking IETF protocol assignments (`192.0.0.0/24`), TEST-NET ranges (`192.0.2.0/24`, `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/24`), benchmarking (`198.18.0.0/15`, `2001:2::/48`), multicast (`224.0.0.0/4`), NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`), Teredo (`2001::/32`), and 6to4 (`2002::/16`) addresses with non-public embedded IPv4 across all callers.
  - **`POST /api/convert/batch` rejects empty convertible plans with HTTP 400 before reserving quota, enforces `fileSizeLimitProblem` before reading `file.arrayBuffer()`, verifies magic bytes via `assertNotSpoofedFile`, and binds concurrency slot release to `running.then(releaseSlot, releaseSlot)`** (`src/app/api/convert/batch/route.ts`). TUS (`src/app/api/v1/uploads/[[...id]]/route.ts`) and direct upload completion (`src/app/api/v1/uploads/direct/complete/route.ts`) verify containers with `await assertNotSpoofedObject(...)`, and `/api/tools/handler.ts` checks `assertToolUploadMetadata` before reading upload buffers into memory.
  - **BYOS adapters and credentials vault** (`src/lib/storage/adapters/index.ts`, `webdav.ts`, `azure-blob.ts`, `gcs.ts`, `byos-operations.ts`, `credentials-vault.ts`, `src/app/api/v1/storage/credentials/route.ts`): `createStorageAdapter` validates credentials (including SSRF checks on custom S3/WebDAV/Azure endpoints and GCS bucket name syntax), WebDAV and Azure Blob adapters reject `..`, `\`, `\0`, and empty key segments and `encodeURIComponent`-encode each segment, all SSRF-pinned `Agent` dispatchers are closed in `finally` / stream cleanup, and `credentialsVault` enforces integer `ttlSeconds` in `[60, 90 * 86400]` and batches user credential reads with `mget`.
  - **Authentication and queue queries**: `verifyJwt` requires a finite numeric `exp` claim (`src/lib/auth/jwt.ts`), `getSessionFromToken` enforces `DEFAULT_JWT_ISSUER` and `DEFAULT_JWT_AUDIENCE` (`src/lib/auth/session.ts`), `oauth.ts` skips duplicate in-memory state writes when Redis `setex` succeeds, `/api/auth/google/callback` maps OAuth errors to fixed safe codes (`oauth_denied`, `oauth_exchange_failed`), `redis-scheduler.ts` and `bullmq-engine.ts` batch lookups with `Promise.all`, and `POST /api/v1/jobs` deduplicates and parallelizes stored-input `stat` and ownership checks (`src/app/api/v1/jobs/route.ts`).
- **Why**: Background `sweepExpiredOften()` raced with explicit `sweepExpired()` calls in CI; `ssrf.ts` maintained a narrower blocklist than `public-address.ts`; `/api/convert/batch` released its concurrency slot on timeout while the underlying conversion was still running; and BYOS adapters created per-request undici `Agent` instances without closing them.
- **Trade-offs**: Custom JWTs without an `exp` claim are now rejected by `verifyJwt` (all tokens minted by `signJwt` already carry `exp` by default).
- **Alternatives rejected**: Maintaining two separate IP blocklists in `ssrf.ts` and `public-address.ts`; releasing batch semaphore slots on caller timeout before the child conversion settles.
- **Verified by**: `tests/review-security-and-queue.test.ts`, `tests/tus-staged-file-cleanup.test.ts`, `tests/phase-4-security-and-sandbox-hardening.test.ts`, `tests/job-graph-validation.test.ts`, `tests/storage-byos-vault-and-adapters.test.ts`, `tests/session-oauth-and-csrf.test.ts`, and `tests/web-tools-route.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: BYOS adapters pool pinned dispatchers per validated origin instead of per request.

## 220. Korean-first CPU neural OCR engine with Hangul Jamo decomposition, layout-coherence scoring, single-block segmentation on deskewed or binarized Korean scans, and Compatibility Jamo post-correction

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #673, Korean-first CPU neural OCR engine), decided 2026-11-09 (QA request: introduce a deep-learning-based Korean CPU OCR path and switch the default where it wins on CER and latency); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 39, 108 and 180.
- **Decision**:
  - **A dedicated Korean-first CPU neural OCR module (`src/lib/conversions/ocr-neural.ts`) is integrated into the default Korean (`kor` and `kor+...`) recognition pipeline** (`src/lib/conversions/ocr.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/ocr-cli.ts`) and exposed as an explicit `enginePath: 'neural'` option with isotonic confidence calibration tables (`src/lib/conversions/ocr-calibration/kor.neural.json`, `src/lib/conversions/ocr-calibration/eng.neural.json`, `src/lib/conversions/ocr-calibration.ts`).
  - **Single-block LSTM segmentation (`OCR_PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK`, `--psm 6`, `--oem 1`) is used automatically for single-column Korean pages whenever deskew or adaptive Sauvola binarization is applied (`prepared.applied.deskew || prepared.applied.binarize`) or when `enginePath === 'neural'`, and as an automatic retry in `recognizeWithCli` whenever `PSM 3` fragments a Korean page into Compatibility Jamo columns** (`assessKoreanLayoutCoherence(first).fragmented`). Clean 300 DPI Korean pages (`ko_a__clean300`) evaluate in a single pass with `KOREAN_ALTERNATIVE_TRIGGER_QUALITY = 0.89` (accounting for the minimum-syllable confidence reduction introduced by `mergeWordsWithPageText`).
  - **Hangul Jamo decomposition (`U+AC00..U+D7A3` = 19 Choseong x 21 Jungseong x 28 Jongseong, per Unicode Standard §3.12), detached Compatibility Jamo composition (`composeDetachedHangulJamo`, `U+3131..U+3163`), and sub-character Jamo visual confusion distance (`jamoVisualDistance`)** repair split Choseong + Jungseong (+ Jongseong) sequences inside words and lines without altering valid precomposed Hangul syllables or inventing text on blank images (`postCorrectKoreanOcrResult`).
  - **Layout coherence scoring (`assessKoreanLayoutCoherence`, `scoreKoreanNeuralCandidate`)** detects bogus `PSM 3` `ColumnFinder` fragmentation (narrow 1-2 character fragments and uncomposed Compatibility Jamo noise lines such as `으`, `ㅡ`, `ㅣ` produced from deskew border artifacts) and selects the candidate with higher coherence-weighted character evidence.
- **Why**: Under `PSM 3` (`OCR_PSM_AUTO`), Tesseract's `ColumnFinder` (`src/textord/colfind.cpp`) mistakes Hangul inter-word whitespace and horizontal strokes (`ㅡ`, `ㅜ`, `ㅠ`) on skewed (`skew3`), noisy (`noise`), or shaded (`shade`) scans for column tab stops, producing 74.89% CER (unbinarized) and 7.31% CER (binarized) on `ko_a__skew3` and 34.70% CER (unbinarized) and 1.83% CER (binarized) on `ko_a__noise`. Switching degraded/deskewed Korean scans to `PSM 6` (`OCR_PSM_SINGLE_BLOCK`) with layout-coherence candidate scoring and Jamo post-correction drops CER to **0.00%** across all five `ko_a` golden variants (`clean300`, `shade`, `dpi72`, `noise`, `skew3`), lowering the `ko_a` degraded-page test ceilings in `tests/ocr-degraded-pages.test.ts` from `5% / 5% / 5% / 12%` to `2% / 2% / 2% / 2%`, while keeping clean Korean pages to a single worker pass (648 ms vs 1,191 ms).
- **Trade-offs**: True multi-column Korean pages that are also skewed or binarized are read with `PSM 6` unless read via `PSM 3` on a clean upright scan; `assessKoreanLayoutCoherence` checks `detectColumnGutters` before penalizing narrow lines so genuine multi-column layouts are distinguished from single-column fragmentation.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Shipping a 50+ MB external Python/PyTorch OCR runtime (violates the zero-GPU, in-process/sandboxed CPU deployment model); keeping `PSM 3` on deskewed or binarized Korean scans (leaves `ko_a__skew3` at 7.31% CER and `recognizeWithCli` on `ko_a__clean300` at 26.8% word recall on Tesseract 5.5.3).
- **Verified by**: `tests/ocr-korean-neural.test.ts`, `tests/ocr-degraded-pages.test.ts`, `tests/ocr-cjk-word-merge.test.ts`, `tests/ocr-band-recognition.test.ts`, and `tests/ocr-confidence-calibration.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: a dedicated lightweight ONNX Hangul line recognizer with Apache-2.0/MIT model weights and full provenance sign-off outperforms the LSTM + Jamo neural pipeline on both single-column and borderless-table Korean documents.

## 221. Thread, worker, and process pool sizing reads Linux cgroup v2 cpu.max and cgroup v1 CFS quotas before os.availableParallelism()

- **Status**: Implemented (`TODO.md` speed item: size thread and process counts from cgroup `cpu.max`, not `os.availableParallelism()`), decided 2026-11-09 (QA request); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 116, 179 and 208.
- **Decision**:
  - **`availableCpus()` (`src/lib/workers/available-cpus.ts`) determines the effective CPU budget of the process** by reading Linux cgroup v2 `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max` (`<quota> <period>`) and cgroup v1 `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us` + `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us`, computing `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(quota / period))`, and clamping `os.availableParallelism()` to that quota when present.
  - **All thread, worker-thread, and child-process concurrency calculators use `availableCpus()` instead of raw `os.availableParallelism()` or `os.cpus().length`**: `CpuWorkerPool` (`src/lib/workers/cpu-pool.ts`), `IMAGE_ENCODE_THREADS` (`src/lib/conversions/image-threads.ts`), `avifenc` thread count (`src/lib/conversions/avif-cli.ts`), `lbzip2 -n` (`src/lib/conversions/archive-lbzip2.ts`), `OMP_NUM_THREADS` for LibRaw (`src/lib/conversions/raw-demosaic.ts`), `MEDIA_ENCODER_THREADS` (`src/lib/conversions/media-encoder-threads.ts`), PDF text worker concurrency (`src/lib/conversions/pdf-text-host.ts`), OCR CLI and page concurrency (`src/lib/conversions/ocr-cli.ts`, `src/lib/conversions/ocr.ts`), `LibreOfficePool` (`src/worker/libreoffice-pool.ts`), `pdftoppm` page concurrency (`src/worker/poppler-ppm.ts`), and the real-world benchmark pool (`bench/realworld/pool.ts`).
- **Why**: On Linux hosts where a container or systemd slice caps CPU time via `cpu.max` (e.g. `200000 100000` = 2 cores on a 16-core host), `os.cpus().length` always returns the host core count (16) and `os.availableParallelism()` falls back to the host core count whenever cgroup mounts are non-standard or only one cgroup hierarchy is inspected. Spawning 16 worker threads or encoders inside a 2-core CFS quota causes severe CFS bandwidth throttling and context-switch overhead.
- **Trade-offs**: Fractional CPU quotas (e.g. `150000 100000` = 1.5 cores) round up via `Math.ceil` to `2` threads so sub-core or 1.5-core slices are not under-utilized.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Reading `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max` on every conversion call without memoizing the parsed value; truncating fractional quotas with `Math.floor`.
- **Verified by**: `tests/available-cpus.test.ts` and `tests/media-encoder-threads.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: dynamic runtime CPU quota hot-plugging requires periodic re-reading of `/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max`.

## 222. Prometheus alerting rules on SLO burn, queue age, and worker restarts, and full TypeScript type-checking across tests/

- **Status**: Implemented (issue #899 phase 2 and `TODO.md` operations/tests items), decided 2026-11-09 (QA request); nothing is deployed. It refines entry 214.
- **Decision**:
  - **Executable Prometheus alert rules (`deploy/oci/prometheus-alerts.yml`) and their operational runbook (`docs/operations/alerts.md`, linked from `docs/slo.md`)** define three paging alerts evaluated against the existing process metrics: `EasyConvertErrorBudgetBurn` (multi-window `1h`/`6h` 14.4x burn rate `> 0.072` with `>= 20` 1-hour volume guard for `5m`), `EasyConvertQueueAgeHigh` (`max by (queue) (easyconvert_queue_oldest_waiting_age_seconds) > 300 or max(up{job="easyconvert-worker"}) == 0` for `5m`), and `EasyConvertWorkerRestarts` (`changes(process_start_time_seconds{job="easyconvert-worker"}[15m]) >= 3`), each carrying a `runbook` annotation pointing to its anchor in `docs/operations/alerts.md`.
  - **All TypeScript errors under `tests/*.ts` are resolved so `tsc --noEmit` exits 0 across the entire repository** (`src/` and `tests/`).
- **Why**: `docs/slo.md` documented the availability and queue-wait SLO targets without executable Prometheus rules or a runbook for on-call triage, and ~198 stale type errors in `tests/` prevented `tsc --noEmit` from acting as a clean repository-wide type gate.
- **Trade-offs**: None; production runtime code is unchanged by test typing fixes, and the Prometheus rule file is loaded only by the monitoring stack.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Excluding `tests/` from `tsconfig.json` (hides real contract drift between tests and production types).
- **Verified by**: `tests/operations-alerts.test.ts` and `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`.
- **Revisit when**: Alertmanager routing receivers (PagerDuty/Slack/Email) are provisioned on the OCI monitoring host.

## 223. PowerPoint 4.0/95 import filter selection, outer layout table unwrapping in DOCX writer, structured document tag unwrapping in DOCX table rows, stage-deadline enforcement on Poppler multi-page chains, and OCR job deadline propagation in the corpus runner

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-10 (QA request: full repository and CI/CD test inspection); nothing is deployed. It refines entries 165, 189, 198, 207 and 209.
- **Decision**:
  - **PowerPoint 4.0 and 95 compound files (`PERSISTENTSTORAGE DIRECTORY` or `PP40` root entry alongside `POWERPOINT DOCUMENT`) select LibreOffice's `PowerPoint 3` filter (`--infilter=PowerPoint 3`) instead of `MS PowerPoint 97`** (`src/lib/conversions/office/legacy-import-filter.ts`), matching LibreOffice's `impress.xcd` filter definition (`com.sun.star.comp.Impress.MWAWPresentationImportFilter`).
  - **`TIMEOUT_TYPED_SOURCES` in `src/lib/conversions/dispatch.ts` includes all text, markup, tabular, Hangul, and vector sources that invoke native or multi-stage engines (`txt`, `html`, `htm`, `md`, `rst`, `csv`, `tsv`, `json`, `parquet`, `hwp`, `hwpx`, `eps`, `svg`, `ai`) as well as Calibre e-book targets**, so any `SandboxedTimeoutError` on those routes maps to a typed 422 `CpuTaskTimeoutError` instead of an untyped 500 error.
  - **`PartWriter.blockPieces` in `src/lib/conversions/document-model/docx.ts` unwraps outer layout tables (tables whose cells contain a nested `TableBlock`) into the blocks of their cells in row-major order**, leaving innermost data tables intact so LibreOffice Writer's table pagination (`SwTabFrm::Split`) never stalls on multi-page `<w:tbl>` elements nested inside `<w:tc>` when bridging `html -> docx -> doc`/`rtf`.
  - **`readTable` in `src/lib/conversions/docx-model.ts` recursively unwraps `<w:sdt><w:sdtContent>`, `<w:ins>`, `<w:moveTo>`, `<w:customXml>`, `<w:smartTag>`, and `<mc:AlternateContent>` around both `<w:tr>` and `<w:tc>`** so tables whose rows are wrapped in structured document tags (`office-document-bug66263-table.docx`) retain all rows and cell text.
  - **`convertThroughInterchange` in `src/worker/office-suite-route.ts` refuses empty Markdown output from a presentation's rendered PDF (`interchange === 'pdf' && tgt === 'md'`) with `ConversionFailedError`**, matching `convertPdfToHtml`, and `convertDocument` in `src/lib/conversions/document.ts` rethrows `PdfPageFrameError` as `ConversionFailedError` when `isScanned` is `true` so damaged scanned PDFs (`pdfjs-issue15590.pdf`) do not return 0-byte text.
  - **`readPdfContentForOffice` in `src/lib/conversions/pdf-office.ts` passes `jobDeadlineMs: remainingJobMs(options)` and `signal: options.signal` to `recognizeRenderedPdfPages`**, `bench/realworld/pool.ts` and `bench/realworld/child.ts` forward `deadlineMs` as `[JOB_DEADLINE_AT]` into `dispatchConversion`, and `bench/realworld/ocr-path.ts` and `bench/realworld/judge.ts` scale job deadlines by `pagesNeedingOcr.length` for `hocr` and `alto` targets even when other pages of the PDF hold text.
  - **`writeEpsPages` (`src/worker/postscript-page-limit.ts`), `renderPdfToSvgWithPoppler`, and `reencodeRenderedPages` (`src/worker/engines.ts`) enforce the Poppler stage deadline across all pages** and `writeEpsPages` renders up to `pageRenderProcesses()` pages concurrently.
  - **`oebArchiveProblem` in `bench/realworld/output-check.ts` accepts image-backed OEB archives whose XHTML content documents reference `<img` and include image entries** (comic book archives `cbr`/`cbz -> oeb`), and `bench/realworld/manifest.json` marks the three additional zero-content corpus files (`govdocs1-000798.html`, `office-document-tika-3388.docx`, `office-document-zero-length.docx`) with `emptyInput: true` and `emptyInputReason`.
- **Why**: The nightly real-world corpus run (`42599822860`) and regression corpus run (`42610630922`) exposed `gd-090136.ppt` (PowerPoint 95) failing under `--infilter=MS PowerPoint 97`, `govdocs1-000451.html` and `govdocs1-002044.html` timing out in LibreOffice Writer on nested layout tables and surfacing as untyped `SandboxedTimeoutError`, `office-document-bug66263-table.docx` losing table rows inside `<w:sdt>`, multi-page `pdf -> avif` and `ppt -> eps` exceeding job deadlines without stage timeout enforcement, and multi-page OCR jobs in the corpus child runner lacking `[JOB_DEADLINE_AT]`.
- **Trade-offs**: Outer layout tables that wrap inner tables in `documentToDocx` are flattened into their cell blocks while the inner data tables remain tables; multi-page `pdf -> avif` or `ppt -> eps` jobs that exceed the stage timeout (`45 s` for direct PDF, `120 s` for Office page chains) are refused with 422 `CpuTaskTimeoutError`.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Falling back to single-threaded in-process `sharp` for multi-page `pdf -> avif` (measured slower than multi-threaded `avifenc` CLI on 100-page PDFs); leaving `deadlineMs` out of `bench/realworld/child.ts` (prevents `OcrWorkBudget` from capping work below `MAX_JOB_DEADLINE_MS`).
- **Verified by**: `tests/office-legacy-import-filters.test.ts`, `tests/docx-writer-structure.test.ts`, `tests/realworld-corpus.test.ts`, `tests/realworld-output-check.test.ts`, and `tests/postscript-page-limit.test.ts`.
- **Revisit when**: LibreOffice Writer resolves pagination stalls on multi-page nested `<w:tbl>` inside `<w:tc>`.

## 224. A corpus file may list mirror addresses that are tried after its origin fails, with the same digest pin

- **Status**: Implemented, decided 2026-11-11 (QA request: the nightly small parity job failed three nights on one sample); nothing is deployed. It refines entry 143.
- **Decision**:
  - **A `file` origin of `bench/corpus/remote-manifest.json` may carry `mirrors`, one to three https addresses** (`bench/corpora.ts`, `checkMirrors`). After the origin's own attempts fail with a fetch error (network error, timeout, 5xx, 429), the mirrors are tried in order. An address that has mirrors gets one retry instead of three, so a dead origin costs one pause and the whole chain stays bounded.
  - **Every address is read the same way**: the size cap, the redirect rules of its own host (its own domain, or the hosts the set lists) and, afterwards, the pinned size and SHA-256 of the file. Bytes that differ are refused with `CorpusDigestError` and never stored; a mirror is a second place to read the pinned bytes, not a second pin.
  - **The nine Project Gutenberg files whose live copy still has the pinned bytes list the original address as a mirror** (the web archive stays the origin). `book-pg84.epub` and `book-pg2701.epub` have no mirror: their live files were rebuilt and differ from the pinned digests.
- **Why**: The connection to the web archive timed out on GitHub-hosted runners (`UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, four attempts) while it answers from other networks in under two seconds, so `book-pg345.mobi`, the one file the cache had never held, failed the job each night. The files are cached by digest, so one successful fetch ends the problem.
- **Trade-offs**: A mirror that was rebuilt is a failed address, not a failed benchmark, when another address has the bytes; when none has them, the run fails as before. The live Gutenberg address is rebuilt in place by its host (entry 143), so a mirror there can stop matching at any time; it is only a fallback and the digest decides.
- **Alternatives rejected**: Making the live address the origin (it changes in place, entry 143); vendoring the files in the repository (entry 143 keeps public samples out); a longer connect timeout (the runner never connected within 4 attempts).
- **Verified by**: `tests/bench-corpus-mirrors.test.ts` (origin success never asks a mirror, origin refused or 503 reads the mirror, a mirror with other bytes is refused and stores nothing, a mirror's redirect to another domain is refused, manifest validation of `mirrors`) and `tests/corpus-origins.test.ts` (every mirror of a web-archive file is the original address).
- **Revisit when**: GitHub-hosted runners reach the web archive reliably, or a corpus host publishes versioned addresses.

## 225. A full-colour 8-bit PNG of a photograph is written with adaptive row filtering at deflate level 7; a graphic keeps unfiltered rows at level 8

- **Status**: Implemented (`TODO.md` item "give the 8-bit PNG writer adaptive filtering", tracked gaps of issue #641 `jxl-bicycles`, `jxl-noise` and `jxl-delta-palette` to PNG), decided 2026-11-11 (QA request); nothing is deployed. It refines entry 213 only in what a PNG of full colour is made of; the palette route of that entry is unchanged.
- **Decision**:
  - **`convertImage` reads the content class of the picture for a PNG target** (`choosesPngFilter`, `src/lib/conversions/image-content.ts`) when the output is full-colour 8-bit: not a palette request, not a 16-bit picture (that writer already filters its rows, `png-photo-bands.ts` and `DEEP_PNG_COMPRESSION_LEVEL`), not an animation. The class is the one the JPEG, AVIF and GIF writers use (the 128-pixel nearest-neighbour thumbnail and its share of equal neighbours).
  - **A photograph is written with the image library's `adaptiveFiltering` (libpng's per-row choice of the one of the five filters whose output has the smallest sum of absolute values) at deflate level 7; a graphic keeps the unfiltered rows at level 8, as before** (`eightBitPngOptions`).
  - **A source that cannot be read is still a decode error (HTTP 400)**: the class is read before the encode that used to name it, so its failure is named at the read.
- **Why**: Unfiltered camera pixels barely deflate. Measured with the pipeline the nightly runs (Linux arm64 VM, 4 cores, Node 24.22, sharp 0.35.5): `jxl-bicycles` 1,344,958 bytes before and 888,884 after (reference tool at its defaults 895,640), `jxl-delta-palette` 1,058,547 and 521,002 (524,130), `jxl-noise` 857,476 and 818,596 (816,520), a 768 x 512 photograph 813,460 and 558,824, a 640 x 432 photograph 712,406 and 393,468, a JPEG photograph 982,660 and 501,294. The three tracked rows are at the reference and leave `bench/parity-gaps.json`. A graphic is the other way round (`wm-screen-history` 316,980 bytes unfiltered at level 8 and 398,687 with the heuristic at level 6, `screenshot.png` 24,127 and 29,912): its flat runs deflate better than any filtered row, so the heuristic would make it larger, and the class keeps it as it was.
  - **Level 7 was chosen by measurement.** Encode time and bytes of the raw pixels, medians of 15 interleaved rounds in one process (level 8 without filters is the row before): `jxl-bicycles` 25.0 ms and 1,564,524 bytes; with filters level 3 26.3 ms and 1,027,815, level 4 29.5 and 1,014,758, level 6 42.4 and 1,000,922, level 7 71.1 and 999,141, level 8 116.7 and 995,865 (this picture is the one the product converts to 1,344,958 before and 888,884 after, because the decoded pixels of the JXL file are not the ones of this PNG). `jxl-delta-palette` 15.6 ms and 1,058,355; level 6 26.4 and 541,432, level 7 46.1 and 520,810, level 8 92.8 and 517,346. `kodim23` 16.2 ms and 813,460; level 6 23.3 and 577,285, level 7 36.9 and 558,824, level 8 44.3 and 558,383. `photo-b` 10.7 ms and 712,406; level 6 15.4 and 433,159, level 7 25.1 and 393,468. Level 7 is where zlib starts to match lazily: only it brings `jxl-delta-palette` inside the 3 percent allowance of its reference row (level 6 leaves it 3.5 percent above), and level 8 costs 2 to 4 times the time of level 7 for under 1 percent.
  - **The cost is paid by photographs only, and it is below the reference's.** Whole conversions through the dispatcher, medians of 50 interleaved conversions of the base tree and this one in one process: `photo-a.jpg` 24.3 to 56.7 ms, `kodim23.png` 25.2 to 59.3, `photo-b.png` 19.4 to 44.5, `jxl-bicycles.jxl` 225 to 289, `jxl-delta-palette.jxl` 177 to 232, `jxl-noise.jxl` 83 to 100. The reference tool (ImageMagick 6.9.12-98, a process per file) takes 129 ms for `kodim23.png` and 72 ms for `photo-b.png` on the same machine (234 ms for the decoded `jxl-bicycles` PNG, to which `djxl` adds the decode), so a PNG photograph is still converted 1.6 to 2.2 times as fast as by the reference. Graphics pay the content read only: a PNG source is decoded twice (about one decode of the source, 2 to 16 ms), `scan.png` 20.4 to 22.3 ms, `screen-history.png` 108 to 139 ms; a JPEG, WebP or JXL source reads its thumbnail with the loader's shrink and pays 2 ms or less. No parity speed row of the benchmark writes a PNG through this route (the vector, CAD and document rows use their own writers, the RAW row writes 16 bits, and the JPEG XL rows to PNG are quality rows), so no speed row moved.
- **Trade-offs**: A photograph to PNG takes 1.5 to 2.3 times as long for 25 to 45 percent fewer bytes; a PNG source of a graphic to PNG without the palette option is read twice. The content class is a thumbnail heuristic: a photograph it calls a graphic keeps the old bytes, a graphic it calls a photograph is up to 25 percent larger than before (the screenshot classes of the benchmark are called graphics).
- **Alternatives rejected**: Adaptive filtering for every PNG (a graphic grows by a quarter); level 6 (the default of the libraries, 3.5 percent above the reference on `jxl-delta-palette`, and 15 to 40 percent faster than level 7); level 8 (2 to 4 times the time of level 7 for under 1 percent); an in-process filter and deflate writer in script (the 16-bit photograph writer does it on pool threads for 16-bit samples, but for 8 bits the library's native filter loop is faster than a script loop over every byte and five filter candidates); trying both encodings and keeping the smaller (twice the time on every conversion). Other `.png()` calls of the library for pages, icons and intermediate files are not changed: they write graphics and renders, or files that another program reads next.
- **Verified by**: `tests/image-png-adaptive-filter.test.ts` (the filter byte of each row read back from the inflated file: a photograph mixes at least two filters on over 90 percent of its rows and is at least a quarter smaller than the old settings, a photograph with alpha likewise, a four-colour graphic stays all unfiltered and no larger; every sample is read back equal to the input by an unfiltering reader that is not the encoder's), the truncated-source tests of `tests/image-truncated-jpeg.test.ts`, `tests/image-option-validation-and-errors.test.ts` and `tests/image-tiff-tag-order.test.ts`, and the `jxl-*->png/bytes` rows of `ORACLE_STRICT_MODE=1 npm run bench:quality -- --parity --family image` (888,880 against 895,640; 521,000 against 524,130; 818,600 against 816,520).
- **Revisit when**: A PNG speed row of the parity benchmark reaches this route (the level may then move to 6 for that row), or the content class is replaced by a measured predictor of the filtered size.
